title: Félix Tshisekedi and AU Facilitators Discuss Peace Initiatives in the Great Lakes Region

body_en:
The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, met on Thursday, January 29, with the African Union’s panel of facilitators to discuss peace initiatives in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.
According to the Presidency of the Republic, the Head of State commended the facilitators’ efforts and reaffirmed his commitment to a lasting and verifiable peace in eastern DRC.
He also reiterated his support for regional stability, in line with the commitments made by all parties.
For her part, Ms. Sahle-Work Zewde, former President of Ethiopia, stressed the urgency of action to end civilian suffering:
“We are on a tour. We will listen to everyone and see what can be done for the well-being of this population, which has suffered greatly for decades. We forget that behind all this, there is human suffering that must be stopped.”
The AU delegation included prominent figures such as Olusegun Obasanjo, former President of Nigeria, Ms. Sahle-Work Zewde, former President of Ethiopia, and Ms. Catherine Samba-Panza, former President of the Central African Republic.

title: Maxime Prévot Sounds the Alarm: “A Woman Is Raped Every 4 Minutes, a Child Every 30 Minutes in Eastern DRC”
excerpt: The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Describing the si
title_en: Maxime Prévot Sounds the Alarm: “A Woman Is Raped Every 4 Minutes, a Child Every 30 Minutes in Eastern DRC”
excerpt_en: The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Describing the si
body_en:
The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Describing the situation as a “forgotten conflict,” the Belgian minister highlighted the scale of sexual violence, stating that “a woman is raped every four minutes and a child every 30 minutes in eastern DRC.”
Faced with this emergency, Maxime Prévot called for stronger and more immediate EU action.
“On the ground, the situation is worse than ever, extremely worrying from a humanitarian perspective. This is one of the reasons why, along with other colleagues, we insisted that this issue be placed on the agenda. I am also surprised that this is only the second time in a year that the situation in eastern Congo has been examined. This cannot be a forgotten conflict: the European Union has a role to play,” he said.
He stressed the need to continue political mediation toward a genuine ceasefire and lasting peace, while calling for the withdrawal of M23 and Rwandan troops and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC.
However, he emphasized that the humanitarian emergency remains the top priority.
“A woman is raped every four minutes, a child every thirty minutes.” He therefore urged a rapid and effective European response, particularly through the reactivation of Goma airport to enable the large-scale delivery of humanitarian aid, insisting that “there is absolutely no question of military use of this airport.”

title: CENI Releases Electoral Calendar for Governor and Vice-Governor Elections in Sankuru
excerpt: The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29. The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcem
title_en: CENI Releases Electoral Calendar for Governor and Vice-Governor Elections in Sankuru
excerpt_en: The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29. The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcem
body_en:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29.
The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcement of provisional results.
Key Stages of the Electoral Process
The timeline runs from January 28 to March 24:
January 28 – February 3: Technical preparations, staff training, and establishment of the Candidate Reception and Processing Office (BRTC)
February 4 – 10: Submission of candidacies to the Provincial Executive Secretariat in Lusambo
February 19: Publication of the provisional list of candidates
March 2 – 6: Filing of appeals with the Sankuru Court of Appeal
March 9: Publication of the final list
March 20 – 22: Election campaign
March 24: Voting by provincial deputies
March 24: Proclamation of provisional results by the Plenary Assembly
This election is being held in a sensitive political context. The outgoing governor, Victor Kitenge, was removed from office on May 26 by the Provincial Assembly, which accused him of mismanagement, particularly regarding security, and of refusing to respond to parliamentary summons.

title: President Félix Tshisekedi Reaffirms Commitment to Inclusive and Peaceful Dialogue
excerpt: On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa. “In this context, national unity is more essential than ever.
title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Reaffirms Commitment to Inclusive and Peaceful Dialogue
excerpt_en: On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa. “In this context, national unity is more essential than ever.
body_en:
On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa.
“In this context, national unity is more essential than ever. That is why we reaffirm our openness to a peaceful and inclusive dialogue, resolutely aimed at consolidating national cohesion, without ever calling into question the institutions established through universal suffrage,” he declared.
The Head of State emphasized that any such dialogue would take place on national soil and be organized by the institutions of the Republic, in accordance with the Constitution, the laws of the Republic, and democratic principles.
He stressed that this process cannot serve to downplay aggression or dilute responsibilities.
“Justice will take its normal course, rigorously, to the very end, and without leniency, in order to honor the memory of those unjustly killed,” he said.
On this occasion, the President called on the international community to take concrete action to protect the country’s sovereignty and support peace efforts. He reiterated his refusal to negotiate with the perpetrators of crimes committed against the Congolese people.
He also pointed to recent remarks by a Rwandan diplomat before the U.S. Congress, officially acknowledging security cooperation between Rwanda and the AFC/M23 rebellion, saying this confirms the DRC’s position and must be taken seriously by the international community.
“This recognition is not a mere communication ploy, nor a political strategy. It sheds a harsh light on what numerous reports and multiple partners have long been pointing out: the existence of decisive support for an armed insurgent movement operating on the sovereign territory of the Democratic Republic of Congo,” he added.
He concluded by stating that no cause, narrative, or security justification can legitimize occupation, parallel administrations, forced displacement, or the plundering of resources to the detriment of a United Nations member state.

title: Washington Hosts Inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals, Spotlight on DRC
excerpt: Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gatheri
title_en: Washington Hosts Inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals, Spotlight on DRC
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gatheri
body_en:
Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gathering aims to strengthen and diversify global supply chains to reduce China's dominance in this strategically vital sector.
The meeting forms part of “Project Vault,” an initiative launched under the Trump administration to establish a strategic U.S. reserve of critical minerals including rare earth elements, cobalt, and lithium, backed by $12 billion in funding.
Global Participation Organizers expect delegations from over 50 countries, spanning Europe, Asia, and Africa. The DRC will be represented at the highest level, with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi officially attending.
A Central Player The Democratic Republic of Congo, with its vast reserves of cobalt and coltan, is considered a key actor in the global energy transition. Analysts say the Washington meeting could redefine the geopolitical balance around critical minerals, positioning Kinshasa as a strategic partner of the United States.
Recent bilateral engagements, particularly with Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba, underscore a new phase in the DRC-U.S. strategic partnership. Washington has signaled interest in a “minerals for security” agreement, potentially offering preferential access to Congolese copper, cobalt, and coltan in return for American investments in infrastructure.
The outcomes of this ministerial meeting are expected to have far-reaching implications for both the global supply of critical minerals and the economic and strategic positioning of the DRC on the international stage.

title: Citizens Launch Petition to Dissolve Equateur Provincial Assembly
excerpt: Mbandaka, February 5, 2026 – A collective of citizens, calling themselves the “Rebellious Citizens,” has launched a petition demanding the dissolution of the Equateur Provincial Assembly, intensifying political tensions in the provincial capital. Accusations of Interference and P
title_en: Citizens Launch Petition to Dissolve Equateur Provincial Assembly
excerpt_en: Mbandaka, February 5, 2026 – A collective of citizens, calling themselves the “Rebellious Citizens,” has launched a petition demanding the dissolution of the Equateur Provincial Assembly, intensifying political tensions in the provincial capital. Accusations of Interference and P
body_en:
Mbandaka, February 5, 2026 – A collective of citizens, calling themselves the “Rebellious Citizens,” has launched a petition demanding the dissolution of the Equateur Provincial Assembly, intensifying political tensions in the provincial capital.
Accusations of Interference and Patronage The group accuses members of the provincial assembly of paralyzing the executive branch through untimely interference and patronage practices. According to the petitioners, the deliberative body has overstepped its constitutional oversight role, interfering in the day-to-day management of the provincial government.
“The members of parliament are behaving like managers. They are blocking important files and interfering in the executive branch's responsibilities. We say enough is enough; this assembly must be dissolved to allow the province to breathe,” said Papy Ekate Ekofo, spokesperson for the “Rebellious Citizens” collective.
The collective has begun a large-scale signature campaign across Mbandaka, aiming for 25,000 signatures to appeal directly to President Félix Tshisekedi, the only authority empowered to order the dissolution of a provincial assembly in cases of persistent crisis.
Allegations of Bribery Rumors circulating in Mbandaka suggest that some assembly members are engaged in bribery, allegedly pressuring public institutions to hire relatives, disadvantaging local talent.
Assembly Responds The Equateur Provincial Assembly has rejected the petition. Rapporteur Ézéchiel Ambokani emphasized that the initiative lacks legal standing, stating:
“This petition has no legal standing to dissolve our institution. The mechanisms for dissolution are strictly defined by the Constitution and do not depend on collecting signatures in the street.”
Implications for Governance Observers warn that this standoff comes at a time when Équateur Province is struggling with infrastructure and social development. If unresolved, the conflict between citizens and elected officials could further weaken state authority in the region.

title_en: DRC, Zambia, and Angola Launch Strategic Coordination Meeting in Luanda
excerpt_en: Luanda, February 5, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Zambia, and Angola kicked off an inaugural coordination meeting in Luanda on Thursday, February 5, focusing on the implementation of the strategic Lobito Corridor project. The two-day session, held in partnership
body_en:
Luanda, February 5, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), Zambia, and Angola kicked off an inaugural coordination meeting in Luanda on Thursday, February 5, focusing on the implementation of the strategic Lobito Corridor project. The two-day session, held in partnership with the World Bank, gathers the Ministers of Transport, Finance, and Foreign Trade from the three countries to align policies, coordinate investments, and mobilize public and private partners.
A Regional Driver of Growth The Lobito Corridor is positioned as a key driver of economic growth, intra-African trade, and job creation, linking Southern and Central Africa to global markets. During the opening, Angolan President João Lourenço urged the participating states and financial partners to adopt a pragmatic approach to accelerate implementation.
DRC Prioritizes an Integrated Approach Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Transport Jean-Pierre Bemba emphasized that the DRC is pursuing a comprehensive strategy, combining transport, logistics, energy, trade, and industrial development. The initial priority focuses on the Dilolo-Kolwezi-Tenge section.

title: Washington Hardens Stance: Direct Sanctions Loom Over Kigali Amid DRC Strategic Realignment
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secur
title_en: Washington Hardens Stance: Direct Sanctions Loom Over Kigali Amid DRC Strategic Realignment
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secur
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secure geostrategic and economic support during his international tour.
Targeted Sanctions on Kigali The U.S. is reportedly considering direct sanctions against high-level Rwandan officials for their involvement in the M23 rebellion, despite previously signed agreements. These measures form part of a broader strategy to pressure Kigali and safeguard stability in eastern DRC.
DRC Secures Strategic Support The DRC is increasingly positioned as a strategic partner in critical minerals, with Washington reinforcing its willingness to support Kinshasa in both security and economic initiatives. A framework is being established to back high-impact development projects, translating political commitments into concrete actions for economic growth and supply chain security.
High-Level Engagements President Tshisekedi has held cordial discussions with prominent U.S. leaders, emphasizing strategic cooperation. These talks highlight the deepening bilateral ties and personal support for Tshisekedi, framing him as a key actor in regional stabilization and development.
Kigali Faces Growing Isolation Rwanda is reportedly confronting increasing international pressure, with historic allies shifting their positions. The country’s leadership has rejected accusations regarding interference in the DRC and defied calls for compliance, intensifying its diplomatic isolation. Analysts view this shift as a direct consequence of Rwanda’s admission of involvement in destabilizing eastern Congo, leaving Kigali with fewer international allies.
Implications for the Region The evolving dynamics signal a geostrategic realignment in Central Africa, strengthening the DRC’s role as a security and economic pivot while placing Rwanda under heightened scrutiny. Observers suggest these developments could reshape regional alliances and influence the future of critical mineral access and security cooperation.

title: Julien Paluku Accuses Rwanda of Targeting Congolese Minerals Behind the M23 Conflict
excerpt: Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterat
title_en: Julien Paluku Accuses Rwanda of Targeting Congolese Minerals Behind the M23 Conflict
excerpt_en: Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterat
body_en:
Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterated a strong position of the Congolese government: “The occupation of certain urban areas by the AFC/M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, has not only a military dimension, but above all an economic one.”
A Strategy of Destruction and Seizure
Julien Paluku denounced what he calls Rwanda’s strategy of destroying the human capital and economic fabric of the DRC. According to him, behind the military offensives lies a logic of systematically plundering Congolese natural resources.
“The volume of mineral exports to Rwanda has increased from $70 million to $2 billion in one year, even though Rwanda does not possess any mineral deposits. The real FDLR he is pursuing in the DRC is Congolese minerals,” he stated.
This declaration highlights one of the central issues of the conflict: the transformation of Congolese minerals into foreign wealth, fueling a parallel economy that weakens the Congolese state and deprives local populations of the benefits of their own resources.
At both the UN and the African Union, President Félix Tshisekedi and the government repeatedly emphasize that the war waged in eastern DRC by “Rwanda via the AFC/M23” has economic aims through the plundering of mineral resources.
On February 18, 2025, during a press conference, the Minister of Mines, Kizito Pakabomba, accused Rwanda of costing the DRC more than $1 billion annually. He also warned of Rwanda’s goal of reaching over $2 billion by 2026 through the illegal exploitation of Congolese mines.
One Year After the Fall of Goma
Paluku's remarks were made during the commemoration of the first anniversary of the M23's capture of Goma. The Suminwa government sought to mark this date by paying tribute to the resilience and unity of the Congolese people in the face of occupation.
The Minister of Communication and Media, Patrick Muyaya, emphasized the refusal to forget or trivialize the war in the East, recalling that remembrance is "an act of governmental responsibility."
The Themes of the Commemoration
The day of remembrance was structured around four themes:
The humanitarian crisis: thousands of displaced persons and victims of violence.
The economic stakes: the plundering of minerals and the weakening of the productive sector.

title: Kinshasa Launches Property and Rental Income Tax Awareness Campaign for 2026
excerpt: The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2
title_en: Kinshasa Launches Property and Rental Income Tax Awareness Campaign for 2026
excerpt_en: The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2
body_en:
The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2026.
At a press conference, the provincial Minister of Finance, Magloire Kabemba, announced the start of the campaign. During the event, the Kinshasa Revenue Authority (DGRK) presented the tax clearance certificate, an official document certifying payment of property taxes, rental income, and, where applicable, vehicle taxes. Printed on secure paper, this certificate is valid from the date of issue and forms part of a strategy to increase local revenue ahead of the deadline.
Decentralization of Tax Collection Sites
Alongside the minister, Gérard Kaja Kambowa, special advisor at the DGRK, stressed the importance of decentralizing tax collection sites to avoid congestion and facilitate taxpayer access.
This initiative is part of a broader effort to strengthen tax compliance, according to Kinshasa City Hall.
Following a meeting held on January 21, provincial authorities announced several measures targeting property owners and landlords, including:
Public display of taxpayers in good standing,
The opening of additional counters,
Making certain civil status documents conditional upon the regular payment of municipal taxes.
These measures aim to consolidate the transparency and efficiency of Kinshasa’s tax system while strengthening the culture of tax citizenship, City Hall stated.

title: Congolese Activists Call for Wider Awareness of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code
excerpt: Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa. Speaking at t
title_en: Congolese Activists Call for Wider Awareness of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code
excerpt_en: Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa. Speaking at t
body_en:
Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa.
Speaking at the event, Ghislain Kabeya Mottomoke from the Ministry of Digital Economy stressed that the main goal is to strengthen public awareness of the Digital Code.
“We have the Digital Code, particularly Article 356, which defines everyone’s responsibilities. Anyone who spreads tribalist, racist, or xenophobic content faces penalties ranging from one month to two years in prison and fines of 500,000 to 10,000,000 Congolese francs,” he explained. “We then move to Article 359, which condemns harassment.”
He further noted that Article 360 explicitly prohibits the spread of rumors and false information:
“When such content is disseminated, it incurs criminal liability. Penalties range from one to six months in prison and a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 Congolese francs. These penalties may be combined or applied separately, at the discretion of the judge.”
For General Jean-Romain Kalemba Makengo, representing the Directorate of Telecommunications and New Technologies of the Congolese National Police, public collaboration remains essential in combating cybercrime.
“The Congolese National Police is working hand in hand with the public to stop cyberbullies in their harmful activities,” he said.
The conference was organized by the Political Affairs Division of MONUSCO, in partnership with the Ministry of Digital Economy.

title: United States Renews AGOA, Opening Major Export Opportunities for the DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 – The United States Congress has officially renewed the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) until December 31, 2026, allowing the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to continue exporting over 6,000 products duty-free to the American market. Govern
title_en: United States Renews AGOA, Opening Major Export Opportunities for the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 – The United States Congress has officially renewed the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) until December 31, 2026, allowing the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to continue exporting over 6,000 products duty-free to the American market. Govern
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 – The United States Congress has officially renewed the African Growth and Opportunity Act (AGOA) until December 31, 2026, allowing the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to continue exporting over 6,000 products duty-free to the American market.
Government Welcomes Renewal The Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, hailed the decision on Wednesday, February 4, describing it as a “strong signal” for the diversification of the national economy. He emphasized that the renewal reflects international recognition of Kinshasa’s economic reform efforts.
The DRC has identified 26 priority products eligible for U.S. trade preferences, and Minister Paluku urged economic operators, particularly in agribusiness, to seize the opportunity.
“We are calling on our economic operators: cocoa, coffee, palm oil, and many other products are included. This allows our people to return to their roots, to cultivate more. Today, the American market is available to Congolese people to sell their products,” the minister declared.
Banana Port: Key Infrastructure Boost In parallel with the AGOA renewal, the minister provided an update on the deep-water port of Banana, crucial for shipping Congolese exports. During his mission to Dubai, he met executives of DP World, the concessionaire of the port.
Key updates include:
Deadline: Completion of the first phase by the end of 2026
Impact: Arrival of the first cargoes and improved trade flow between the DRC and global markets
Goal: Reduce reliance on neighboring countries’ ports and enhance export competitiveness
AGOA Forum in Kinshasa The renewal of AGOA coincides with preparations for the next AGOA Forum in Kinshasa. body_en:
Lubumbashi, February 4, 2026 – The Ministry of Environment took decisive action against the CDM mining company on Wednesday, February 4, following a catastrophic acid water spill in November 2025. Environment Minister Marie Nyange ordered the suspension of operations, making any resumption contingent on a comprehensive environmental risk assessment.
Incident Spurs Expert Investigation The November 4th incident involved the overflow of an acid water discharge basin, severely polluting Lubumbashi’s environment. In response, the minister established a commission of national and international experts tasked with:
Analyzing technical and structural causes of the spill
Identifying shortcomings in toxic waste management
Proposing sustainable solutions to prevent recurrence and safeguard ecosystems
Compliance With Environmental Standards During a meeting with mining operators in Haut-Katanga, Minister Nyange underscored the government’s stance: industrial development must not compromise environmental standards.
“Our approach aims to establish mining operations that respect environmental standards and comply with the country’s international commitments. Pollution will no longer be tolerated,” Nyange emphasized.
Rising Pressure on Mining Sector This action reflects increasing pressure on the mining industry in Haut-Katanga province to assume its social and environmental responsibilities, especially in a region characterized by heavy industrial activity.

body_en:
Manono – February 8, 2026 – Employees of COLINGO, a subcontractor of Manono Lithium, staged a demonstration on Friday, February 6, demanding the implementation of the government-mandated minimum wage of 21,500 FC per day, instead of the 13,500 FC they currently receive.
A COLINGO supervisor explained the background of the dispute:
“We had agreed with our supervisor that he would start paying us 13,500 FC per day. There was also the issue of work uniforms that needed to be resolved: we had to buy the uniforms and vests for 48,000 FC, and that was done.”
The supervisor, who has been working with the company for six months, highlighted the challenges faced by employees in securing fair wages and proper work conditions.

title: The Beni Health Zone Receives Medication for Malnutrition and Malaria
excerpt: The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severe
title_en: The Beni Health Zone Receives Medication for Malnutrition and Malaria
excerpt_en: The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severe
body_en:
The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severely affected by these endemic diseases, worsened by armed conflict, according to regional authorities.
Local health officials welcomed this aid as the result of repeated advocacy efforts, following a rise in cases and deaths linked to malaria and malnutrition.
The zone’s chief medical officer, Dr. Kasereka Tosalisana Michel, thanked the national and provincial authorities for their swift response to a scourge devastating the population.
“We thank the central and provincial governments for this crucial step in the fight against malaria, in addition to the horrors of war,” said Dr. Kasereka.
Prisca Kamala Luanda, the provincial health coordinator, added:
“This endemic area has recorded numerous cases and deaths; the government has heard the population’s cries for help.”
The handover ceremony took place at the Beni health zone office, in the presence of provincial authorities and health partners, signaling hope for a significant decrease in cases in the coming weeks.

title: Five Dead in SNCC Train Derailment Near Kabanda Bridge

title_en: Five Dead in SNCC Train Derailment Near Kabanda Bridge
excerpt_en: On Saturday, January 31, a train operated by the National Railway Company of Congo (SNCC) derailed in Tanganyika province, resulting in five deaths and multiple injuries. Two of the victims were burned beyond recognition. The Bana-Katanga train left the tracks and plunged into a
body_en:
On Saturday, January 31, a train operated by the National Railway Company of Congo (SNCC) derailed in Tanganyika province, resulting in five deaths and multiple injuries. Two of the victims were burned beyond recognition.
The Bana-Katanga train left the tracks and plunged into a ravine near the Kabanda bridge, between the villages of Kiluba and Makala, causing a fire and significant material damage.
According to Norris Mulongoy, provincial Minister of Transport for Tanganyika, the accident was caused by the poor condition of the tracks. Several injured passengers were transferred to Kalemie for medical care.
“The locomotive left the tracks before plunging into the ravine, causing a fire. Five people—three men, a woman, and a baby—were burned beyond recognition. This morning, the provincial government dispatched a team that provided details of the tragedy,” Mulongoy said.
Authorities continue to search for any additional bodies in the wreckage. Some local sources suggest the death toll may be higher, reporting eight dead and five injured.

title: NGO Launches $70,000 Appeal for ADF Attack Survivors in Lubero
excerpt: Lubero, North Kivu – 07/02/2026 – Facing a humanitarian emergency in the Lubero territory, the Integrated Federation for Reconstruction and Development (FIRD) has launched a $70,000 fundraising campaign to assist survivors of ADF attacks. The solidarity initiative, named “Save th
title_en: NGO Launches $70,000 Appeal for ADF Attack Survivors in Lubero
excerpt_en: Lubero, North Kivu – 07/02/2026 – Facing a humanitarian emergency in the Lubero territory, the Integrated Federation for Reconstruction and Development (FIRD) has launched a $70,000 fundraising campaign to assist survivors of ADF attacks. The solidarity initiative, named “Save th
body_en:
Lubero, North Kivu – 07/02/2026 – Facing a humanitarian emergency in the Lubero territory, the Integrated Federation for Reconstruction and Development (FIRD) has launched a $70,000 fundraising campaign to assist survivors of ADF attacks. The solidarity initiative, named “Save the Survivors of the ADF Massacres,” seeks to provide medical and social care to dozens of victims affected by recent attacks in the Bapere sector and Baswagha chiefdom.
According to FIRD, the wounded are in critical condition, with many forced to interrupt treatment due to lack of financial resources. The campaign targets the immediate needs of more than 80 people, including:
Over 30 seriously injured individuals hospitalized in various healthcare facilities.
More than 40 orphaned children who lost their parents in the massacres.
Exorbitant medical costs, which some patients cannot cover.
Zaidel Ngolo, coordinator of FIRD, highlighted the scale of the financial needs, noting that some patients require transfers to specialized centers or even treatment abroad.
“The need is immense. Some of the injured face medical bills of $2,000 to $3,000. This campaign aims to raise approximately $70,000 to address urgent healthcare needs,” Ngolo explained.
The NGO is appealing to individuals, businesses, and all people of goodwill for compassion and generosity to save the lives of those affected by the violence.

title: Awareness Campaigns Promote Peaceful Coexistence in Djugu
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri February 6, 2026 – Public gatherings are being regularly organized in the Walendu Djatsi sector of Djugu territory to promote peace and social cohesion, a Radio Okapi reporter observed on Friday, February 6. Initiated by traditional authorities and security forces, t
title_en: Awareness Campaigns Promote Peaceful Coexistence in Djugu
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri February 6, 2026 – Public gatherings are being regularly organized in the Walendu Djatsi sector of Djugu territory to promote peace and social cohesion, a Radio Okapi reporter observed on Friday, February 6. Initiated by traditional authorities and security forces, t
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri February 6, 2026 – Public gatherings are being regularly organized in the Walendu Djatsi sector of Djugu territory to promote peace and social cohesion, a Radio Okapi reporter observed on Friday, February 6.
Initiated by traditional authorities and security forces, these awareness campaigns aim to foster peaceful coexistence among local communities. The initiatives have been welcomed by civil society, which calls for greater involvement of young people in the process.
According to Justin Gudza, head of the Walendu Djatsi sector, all segments of society are engaged, including youth, religious leaders, educators, and military and police authorities.
“Markets and places of worship are frequented by all communities. Traffic flows smoothly. People need to interact, speak the same language, and consider each other as brothers,” Gudza explained.
Youth Called Upon to Get Involved
Germain Mapasa, local civil society coordinator, stressed that lasting peace depends on the active involvement of young people.
“We ask all the communities of Djugu to accept one another and forget the past. We call on our youth to support all initiatives likely to bring about lasting peace. Before, we didn’t question who was Mulendu or Muhema. We must not let manipulators divide us,” he emphasized.
During the campaigns, local authorities also highlight the importance of good civil-military relations to ensure the effective protection of the population.

title: PDDRCS Seen as Key to Strengthening Peace Efforts in Ituri
excerpt: Djugu, Ituri, February 7, 2026 – The administrator of Djugu territory, Chief Commissioner Ruffin Mapela, has emphasized that the Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization Program (PDDRCS) could play a critical role in strengthening peace efforts in Ituri.
title_en: PDDRCS Seen as Key to Strengthening Peace Efforts in Ituri
excerpt_en: Djugu, Ituri, February 7, 2026 – The administrator of Djugu territory, Chief Commissioner Ruffin Mapela, has emphasized that the Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization Program (PDDRCS) could play a critical role in strengthening peace efforts in Ituri.
body_en:
Djugu, Ituri, February 7, 2026 – The administrator of Djugu territory, Chief Commissioner Ruffin Mapela, has emphasized that the Disarmament, Demobilization, Community Recovery and Stabilization Program (PDDRCS) could play a critical role in strengthening peace efforts in Ituri.
Speaking on Saturday, February 7, the Congolese National Police officer praised armed groups that are implementing recommendations from the Aru 1 and Aru 2 talks.
“It is already a first step for us to see these young armed men agree to meet and seek solutions for peace. We know that there is a program, the disarmament and demobilization program, which should support these young people who participated in the Aru 1 and Aru 2 dialogues so that they can implement the resolutions from these meetings,” said Mapela.
The administrator also acknowledged that one armed group continues to disrupt the situation. He pledged to take all necessary steps to involve this faction in the peace program.
“There are always difficulties that require solutions. Since other armed groups have agreed to join this program and surrender their weapons, we will continue to build on this momentum so that peace is fully restored throughout the country,” Mapela concluded.

body_en:
Beni, North Kivu, February 7, 2026 – On Saturday, religious leaders urged the army’s civic and patriotic education service and the FARDC Grand North operational sector command to strengthen civil-military relations, seen as a guarantee of lasting peace, in Beni, North Kivu.
The appeal came during a working session attended by nearly 100 religious leaders and FARDC Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of operations and intelligence, General Jacques Kyaligonza Nduru.
During his mission in Beni, General Nduru emphasized the need to involve all segments of the population, including the religious community, in efforts to find lasting solutions to restore peace in the region.
The area remains affected by the activities of the ADF rebels. According to a report by the Congolese Institute for Research on Politics, Governance and Violence (Ebuteli), this rebel group is responsible for some of the most atrocious acts of violence in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The report notes that the ADF perpetrates massacres not only to recruit new fighters, but also to undermine the legitimacy of governments combating them.

title: Trial of General Philémon Yav: Informant Confirms Alleged Demoralizing Remarks in Goma
excerpt: Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
title_en: Trial of General Philémon Yav: Informant Confirms Alleged Demoralizing Remarks in Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
body_en:
Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
Those heard by the court were Lieutenant General Ndima Kongba Constant, former military governor of North Kivu; Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa Efomi, former communications adviser to the same governor; Brigadier General Yangba Tene Dany, former operations adviser; and Brigadier General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, former commander of the Sukola 2 South operational sector in South Kivu.
The judges questioned the witnesses about two messages that, according to the prosecution, form the basis of the charges and the arrest of General Yav. General Mwehu was specifically asked about a conversation with the defendant during a meeting in Goma, during which General Yav allegedly told him: “You, General Mwehu, are always at the front. The victory will benefit these Bangala. We won’t see you.” The prosecution argues that this statement was likely to demoralize the troops.
In his testimony, General Mwehu confirmed the exchange, stating that such remarks, coming from a superior officer, could indeed discourage soldiers. According to the prosecution, this constitutes the offense of inciting military personnel to act contrary to duty or discipline, while another message reportedly attributed to the late General Peter Cirimwami is being treated as treason, comparable to participation in an insurrection.
“Your Honor, it’s true,” General Mwehu told the court. “The Commander of the Third Defense Zone did not have an office in Goma; his office was in Kisangani. He often came for hearings or operational meetings and usually stayed at the Serena Hotel. I was returning to the field when I learned he was in Goma. I went to see him to give operational reports. As we were leaving the hotel courtyard, he made that statement. I did not react, and we moved on to another topic.”
General Yav Irung is suspected of having links to the inner circle of James Kabarebe. Reassigned to eastern DRC in 2020, he was appointed commander of the Third Defense Zone, a strategic military area covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo. His trial comes nearly three years after his arrest in September 2022.
Nicknamed “The Tiger,” General Yav is among officers from the Greater Katanga region whose arrests have been cited by some political figures, including former President Joseph Kabila, as evidence of marginalization under President Félix Tshisekedi. The Congolese army has consistently rejected these claims, insisting that military justice operates strictly within the framework of the law and without ethnic considerations.

title: OLPA Acknowledges the Release of a Journalist in Kamanyola
excerpt: February 3, 2026 — The Observatory for Press Freedom in Africa (OLPA) confirms the release of Samson Fabrice Nyandabaga, journalist and director of Flash FM, a community radio station in Kamanyola (47 km from Bukavu, South Kivu, DRC). The journalist was released on January 31, 20
title_en: OLPA Acknowledges the Release of a Journalist in Kamanyola
excerpt_en: February 3, 2026 — The Observatory for Press Freedom in Africa (OLPA) confirms the release of Samson Fabrice Nyandabaga, journalist and director of Flash FM, a community radio station in Kamanyola (47 km from Bukavu, South Kivu, DRC). The journalist was released on January 31, 20
body_en:
February 3, 2026 — The Observatory for Press Freedom in Africa (OLPA) confirms the release of Samson Fabrice Nyandabaga, journalist and director of Flash FM, a community radio station in Kamanyola (47 km from Bukavu, South Kivu, DRC).
The journalist was released on January 31, 2026, after 72 hours of detention in the intelligence cell of the AFC-M23 rebel movement.
He had been arrested on January 28, 2026, while covering the living conditions of displaced people in Uvira, following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels. During his detention, he faced intense interrogation about alleged ties to international media and Congolese journalists reporting on issues deemed hostile by the rebels.
OLPA condemns this unjustified imprisonment, highlighting it as a clear violation of press freedom, which is guaranteed by Congolese law and international human rights instruments.
This incident underscores the ongoing risks faced by journalists operating in conflict-affected regions of eastern DRC.

title: The summary proceedings against three magistrates at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal continued on Monday, January 26, at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal in Lubumbashi. The trial pits the public prosecutor against three magistrates from the Tanganyika Court of Appeal, as well as a merchant, all charged with corruption in a case related to attempted rape with violence.

title_en: The summary proceedings against three magistrates at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal continued on Monday, January 26, at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal in Lubumbashi. The trial pits the public prosecutor against three magistrates from the Tanganyika Court of Appeal, as well as a merchant, all charged with corruption in a case related to attempted rape with violence.
excerpt_en: The opening of the hearings on Friday, January 23, was already noteworthy due to the presence of the President of the Court of Cassation and the First Advocate General of the Republic, who traveled from Kinshasa specifically to attend the proceedings. The Court began its investig
body_en:
The opening of the hearings on Friday, January 23, was already noteworthy due to the presence of the President of the Court of Cassation and the First Advocate General of the Republic, who traveled from Kinshasa specifically to attend the proceedings.
The Court began its investigation by identifying the four defendants. Each was then called to the stand to give their account of the events. The defense team challenged the procedure, arguing a lack of evidence in a criminal case being tried under summary proceedings.
At the conclusion of the proceedings, the prosecution requested three years of imprisonment for the magistrates and two years for the merchant. The hearing was adjourned until Monday.
Background
In July 2025, in Kalemie, a woman filed a complaint against merchant Joseph Kafwimbi Kiwele for attempted rape. The Kalemie High Court acquitted the accused. Dissatisfied, the plaintiff appealed to the Tanganyika Court of Appeal.
On December 19, this court sentenced merchant Patrick Kafwimbi to six months of house arrest and a fine of $10,000. Some magistrates deemed this sentence insufficient given the seriousness of the alleged offenses.

title: Kongo Central Assembly Authorizes Judicial Investigation Against Governor Grâce Bilolo
excerpt: The Bureau of the Kongo Central Provincial Assembly authorized, on Wednesday, January 28, the opening of a judicial investigation against the provincial governor, Grâce Nkuanga Masuangi Bilolo. This decision follows a request from the Attorney General at the Court of Cassation, w
title_en: Kongo Central Assembly Authorizes Judicial Investigation Against Governor Grâce Bilolo
excerpt_en: The Bureau of the Kongo Central Provincial Assembly authorized, on Wednesday, January 28, the opening of a judicial investigation against the provincial governor, Grâce Nkuanga Masuangi Bilolo. This decision follows a request from the Attorney General at the Court of Cassation, w
body_en:
The Bureau of the Kongo Central Provincial Assembly authorized, on Wednesday, January 28, the opening of a judicial investigation against the provincial governor, Grâce Nkuanga Masuangi Bilolo.
This decision follows a request from the Attorney General at the Court of Cassation, who submitted an indictment seeking authorization. The governor met with members of the Bureau prior to their deliberations.
The five members of the Bureau stated that they reviewed the relevant legal texts, including the Constitution, the organic law on the Court of Cassation, laws governing the provinces, and the rules of procedure of the Provincial Assembly. They also considered the facts outlined in the indictment, the urgency of the case, and their discussions with the governor.
While reaffirming the importance of the presumption of innocence, the Bureau granted the Attorney General’s request. This decision requires the Governor of Kongo Central to appear before the competent court to present his defense.
Since last week, the Attorney General had sought this authorization following a damning report from the General Inspectorate of Finance (IGF), which revealed the embezzlement of more than one million US dollars.

title: DRC Validates 2026 Roadmap for Recognition of Genocides
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil. The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the Nationa
title_en: DRC Validates 2026 Roadmap for Recognition of Genocides
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil. The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the Nationa
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil.
The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the National Fund for Victim Reparations (FONAREV) and the Inter-institutional Commission for Victim Assistance and Support for Reforms (CIA-VAR), chaired by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba.
During the session, Minister Mbemba and his counterparts outlined planned actions at both national and international levels, including the drafting of a preliminary bill for the preservation and protection of memorial heritage linked to international crimes in the DRC and the suppression of genocide denial.
The discussions also touched on the upcoming dialogue involving members of the Government, the National Assembly, the Senate, parliamentary committees, and the diplomatic corps accredited to the DRC.
Minister Mbemba emphasized that the initiative seeks effective recognition by states and international organizations of genocides committed in the DRC by Rwanda, noting that such recognition has already been acknowledged by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights.

title: FARDC Repels AFC/M23 Attack on Strategic Nkobe Hill Near Pinga
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory. According to the administrativ

excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory. According to the administrativ
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory.
According to the administrative secretary of the Kisimba group, the rebels have launched repeated attempts in recent days to breach security defenses and penetrate Pinga, but without success. On Friday, January 23, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly tried to outflank positions held by the FARDC and the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP) at Nkobe Hill, which overlooks the village of Munsanga.
The assault was met with a strong response from loyalist forces, forcing the attackers to retreat toward Buhaya, near Mpety, in the Banakindi area, considered the rebels’ main stronghold in the Pinga region.
A fragile calm was observed on Saturday, with Nkobe Hill remaining firmly under the control of the FARDC.
The human and material toll of the clashes was not immediately available at the time of publication.

On Friday, January 23, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly tried to outflank positions held by the FARDC and the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP) at Nkobe Hill, which overlooks the village of Munsanga.

The human and material toll of the clashes was not immediately available at the time of publication.

title: FARDC Denounces Alleged Stratagems of Rwandan Army and AFC/M23 After Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal f
title_en: FARDC Denounces Alleged Stratagems of Rwandan Army and AFC/M23 After Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal f
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal from Uvira, in South Kivu province.
In a statement released on Friday, January 23, the FARDC said these maneuvers were observed immediately after the armed groups pulled out of the city. According to the army, on the eve of their departure, the Rwandan forces and AFC/M23 rebels allegedly systematically looted Uvira, leaving the city “at the mercy of well-organized gangs of looters.”
The FARDC reported that the destruction and theft targeted key state and private infrastructure, including road rehabilitation equipment and state-owned vehicles.
The statement further claims that these operations were planned during a meeting on January 17, 2026, in Uvira, involving representatives of the Rwandan army, AFC/M23, and their allies Twiraného and Red Tabara.
The Congolese army also rejected allegations of abuses committed by its forces against certain communities, describing them as “a blatant lie fabricated within the Rwandan army.” The FARDC said it had deployed security and protection measures for all communities, including the Banyamulenge, whom it said had “refused to be manipulated” by armed groups.
This stance echoes remarks by the mayor of Uvira, who acknowledged the complexity of the security situation in the city. The mayor said that “there were imposters posing as FARDC and imposters posing as Wazalendo who harassed the population,” adding that these individuals, after returning from the city, “learned their lesson and will certainly change.”
The mayor further stressed that “not all the incidents that occurred can be attributed to the regular forces, who act in accordance with human rights and the protection of civilians.”
In its statement, the FARDC reaffirmed that it would “not tolerate any act of genocide planned or carried out on Congolese soil” and reiterated its “firm determination to defend the integrity of the national territory and to protect all communities and their property, even unto the ultimate sacrifice.”
Following the withdrawal of the rebels, local authorities returned to Uvira and pledged to prepare for the return of Congolese refugees who had fled to Burundi during the fighting.

title: Kinshasa Pays Final Tribute to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death. The late gener
title_en: Kinshasa Pays Final Tribute to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death. The late gener
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death.
The late general, who died on Friday, September 12, 2025, following a sudden illness while on duty, was laid to rest at the “Le Repos du Soldat” military cemetery in Kinshasa. He passed away at the Uvira General Hospital, where he had been serving in South Kivu province.
His burial was preceded by a state-level funeral ceremony held at the Ave Maria venue in the Kasa-Vubu district, attended by the Second Vice-President of the National Assembly, Christophe Mboso N’kodia, and the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, who represented the President of the Republic and Supreme Commander of the FARDC, Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. Also present were general and senior officers, civil authorities, and members of the bereaved family.
On behalf of the Supreme Commander of the FARDC, the Minister of National Defense laid a wreath, honoring the late officer’s loyal service to the nation and his death in the line of duty.
Speaking for the family, a representative described the general as “a beloved man whose life was built on rigor, sacrifice, and selflessness.” He added that Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel “embodied the fundamental values of the army: honor, discipline, loyalty, and a sense of duty,” noting that he “wore the uniform with dignity, exercised command with justice, and fulfilled his responsibilities with exemplary integrity.”
A graduate of the 23rd class of the Kananga Officer Training School, the late general had served the nation since 1974. “Almost his entire adult life was dedicated to serving his country, often far from his family, with the sole motivation of defending the people and honoring the national flag,” the family representative said.
A well-known figure in the military hierarchy of South Kivu, General Muaku had recently visited those wounded in deadly demonstrations attributed to the Wazalendo. He had arrived in Uvira on August 4, shortly after his appointment, to succeed General Dunia Kashindi as commander of the 33rd Military Region.
He was assisted by two deputies: General Olivier Gasita Mukunda, in charge of operations and intelligence, and Jean-Ladis Mabosso, in charge of administration.
The announcement of his death came amid a tense security context in Uvira, where demonstrations had erupted over the appointment of General Olivier Gasita Mukunda. Sections of the local population had demanded his removal, prompting a government delegation to travel to the city on Thursday, September 11, 2025.

title: After Meeting Denis Sassou Nguesso, Félix Tshisekedi Condemns “Unjust” and “Barbaric” War in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Oyo, January 25, 2026 — President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) met on Saturday, January 24, with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, in the city of Oyo, where the two leaders discussed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation a
title_en: After Meeting Denis Sassou Nguesso, Félix Tshisekedi Condemns “Unjust” and “Barbaric” War in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Oyo, January 25, 2026 — President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) met on Saturday, January 24, with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, in the city of Oyo, where the two leaders discussed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation a
body_en:
Oyo, January 25, 2026 — President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) met on Saturday, January 24, with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, in the city of Oyo, where the two leaders discussed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation and good neighborly relations between their countries.
The talks focused heavily on the deteriorating security situation in the Great Lakes region, particularly the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, and efforts to achieve lasting peace. President Tshisekedi said that despite the existence of the Washington and Doha peace processes, some parties continue to fail to honor their commitments.
“He is an elder statesman of the region, a Head of State who is very influential,” Tshisekedi told the press after the meeting. “It was only natural to brief him on what is happening in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In the East, there is a war — an unjust and barbaric war imposed upon us. There are peace processes that have been initiated, to which the protagonists have committed, but which are not being respected by some.”
The meeting comes amid persistent tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali, despite the involvement of U.S. President Donald Trump and what authorities describe as renewed momentum in the Washington process, marked by the ratification of agreements by Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame. However, the situation on the ground remains fragile, with both sides exchanging accusations of non-compliance.
A similar impasse is affecting the Doha talks, held under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar, between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 rebellion, which the Congolese government says is supported by Rwanda. These negotiations, intended to address the root causes of the conflict — including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups — have yet to yield tangible results. Several agreed measures, including those outlined in the joint communiqué, the ceasefire mechanism, the declaration of principles, and the framework agreement, remain unimplemented.
This diplomatic inertia has coincided with the continuation of violent clashes between the AFC/M23 and government forces. Meanwhile, calls from socio-political actors to convene a national dialogue have yet to be heeded.
After announcing its withdrawal from mediation efforts in March 2025, Angola has begun a gradual and discreet return to the peace process, relaunching consultations and increasing contacts with key stakeholders. In parallel, Togo hosted a high-level meeting on Saturday, January 17, 2026, aimed at strengthening the coherence and consolidation of peace initiatives in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.

title: FARDC Airstrikes Hit AFC/M23 Strongholds Mpety and Mindjendje in Walikale
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu – January 25, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have intensified military pressure on the AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, launching targeted airstrikes on what are described as their main strongholds. Late on Saturday e
title_en: FARDC Airstrikes Hit AFC/M23 Strongholds Mpety and Mindjendje in Walikale
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu – January 25, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have intensified military pressure on the AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, launching targeted airstrikes on what are described as their main strongholds. Late on Saturday e
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu – January 25, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have intensified military pressure on the AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, launching targeted airstrikes on what are described as their main strongholds.
Late on Saturday evening, January 24, an FARDC attack drone bombed rebel positions in Mpety and Mindjendje, located in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group. These two sites are considered the principal logistics and operational bases of the rebels around the strategic town of Pinga.
According to local sources, the drone flew over the Banakindi airspace at around 6:00 p.m. local time before dropping several bombs on the targeted positions. Mpety, situated just 18 kilometers from Pinga, reportedly housed a major logistical hub for the AFC/M23.
The information was confirmed by Lavie Changwi, administrative secretary of the Kisimba group, who said the explosions triggered widespread panic among residents.
“The population was caught off guard by the loud detonations. People stayed indoors, fearing reprisals or an escalation of the fighting,” he said.
While the official human and material toll remains unknown, multiple sources in the area report the destruction of several rebel positions, with significant loss of life and heavy material damage.
Local leaders say Mpety and Mindjendje served as regrouping and supply centers for the rebels, who had recently received reinforcements from Kitshanga, Mwesso, and Kalembe in Masisi territory. These reinforcements were reportedly intended to prepare a large-scale offensive against Pinga, a key strategic stronghold in this part of North Kivu.
The latest airstrikes come just 24 hours after the bombing of Buleusa, in the Ikobo area, where another AFC/M23 position was reportedly completely destroyed. Through these successive air operations, the FARDC appears determined to degrade the rebels’ operational capacity and prevent any advance toward other strategic locations in Walikale territory.

title: AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira: Government Says “Chaos Envisioned by the Enemy Did Not Occur”
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 25, 2026 — The withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, was discussed for the first time during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, January 23, at the African Union City complex, under the ch
title_en: AFC/M23 Withdrawal from Uvira: Government Says “Chaos Envisioned by the Enemy Did Not Occur”
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 25, 2026 — The withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, was discussed for the first time during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, January 23, at the African Union City complex, under the ch
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 25, 2026 — The withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion from the city of Uvira, in South Kivu province, was discussed for the first time during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, January 23, at the African Union City complex, under the chairmanship of Prime Minister Judith Suminwa.
Presenting the operational situation across the country, particularly in North Kivu and South Kivu, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, reported the return of security forces to Uvira to ensure public order and the protection of civilians.
He said the chaos scenario predicted by the rebellion following its withdrawal had been thwarted, thanks to measures taken with various military commands to guarantee the safety of all communities.
“Following the withdrawal of RDF/M23 coalition troops from the city of Uvira, units of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo resumed their initial positions to ensure the firm defense of the city and the protection of the population, particularly members of the Banyamulenge community. The chaos envisioned by the enemy, through the manipulation of local communities, did not materialize, thanks to the firm instructions given to the commanders of operations as well as to the military justice authorities, with a view to punishing any transgressions,” read the minutes of the Council of Ministers.
This development comes amid controversy surrounding the AFC/M23 announcement of its withdrawal from Uvira, which Congolese authorities believe was intended to divert attention and ease international pressure, particularly from the United States, on Kigali, which the United Nations considers the rebellion’s main supporter.
On the ground, however, the AFC/M23 continues to make territorial gains and to establish a parallel administration beyond the control of central authorities.
In a letter dated Thursday, January 15, 2026, to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the political coordinator of the AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, announced that he had placed the strategic city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community. The group said this move was consistent with its decision to withdraw its forces, first announced on December 15, 2025, and recently reiterated, citing its commitment to the ceasefire.
In the same letter, the AFC/M23 also announced the immediate withdrawal of its “observation and monitoring unit,” declining any further responsibility for the security of the city.
A strategic hub in the Congolese government’s security architecture in South Kivu, Uvira had briefly slipped from Kinshasa’s control, strengthening the rebellion’s grip in North and South Kivu. The city is viewed as a key gateway that could facilitate an advance toward the Greater Katanga region, considered the economic heartland of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: When Diplomacy Failed: The Weeks Leading to the Fall of Goma
excerpt: Goma, January 26, 2026 — One year ago, the city of Goma, the provincial capital of North Kivu and the main urban center of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), fell under the control of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 movement. The battle that preceded its capture was of unprec
title_en: When Diplomacy Failed: The Weeks Leading to the Fall of Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, January 26, 2026 — One year ago, the city of Goma, the provincial capital of North Kivu and the main urban center of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), fell under the control of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 movement. The battle that preceded its capture was of unprec
body_en:
Goma, January 26, 2026 — One year ago, the city of Goma, the provincial capital of North Kivu and the main urban center of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), fell under the control of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 movement. The battle that preceded its capture was of unprecedented intensity, marking a major turning point in the conflict in eastern Congo.
One year later, with the movement still administering the city, this report revisits the political, diplomatic, and military events that paved the way for the Battle of Goma.
December 2024: The Failure of Angolan Mediation
On December 15, 2024, in Luanda, hopes were high. Angola was on the verge of brokering a peace agreement between Kinshasa and Kigali. Both delegations had nearly finalized a text, including a Concept of Operations (CONOPS) detailing military commitments and an implementation timeline.
However, negotiations collapsed over one key issue: Kinshasa’s categorical refusal to negotiate with the AFC/M23, a condition set by Rwanda for signing the agreement. On December 16, President Paul Kagame did not travel to Luanda. President Félix Tshisekedi arrived alone. The agreement was never signed.
Following this diplomatic failure, military pressure rapidly intensified on the ground.
A Military Escalation Documented by the United Nations
In the days that followed, the United Nations documented the deployment of sophisticated weaponry by Rwandan forces in M23-controlled areas, including surface-to-air missiles and GPS jamming systems. These capabilities severely restricted the use of aircraft and drones by Congolese forces and their allies.
In response, President Félix Tshisekedi sought regional support. On December 21, he traveled to Brazzaville, followed by Bujumbura on December 22. Domestically, he initiated sweeping changes within the military command. Four days later, several senior officers were replaced, including the commander of the Third Defense Zone, responsible for North Kivu. The FARDC Chief of Staff had already been replaced ten days earlier.
January 2025: The M23 Advance Toward Goma
The conflict soon shifted decisively to the battlefield. On Friday, January 3, the AFC/M23 captured Katale. The next day, Masisi-centre fell, bringing rebel forces within 80 kilometers of Goma. On January 7, fighting was reported around Saké, a strategic town about 30 kilometers west of Goma.
At the same time, UN experts stated that Rwandan Defense Forces had “continued to provide systematic support to the M23 and effectively controlled its operations.” According to these reports, General Sultani Makenga, the movement’s military leader, continued to “receive instructions and support from Rwandan forces and intelligence services.”
During the first two weeks of January, multiple fronts became active simultaneously — in Masisi, southern Lubero, Rutshuru, and Nyiragongo. Fighting was intense, prolonged, and steadily advanced toward Goma.
The Final Week Before the Fall
On January 18, 2025, President Tshisekedi addressed ambassadors accredited in Kinshasa, calling on Western countries to impose targeted sanctions against Rwanda, which he accused of backing the M23.
Five days later, fighting around Saké escalated further. On January 23, Major General Peter Cirimwami, military governor of North Kivu, was shot and seriously wounded while traveling to the front line west of Goma. He later succumbed to his injuries.
On Saturday, January 25, clashes reached the immediate outskirts of Goma. The Congolese army and its allies faced the M23, backed by Rwanda. Thirteen soldiers — from South Africa, Malawi, and Uruguay, deployed with the SADC regional force or the UN mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) — were killed.
In response, Kinshasa recalled its diplomats from Kigali and gave Rwanda 48 hours to cease all diplomatic activity on Congolese soil.
Goma Plunged Into Chaos
The impact on the city was immediate. High-voltage power lines were cut during the fighting, plunging Goma into darkness and soon cutting off water supplies. M23 fighters and Rwandan soldiers entered the city.
On Monday, January 27, gunfire was heard in the city center, and M23 elements and Rwandan special forces were reported in several neighborhoods. The day before, UN Secretary-General António Guterres had directly blamed Kigali after another day of fighting.
Clashes continued, particularly around the southern part of Goma airport. On the Rwandan side, a spokesperson for the Rwandan Defense Forces reported at least five dead and 24 seriously wounded in a border locality.
That same day, a mass escape occurred at Munzenze prison, which held around 3,000 inmates. On Tuesday, January 28, Goma awoke to heavy detonations and exchanges of fire, while in Kinshasa, protests erupted in several districts, including Limete, Kitambo, and the administrative area of Gombe.
Hospitals in Goma were overwhelmed, unable to cope with the influx of wounded.
On Wednesday, January 29, several hundred Romanian nationals — described by Kinshasa as military instructors with the FARDC and by Kigali as mercenaries — crossed into Gisenyi, Rwanda, before being evacuated to Romania.
