title: Fighting Intensifies, Thousands Displaced Without Humanitarian Assistance in Fizi
excerpt: South Kivu February 4, 2026 — Thousands of displaced people in Fizi, South Kivu, are living in inhumane conditions, lacking water, food, and healthcare, as ongoing fighting between the Congolese army (FARDC) and allies against AFC/M23 rebels worsens the humanitarian crisis. Autho
title_en: Fighting Intensifies, Thousands Displaced Without Humanitarian Assistance in Fizi
excerpt_en: South Kivu February 4, 2026 — Thousands of displaced people in Fizi, South Kivu, are living in inhumane conditions, lacking water, food, and healthcare, as ongoing fighting between the Congolese army (FARDC) and allies against AFC/M23 rebels worsens the humanitarian crisis. Autho
body_en:
South Kivu February 4, 2026 — Thousands of displaced people in Fizi, South Kivu, are living in inhumane conditions, lacking water, food, and healthcare, as ongoing fighting between the Congolese army (FARDC) and allies against AFC/M23 rebels worsens the humanitarian crisis. Authorities report that at least one million inhabitants have fled their homes along various routes within the territory.
On the orders of armed groups, no displacement camps have been established, forcing people to stay with host families and struggle daily for survival.
In Ekengya village, located dozens of kilometers from Fizi town, nearly two thousand displaced people face severe hardships. Angela Mauwa Ndone, a mother of eight who fled Point Zero, described her plight:
“I am suffering greatly. Since I arrived here, my children have stopped going to school. You might find me pounding this small amount of corn; it’s today’s ration, and I don’t know where to find the rest for tomorrow. I am appealing to the Congolese government and its partners for assistance.”
Malyani Makambe, chief of Ekengya, emphasized that displaced people are exposed to disease and unable to afford healthcare fees.
“We have 1,883 displaced people from Point Zero, Rugezi, Kavanja, Kitumba, and other areas. They fled, leaving everything behind. Here, they have no access to drinking water or healthcare, and cannot pay the 50,000 to 100,000 Congolese francs required for treatment.”
Residents remain at risk from ongoing gunfire. Local observer Maurice Musema explained that with each battle in Point Zero or the Mitumba mountains, fear grips the population, who dread further escalation.
The displaced communities are calling for government intervention and comprehensive strategies to end the conflict, which is seen as the only way to stop uncontrolled displacement.
Children are out of school, some are malnourished, and adults remain uncertain about the future, highlighting the scale of the humanitarian crisis in Fizi.
The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) is working to address immediate needs, though the complexity of the crisis continues to grow daily due to ongoing fighting.

title: 4 Dead and Several Injured After Clashes Between Police and Bandits in Panu
excerpt: Panu Kwilu, February 4, 2026 — Four people were killed and several others injured during clashes between police and a group of bandits (Kuluna) in Panu, Idiofa territory, Kwilu province. Among the deceased were two police officers and two civilians. The bandits attacked in retali
title_en: 4 Dead and Several Injured After Clashes Between Police and Bandits in Panu
excerpt_en: Panu Kwilu, February 4, 2026 — Four people were killed and several others injured during clashes between police and a group of bandits (Kuluna) in Panu, Idiofa territory, Kwilu province. Among the deceased were two police officers and two civilians. The bandits attacked in retali
body_en:
Panu Kwilu, February 4, 2026 — Four people were killed and several others injured during clashes between police and a group of bandits (Kuluna) in Panu, Idiofa territory, Kwilu province. Among the deceased were two police officers and two civilians. The bandits attacked in retaliation after the arrest of their leaders, plunging the town into total panic.
Many residents spent the night in the forest, while others sought refuge along the border between Idiofa territory and Maï-Ndombe province.
Nico Mbuka, a provincial deputy from Idiofa, demanded a thorough investigation to hold perpetrators accountable and called for police reinforcements.
“They arrested one of their leaders, and the bandits, in turn, attacked the police. The clashes resulted in four deaths, two police officers and two civilians. As of now, the population is not calm. Some spent the night in the forest. Others went to the river, to the border with Maï-Ndombe, to the sandbars. There is no peace in Panu at this time.” — Nico Mbuka, provincial deputy
The territory administrator, Adelar Kintolo, confirmed the incident but noted a gradual return to calm.
These clashes have disrupted daily life in the area: markets were deserted, and activities in hospitals and schools were paralyzed.

title: Governor Announces Strengthened Security Measures Following AFC/M23 Drone Attacks at Kisangani Airport
excerpt: Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion
title_en: Governor Announces Strengthened Security Measures Following AFC/M23 Drone Attacks at Kisangani Airport
excerpt_en: Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion
body_en:
Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion.
Recipients of the circular — including village chiefs, street chiefs, block leaders, concession holders, and owners of hotels and guesthouses — are instructed to report any unknown or suspicious person within their jurisdictions.
The governor emphasized the active involvement of local officials in security operations codenamed "Yeba Voisin" and "Filimbi" (Know thy neighbor; whistle), aiming to strengthen community surveillance and prevent suspicious infiltration.
“No tolerance will be shown for any failure to comply with these instructions. Any official who fails, neglects, or refuses to transmit the required information will be held personally responsible and could be considered an accomplice, with all the consequences provided by law.” — Governor Paulin Lendongolia
Regarding the airport, the provincial governor visited Bangboka Airport, noting that operations are proceeding normally.
The AFC/M23 claimed that it targeted the drone command center at Kisangani Airport, which they assert is used to launch attacks in Walikale, Rutshuru, Lubero, Kalehe, Mwenga, Masisi, and Minembwe. The rebellion also claims to be monitoring Kisangani Airport. Authorities in Kisangani are calling on the population to remain calm.

title: US Senators Discuss M23 Occupation of Eastern DRC, Backed by Rwanda
excerpt: February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, accordin
title_en: US Senators Discuss M23 Occupation of Eastern DRC, Backed by Rwanda
excerpt_en: February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, accordin
body_en:
February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, according to a US Senate statement.
The senators, chairman and vice-chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, emphasized that the United States is ready to become a stronger partner of the DRC, noting that bipartisan support must be matched by serious efforts by all parties to honor their commitments under the agreements.
Discussions included partnerships around critical minerals and investments to revitalize the Lobito Corridor, presented as a lever for mutual economic growth, regional trade, and long-term cooperation between the US and Africa.
The senators also voiced concern over “the continued occupation of parts of eastern Congo by the Rwandan-backed M23 group”, calling for a complete withdrawal of Rwandan forces to allow for “a real chance at lasting peace.”
The statement highlighted a humanitarian catastrophe in eastern DRC, where 26 million people face acute food insecurity, stressing that women, children, and minority communities cannot remain collateral damage.
Finally, the senators stressed that long-term stability requires the DRC to take decisive action against the FDLR and the violent Wazalendo militias, and called on Kinshasa to engage in credible national dialogue or political solutions to strengthen national cohesion and the future of the bilateral partnership.

title: Burundian Presidency Announces Crisis Monitoring, Including the Situation in Eastern DRC
excerpt: African Union February 5, 2026 — Burundi is preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the African Union (AU) on February 15, 2026, marking a first since the creation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963, which later became the AU, Ambassador Edouard Bizimana an
title_en: Burundian Presidency Announces Crisis Monitoring, Including the Situation in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: African Union February 5, 2026 — Burundi is preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the African Union (AU) on February 15, 2026, marking a first since the creation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963, which later became the AU, Ambassador Edouard Bizimana an
body_en:
African Union February 5, 2026 — Burundi is preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the African Union (AU) on February 15, 2026, marking a first since the creation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963, which later became the AU, Ambassador Edouard Bizimana announced in a public address.
According to the Burundian minister, this presidency represents both “a sign of political confidence”, a political, economic, and strategic opportunity, and a collective responsibility, requiring the involvement of all Burundian society, public and private institutions, the economic sector, youth, researchers, and the country’s partners.
The address emphasizes that the Burundian presidency is occurring in a complex regional and international context, marked by armed conflicts, natural disasters, economic challenges, and a deteriorating climate for international cooperation.
Among the announced priorities are:
Accelerating the implementation of the AU's 2026 theme, “Water and Sanitation for All by 2063”.
Continuing the continental youth dialogue on peace, security, research, and innovation.
Strengthening the participation of young people and women in peace processes, within the “Silencing the Guns by 2030” initiative.
Contributing to the operationalization of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), with a focus on e-commerce, including an international symposium in Bujumbura.
Burundi will also oversee ordinary AU activities, including annual summits, statutory meetings, and monitoring relations with strategic partners, notably the European Union, China, United States, Russia, India, Japan, and the United Nations.
Continental crises will remain a focus, particularly the situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Libya, the Sahel, and Sudan, as well as natural disasters and humanitarian emergencies.
The minister called for general mobilization of the Burundian diplomatic corps and foreign missions, highlighting opportunities for international visibility and investment attraction, while acknowledging financial, logistical, and human capacity challenges.
Ambassador Edouard Bizimana concluded by commending the work of Burundi’s Permanent Mission to the AU and calling for unity to ensure the success of this continental mandate.

title_en: Kagame Defies Sanctions Threats and Rejects Any Involvement in Congo
excerpt_en: DRC–Rwanda, February 5, 2026 – Rwandan President Paul Kagame attributed ongoing tensions with the DRC to the presence of Rwandan Hutu rebels from the FDLR on Congolese territory, rejecting any claims of Kigali’s involvement in mineral exploitation during the opening of the “Umush
body_en:
DRC–Rwanda, February 5, 2026 – Rwandan President Paul Kagame attributed ongoing tensions with the DRC to the presence of Rwandan Hutu rebels from the FDLR on Congolese territory, rejecting any claims of Kigali’s involvement in mineral exploitation during the opening of the “Umushyikirano” national dialogue in Kigali.
Kagame stated:
“The problem Rwanda has with the DRC mainly concerns the FDLR present there, as well as their genocidal ideology,” asserting that these fighters threaten Rwanda. He dismissed accusations that Kigali is motivated by exploitation of Congolese resources or seeks to seize territory, calling them “pretensions.”
According to the Rwandan head of state,
“The war in the DRC was not started by Rwanda, nor did it originate in Rwanda,”adding that Rwanda’s defensive measures are unrelated to Congolese minerals, but are a response to persistent security threats since 1994.

title: Call for Investigations After Assassination of Civil Society Leader in Ituri
excerpt: Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the cir
title_en: Call for Investigations After Assassination of Civil Society Leader in Ituri
excerpt_en: Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the cir
body_en:
Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the circumstances of this crime.
According to an obituary read on Thursday, February 5, by Jean-Marie Ezadri Aguekwa of the Ituri Civil Society Coordination, Malo Dra was killed by unknown assailants in Bule Centre.
“It is with great sadness and regret that the provincial coordination of civil society, Force Vive of Ituri, announces and confirms to the international community the tragic death of one of its active members, the president of the civil society of the Bahema Badjere chiefdom, Désiré Malo Dra, who was cowardly gunned down on February 4, 2026, at around 8:00 p.m. by unidentified armed individuals,” Ezadri stated.
The announcement also noted the abduction of the president of FEC Bule by unidentified assailants, with no communication yet made to his family or professional network.
The civil society coordination urged the security and justice authorities to conduct an independent investigation and called on the international community, including MONUSCO, to assist the Congolese government to ensure a thorough and transparent inquiry.
“The provincial coordination informs the public that funeral arrangements will be announced later. May the soul of our dear colleague rest in peace,” added Ezadri.
Despite the presence of MONUSCO, FARDC, and the UPDF, the security situation in Bule remains fragile, as CRP rebels continue attacks, even though the area is nominally under FARDC control.

title: Woman Raped and Killed by FARDC Soldier, Perpetrator Arrested
excerpt: Lubero February 6, 2026 – North Kivu – A tragic and violent incident occurred in Tembe village, near Bamulumba in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, where a woman was raped and killed on Thursday, February 4, by a soldier of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
title_en: Woman Raped and Killed by FARDC Soldier, Perpetrator Arrested
excerpt_en: Lubero February 6, 2026 – North Kivu – A tragic and violent incident occurred in Tembe village, near Bamulumba in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, where a woman was raped and killed on Thursday, February 4, by a soldier of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_en:
Lubero February 6, 2026 – North Kivu – A tragic and violent incident occurred in Tembe village, near Bamulumba in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, where a woman was raped and killed on Thursday, February 4, by a soldier of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
According to Samuel Kakule Kagheni, president of the Bapere sector civil society, the soldier raped the victim and then decapitated her with a machete while she was locked inside a hut. Shockingly, the act occurred in the presence of the victim’s children.
The administrator of Lubero territory, Colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, confirmed the events and stated that the soldier has been arrested and is currently held at the military prosecutor's office in Mangurejipa, pending trial by the competent military courts.
This incident is part of a series of abuses involving FARDC soldiers in the region since 2025. Previous cases include:
September 8, 2025: A soldier shot and killed his own wife in Kanyatsi.
September 10, 2025: Another FARDC soldier killed a civilian at point-blank range in the village of Lima, approximately six kilometers from Njiapanda, also in Lubero territory.
Authorities and local civil society actors continue to call for accountability and justice to prevent further abuses and restore confidence in security forces.

excerpt_en: Ituri February 7, 2026 – Irumu Territory, Ituri – The security situation in Walese Vonkutu chiefdom remains dire as six civilians were killed in recent attacks attributed to Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels in the village of Pakanza, south of Irumu territory. Local youth fro
body_en:
Ituri February 7, 2026 – Irumu Territory, Ituri – The security situation in Walese Vonkutu chiefdom remains dire as six civilians were killed in recent attacks attributed to Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels in the village of Pakanza, south of Irumu territory.
Local youth from the Bandavilemba group mobilized on Friday to search for missing civilians and discovered the bodies in an advanced state of decomposition.
According to Piscasse Vahingania, first vice-president of the Bwanasura local youth council:
Two of the bodies were recovered and transported to Eringeti for proper burial.
Four bodies were buried on site where they were found.
Mr. Vahingania urged young people to continue cooperating with security forces to help prevent further attacks. He also called on local authorities to strengthen civilian protection and safeguard property, while encouraging the community to maintain hope despite ongoing fear and uncertainty.
The Walese Vonkutu chiefdom continues to be heavily affected by ADF activity, with local communities demanding stronger government action to restore state authority and protect civilians in this part of Ituri.

title: South Africa to Withdraw Troops from MONUSCO
excerpt: February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Sec
title_en: South Africa to Withdraw Troops from MONUSCO
excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Sec
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Secretary-General António Guterres of this decision.
South Africa is among the top ten troop-contributing countries to MONUSCO, with more than 700 soldiers deployed in the DRC under the UN peacekeeping mandate.
In a statement, the Presidency said that during a telephone conversation on January 12, 2026, President Ramaphosa explained that the unilateral withdrawal decision was motivated by the need to consolidate and reorient resources of the South African National Defence Force, after 27 years of supporting UN peacekeeping operations in the DRC.
The Presidency further indicated that South Africa will work with the United Nations to finalize the timeline and modalities of the withdrawal, which is expected to be completed before the end of 2026. President Ramaphosa also welcomed the UN Secretary-General’s appreciation of the decision.
The statement added that the South African government will continue to maintain close bilateral relations with the DRC government and support multilateral peace efforts led by the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union (AU), and the United Nations to achieve lasting peace in the DRC.
In December 2025, the UN Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2808 (2025), extending MONUSCO’s mandate until December 20, 2026, including, on an exceptional basis, its Force Intervention Brigade.
Under this resolution, MONUSCO is authorized to maintain a maximum strength of 11,500 military personnel, 600 military observers and staff officers, 443 police officers, and 1,270 formed police unit members. Its strategic priorities remain:
Protection of civilians in its areas of deployment,
Implementation of the objectives set out in Resolution 2773 (2025), and
Stabilization and strengthening of state institutions in the DRC.
The Council also authorized MONUSCO to support the implementation of a permanent ceasefire in line with Resolution 2773 (2025). France, the penholder of the resolution, said it aims to place MONUSCO “on the front line of support for peace efforts,” including those of the African Union, Togo’s mediation, sub-regional organizations, as well as the United States and Qatar.

title: EU Calls for Rwandan Troop Withdrawal, End to Support for M23, and Neutralization of FDLR by DRC
excerpt: February 8, 2026 – The European Union’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, Johan Borgstam, has completed his third mission to Angola, where he met with the country’s highest authorities to discuss the security situation in eastern DRC and regional efforts toward a
title_en: EU Calls for Rwandan Troop Withdrawal, End to Support for M23, and Neutralization of FDLR by DRC
excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – The European Union’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, Johan Borgstam, has completed his third mission to Angola, where he met with the country’s highest authorities to discuss the security situation in eastern DRC and regional efforts toward a
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – The European Union’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, Johan Borgstam, has completed his third mission to Angola, where he met with the country’s highest authorities to discuss the security situation in eastern DRC and regional efforts toward a political solution to the conflict.
According to a statement from the EU delegation in Luanda, Mr. Borgstam held talks with Angolan President João Lourenço, as well as the Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Defense, and Transport. Discussions focused on Angola’s role in advancing lasting peace in the Great Lakes region and its commitment to an inclusive political dialogue in the DRC.
The European Union reiterated its call for immediate de-escalation in eastern DRC, an effective and lasting ceasefire, and an end to all support for armed groups. Brussels also stressed the need to implement commitments under UN Security Council Resolution 2773, the Washington Agreements, and the Doha Framework, including:
Respect for the territorial integrity of the DRC,
Withdrawal of Rwandan troops from Congolese territory,
An end to support for the M23, and
The neutralization of the FDLR.
During the mission, Mr. Borgstam also chaired the EU delegation at the inaugural coordination meeting for the Lobito Corridor, held on February 5 in Luanda at the request of the governments of Angola, the DRC, and Zambia. The meeting brought together political leaders and international partners to strengthen coordination around this strategic infrastructure project.
Considered a flagship project of the EU’s “Global Gateway” strategy, the Lobito Corridor aims to connect landlocked regions of Angola, the DRC, and Zambia through an open-access transcontinental railway anchored at the Port of Lobito. The EU says investments mobilized under the “Team Europe” initiative for this corridor exceed €2 billion.
Following the meeting, Johan Borgstam welcomed progress in regional and international coordination, highlighting the corridor’s economic and social potential, including its capacity to attract private investment, create jobs, and boost regional trade.

During the mission, Mr. Borgstam also chaired the EU delegation at the inaugural coordination meeting for the Lobito Corridor, held on February 5 in Luanda at the request of the governments of Angola, the DRC, and Zambia. The meeting brought together political leaders and international partners to strengthen coordination around this strategic infrastructure project.
Considered a flagship project of the EU’s “Global Gateway” strategy, the Lobito Corridor aims to connect landlocked regions of Angola, the DRC, and Zambia through an open-access transcontinental railway anchored at the Port of Lobito. The EU says investments mobilized under the “Team Europe” initiative for this corridor exceed €2 billion.
Following the meeting, Johan Borgstam welcomed progress in regional and international coordination, highlighting the corridor’s economic and social potential, including its capacity to attract private investment, create jobs, and boost regional trade.

excerpt: February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at
title_en: AFC/M23 Drone Attack on Kisangani Airport: Investigations Continue and Measures Taken in Response to New Threats (Government)
excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at the African Union City complex, chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa.
In his security briefing, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs, Guy Kabombo, stated that the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are maintaining their positions and ensuring the protection of civilians and property against attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, which have been systematically thwarted.
“This is particularly true of the aerial attacks using kamikaze drones, primarily targeting Bangoka International Airport and other military installations in Kisangani. All the drones launched were destroyed before reaching their targets. Initial findings from the investigation, based on the analysis of recovered debris, indicate the likely country of manufacture, the type of drones used, and the explosive payload carried by each device. However, the investigation is ongoing and appropriate measures are being taken to address any new threats,” the meeting report states.
Regarding South Kivu, the Deputy Prime Minister reported that loyalist forces repelled attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, regaining control of several villages. According to Guy Kabombo, the FARDC are continuing operations to defend national territory in the mid- and high-altitude plateaus of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga.
The drone attack on Kisangani airport, claimed by the AFC/M23, also prompted a strong response from the African Union. Through the Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, the organization firmly condemned the attack on airport infrastructure in a major urban center.
In a statement released on Friday, February 6, the African Union Commission emphasized that such an act, which seriously endangers civilians, constitutes a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution, and warned against the spread of hostilities to cities far from the front lines.
These incidents come months after the ratification of the Washington Accords between Kinshasa and Kigali, yet the situation on the ground remains alarming, marked by ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu. Both sides continue to accuse each other of violating these agreements.
The same applies to the Doha talks, held under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar, which have struggled to produce tangible results. These negotiations, aimed at addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, recently resumed after a prolonged deadlock and resulted in the signing of the terms of reference for the ceasefire verification mechanism between the two parties.
Conclusion
In summary, the period from January 24 to February 8, 2026, reflects a Democratic Republic of Congo at a critical crossroads, defined by a complex interplay of diplomatic hope, persistent conflict, and strategic economic repositioning.
While the government has made significant strides in securing international support—notably through a strategic realignment with Washington regarding critical minerals and the renewal of AGOA trade benefits—the security situation in the East remains dire. The humanitarian crisis continues to escalate, highlighted by the staggering rates of sexual violence and the displacement of thousands due to ongoing clashes with the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 and ADF rebels.
Moving forward, the restoration of peace and territorial integrity will depend on:
Effective implementation of peace accords, such as the Washington and Doha agreements, which currently face significant stagnation.
Strengthening national cohesion through inclusive dialogue and the consolidation of state authority in volatile regions like North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri.
Securing economic sovereignty by ending the illegal plundering of mineral resources and finalizing key infrastructure like the Lobito Corridor and the Banana port.
Ultimately, while the DRC is positioning itself as a central player in the global energy transition, the success of this vision remains tethered to its ability to resolve the persistent cycle of violence and exploitation in its eastern provinces.
By Glad Musema
Jeff Buleli

title: President Félix Tshisekedi in Luanda for Mediation Talks on Eastern DRC
excerpt: Luanda, Angola, February 9, 2026 – President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo is in Luanda as part of ongoing mediation efforts aimed at restoring peace in eastern DRC, a region facing tensions linked to Rwanda. During his visit, President Tshisekedi i

excerpt_en: Luanda, Angola, February 9, 2026 – President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo is in Luanda as part of ongoing mediation efforts aimed at restoring peace in eastern DRC, a region facing tensions linked to Rwanda. During his visit, President Tshisekedi i
body_en:
Luanda, Angola, February 9, 2026 – President Félix-Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo is in Luanda as part of ongoing mediation efforts aimed at restoring peace in eastern DRC, a region facing tensions linked to Rwanda.
During his visit, President Tshisekedi is scheduled to meet with his Angolan counterpart, João Lourenço, who currently serves as Chairperson of the African Union (AU). Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo are also participating in the discussions.
“At the invitation of the President of Angola and current AU Chairperson, João Lourenço, President Tshisekedi is undertaking a working visit to discuss ongoing mediation initiatives aimed at restoring peace to eastern DRC,” said Tina Salama, spokesperson for the Congolese president.
This is President Tshisekedi’s second visit to Luanda in 2026; he previously met with João Lourenço on January 5 to address the security situation in eastern DRC.

title: United Nations Welcomes Angola’s Role in Inclusive National Dialogue in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – The United Nations has welcomed Angola’s willingness to help organize an inclusive national dialogue among the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The announcement was made in Kinshasa by Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Pe
title_en: United Nations Welcomes Angola’s Role in Inclusive National Dialogue in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – The United Nations has welcomed Angola’s willingness to help organize an inclusive national dialogue among the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo. The announcement was made in Kinshasa by Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Pe
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – The United Nations has welcomed Angola’s willingness to help organize an inclusive national dialogue among the people of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The announcement was made in Kinshasa by Jean-Pierre Lacroix, UN Under-Secretary-General for Peacekeeping Operations, following consultations with social and political forces in the DRC and national authorities.
“Regarding dialogue efforts, we noted with great interest Angola’s willingness to support the organization of an inclusive dialogue. Many political groups have high expectations, and the contribution of a third party, such as Angola, is essential to achieving this objective,” said Lacroix.
He emphasized that MONUSCO will continue to support all progress, particularly in verifying compliance with the ceasefire.
“The crucial importance is that diplomatic efforts intensify to implement commitments, especially regarding the ceasefire. MONUSCO must remain ready, available, and proactive to support these advances, focusing on efficiency in line with the Security Council mandate,” Lacroix added.

title: DRC Commits to Leveraging Natural Resources for Peace and Development
excerpt: Cape Town, South Africa, February 10, 2026 – At Mining Indaba 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its commitment to using its natural resources to promote peace, stability, and prosperity for its people. During the “DRC Breakfast” conference, held under the th
title_en: DRC Commits to Leveraging Natural Resources for Peace and Development
excerpt_en: Cape Town, South Africa, February 10, 2026 – At Mining Indaba 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its commitment to using its natural resources to promote peace, stability, and prosperity for its people. During the “DRC Breakfast” conference, held under the th
body_en:
Cape Town, South Africa, February 10, 2026 – At Mining Indaba 2026, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its commitment to using its natural resources to promote peace, stability, and prosperity for its people.
During the “DRC Breakfast” conference, held under the theme “Global Value Chains: The Economic Case for Upstream and Downstream Investments in the DRC”, Minister of Mines Louis Watum presented the government’s vision to position the DRC as a major industrial player in the global energy transition.
Watum emphasized the shift from a reliance on raw material exports toward a model focused on:
Local value creation
Development of battery value chains
Industrialization of critical minerals
Integration of artisanal mining within a formal, structured, and sustainable framework
He also highlighted key government priorities, including strengthening legal security, alignment with international ESG standards, improved governance, and a strengthened fight against fraud and illicit activities. The goal is to offer investors a predictable, transparent, and competitive environment.
The DRC aims to become a major mining transformation hub and a strategic partner in global value chains, benefiting investors, local communities, and the nation.
The event brought together parliamentarians, diplomats, investors, and mining sector partners, along with the Minister of Mines, to discuss the country’s path toward sustainable industrial growth.

title: “Congo First” Advocates for International Criminal Tribunal to Address Decades of Crimes in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 12, 2026 – The political platform “Congo First” (Le Congo d’Abord) has called for the establishment of an International Criminal Tribunal in the DRC to ensure that perpetrators of unlawful acts are held accountable. During the official presentation of the polit
title_en: “Congo First” Advocates for International Criminal Tribunal to Address Decades of Crimes in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 12, 2026 – The political platform “Congo First” (Le Congo d’Abord) has called for the establishment of an International Criminal Tribunal in the DRC to ensure that perpetrators of unlawful acts are held accountable. During the official presentation of the polit
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 12, 2026 – The political platform “Congo First” (Le Congo d’Abord) has called for the establishment of an International Criminal Tribunal in the DRC to ensure that perpetrators of unlawful acts are held accountable.
During the official presentation of the political group on Thursday, coordinator Toussaint Alonga emphasized the need to try those responsible for crimes committed over the past 30 years in the country.
The platform aims to promote values such as goodness, truth, justice, and good governance, while encouraging the exchange of ideas and empowering proposals for the development of the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Alonga noted that the tribunal would help end the cycle of violence that has characterized the DRC’s political life, including elections, disputes, rebellions, dialogues, and governments of national unity.
He further stated that the Head of State’s openness to inclusive dialogue continues existing peace efforts, aiming to reach a consensus on governance reforms, restore national cohesion, and strengthen national unity.
“National cohesion and national unity secure the strategic partnership between the DRC and the USA. Inclusive dialogue, being an extra-constitutional political process, can only be achieved through consensus among actors to reach a lasting solution,” Alonga added.

title: DRC Government Acts Against MTN Rwanda for Illegal Use of Frequencies
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has instructed the DRC government to take immediate technical action against MTN Rwanda for its illegal use of Congolese frequencies. The decision follows a meeting with Minister of Posts and Telecommunications Jo
title_en: DRC Government Acts Against MTN Rwanda for Illegal Use of Frequencies
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has instructed the DRC government to take immediate technical action against MTN Rwanda for its illegal use of Congolese frequencies. The decision follows a meeting with Minister of Posts and Telecommunications Jo
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has instructed the DRC government to take immediate technical action against MTN Rwanda for its illegal use of Congolese frequencies.
The decision follows a meeting with Minister of Posts and Telecommunications José Mpanda Kabangu, the President of the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (ARPTC), and representatives from major mobile operators in the DRC, including Airtel, Orange, and Vodacom.
The discussions focused on MTN Rwanda’s unauthorized occupation of national frequencies, which Minister Mpanda described as a strategic and sovereign issue. The Prime Minister instructed the ARPTC to take the lead in technical communications regarding the matter, with political bodies to intervene once the technical aspects are clarified.
“The issue remains technical. Technical communication will be conducted, and political bodies will come afterward. The Prime Minister has given precise instructions for ARPTC experts to communicate and contact international bodies,” stated José Mpanda.
The DRC intends to defend its frequencies and prevent any malicious foreign intrusion, a concern heightened by the ongoing M23/AFC rebellion in eastern DRC, which reportedly receives support from Rwanda.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, February 11, 2026 – Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has instructed the DRC government to take immediate technical action against MTN Rwanda for its illegal use of Congolese frequencies.
The decision follows a meeting with Minister of Posts and Telecommunications José Mpanda Kabangu, the President of the Postal and Telecommunications Regulatory Authority (ARPTC), and representatives from major mobile operators in the DRC, including Airtel, Orange, and Vodacom.
The discussions focused on MTN Rwanda’s unauthorized occupation of national frequencies, which Minister Mpanda described as a strategic and sovereign issue. The Prime Minister instructed the ARPTC to take the lead in technical communications regarding the matter, with political bodies to intervene once the technical aspects are clarified.
“The issue remains technical. Technical communication will be conducted, and political bodies will come afterward. The Prime Minister has given precise instructions for ARPTC experts to communicate and contact international bodies,” stated José Mpanda.
The DRC intends to defend its frequencies and prevent any malicious foreign intrusion, a concern heightened by the ongoing M23/AFC rebellion in eastern DRC, which reportedly receives support from Rwanda.

title: European Union Allocates €81 Million in Humanitarian Aid for Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The funding aims to assist displaced commu
title_en: European Union Allocates €81 Million in Humanitarian Aid for Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The funding aims to assist displaced commu
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The funding aims to assist displaced communities, address resource scarcity, and provide essential services to Congolese refugees in neighboring countries and fragile communities in Burundi.
The announcement coincides with a visit to the region by European Commissioner for Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, who is assessing urgent humanitarian needs on the ground.
“The objective is to secure the opening of safe corridors to provide relief to hundreds of thousands of people, including those in areas controlled by armed groups,” Lahbib said, emphasizing the need for safe humanitarian access.
The conflict in eastern DRC has resulted in severe shortages of food and water, inadequate shelter, and increased vulnerability of women and children to violence and exploitation.
Commissioner Lahbib’s visit itinerary includes:
Kinshasa, DRC – initial assessments and meetings with key stakeholders
Burundi (February 18–19) – including a planned visit to the Busuma refugee camp, where conditions are particularly dire, with insufficient water, food, and shelter
Kigali, Rwanda (February 20) – to conclude the regional mission
The EU’s intervention underscores the importance of coordinated humanitarian efforts in response to the ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region.

title: DRC and Four African Countries Plan One-Stop Border Crossings to Boost Intra-African Trade
excerpt: Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays. The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, at
title_en: DRC and Four African Countries Plan One-Stop Border Crossings to Boost Intra-African Trade
excerpt_en: Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays. The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, at
body_en:
Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays.
The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, attended by the foreign trade ministers of the five countries, representatives from DP World, and the Secretary-General of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Wamkele Mene.
According to Congolese Minister Julien Paluku Kahongya, the initiative, launched during the 39th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, will lower transport costs and make products more competitive.
“Following the Addis Ababa meeting, we are continuing discussions here in Dubai with our counterparts from Mozambique, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Botswana, along with AfCFTA and DP World, on the construction of one-stop border crossings to streamline trade and eliminate long vehicle queues at our borders,” said Minister Paluku.
AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene highlighted that the initiative supports the effective implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area, aiming to further promote intra-African trade. The meeting also addressed the financing model for these border infrastructures.

title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Appoints New Directors to RVA, ARE, SOKIMO, and Gécamines
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – President Félix Tshisekedi appointed several directors to lead key public enterprises through a series of presidential decrees read on national television (RTNC). Kinkey Mulumba at RVA Blaise Londole and Vincent Futa were appointed Director General a
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – President Félix Tshisekedi appointed several directors to lead key public enterprises through a series of presidential decrees read on national television (RTNC).
Kinkey Mulumba at RVA
Blaise Londole and Vincent Futa were appointed Director General and Deputy Director General, respectively, of the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA). Tryphon Kinkey Mulumba was reappointed as Chairman of the Board of Directors. Londole succeeds Ngoma Mbaki, suspended by the Minister of State Enterprises following a malfunction at N’djili International Airport.
Jean-Marie Beya at ARE
At the Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE), Jean-Marie Beya was named Chairman of the Board of Directors, while Soraya Aziz becomes Managing Director, assisted by Marco Nkuyu as Deputy Managing Director.
Deogratias Ngele Masudi at Gécamines
In the mining sector, Baraka Kabemba was appointed Managing Director of Gécamines, and Deogratias Ngele Masudi becomes Chairman of the Board of Directors of the state-owned mining company.
François Kakese at SOKIMO
A new Management Committee was also appointed to lead the Kilomoto Mining Company (SOKIMO SA). François Kakese Kimaza, formerly Quality and Performance Manager in the Office of the Head of State, becomes Chairman of the Board of Directors, while Yanick Nzonde Mulundu is named Managing Director, succeeding Pistis Bonongo, and Placide Nkala Basadilwa becomes Deputy General Manager (DGA).
These appointments signal a renewed leadership across critical transport, energy, and mining sectors in the DRC.

title: IMF Reports DRC Structural Reforms Met but Remain Fragile
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF). The report not
title_en: IMF Reports DRC Structural Reforms Met but Remain Fragile
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF). The report not
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF).
The report notes that the majority of structural benchmarks were met on schedule, with seven out of eight benchmarks achieved on time, and the remaining one completed with a slight delay. Additionally, three ongoing benchmarks were also fulfilled.
Key advances highlighted by the IMF include:
Strengthening the expenditure chain
Progressive decentralization of budget allocation
Implementation of instruments to improve monetary policy transmission
Enhanced revenue forecasting from the extractive sector
However, the IMF notes persistent institutional weaknesses and legislative delays, particularly regarding the standardized VAT invoicing system, which was not fully adopted by the planned date despite significant progress.
The report warns that while administrative and executive decisions have accelerated reform, this reliance creates institutional fragility in the absence of a stronger legislative framework. It emphasizes the need to:
Sustainably strengthen public financial management
Limit emergency procedures
Improve control and traceability of public expenditures
The IMF concludes that progress on structural reforms is real and significant, supporting the credibility of the program, but stresses that reforms must be consolidated institutionally to ensure long-term sustainability.

title: DRC-US Strategic Partnership Enters Implementation Phase
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries. Key Developments
title_en: DRC-US Strategic Partnership Enters Implementation Phase
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries. Key Developments
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries.
Key Developments
The Committee reviewed the initial Strategic Asset Reserve submitted by the Congolese side, which will guide American private sector investments in the DRC. Projects supported by the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) are prioritized, and American technical teams will be deployed on the ground to identify areas for specific financial and technical support.
The meeting formally activates the Joint Steering Committee as the central body for implementing the agreement, with a defined timetable and regular sessions.
Political Implications
The partnership is now moving from declarative commitments to a structured, institutional mechanism. The Committee serves as a permanent coordination forum, involving several Congolese ministries and U.S. agencies, reducing dependence on short-term political dynamics and creating a stable framework for collaboration.
Economic Implications
Economically, the focus has shifted from general promotion to presenting specific, bankable assets and projects. The inclusion of technical assistance on the ground and project review mechanisms ensures a move from a logic of intention to a logic of execution. Projects that fail to generate interest are re-evaluated after 18 months, reflecting a pragmatic, market-oriented approach.
Governance of Strategic Sectors
The partnership introduces regular dialogue mechanisms on sensitive economic issues, including cobalt export quotas. Congolese authorities are required to provide periodic briefings to the U.S. Embassy, strengthening transparency, accountability, and internal coordination.
A joint committee for the Grand Inga hydroelectric project highlights the strategic importance of this long-term infrastructure initiative and sets a framework for financial and institutional structuring.
Next Steps
The real impact of the partnership will depend on the ability of Congolese institutions to:
Speak with one voice
Propose bankable projects
Translate joint recommendations into actionable regulatory and fiscal decisions
While this initial meeting does not immediately transform the Congolese economic landscape, it establishes a technical, implementation-focused framework that underpins the future strategic collaboration between the DRC and the United States.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rank among the worst-performing countries globally in terms of perceived corruption, according to the 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International. With a score of
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rank among the worst-performing countries globally in terms of perceived corruption, according to the 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International.
With a score of 20 out of 100, the DRC remains at the bottom of the global ranking, reflecting persistent challenges in governance and public accountability. Sub-Saharan Africa, as a region, also performs poorly, with a regional average of 32 points. Only four of the 49 countries assessed scored above 50.
Transparency International notes that, since 2012, ten countries in the region have seen significant deterioration in corruption perception, while only seven improved, illustrating the ineffectiveness of anti-corruption efforts. The DRC remains stagnant, with no notable improvement in recent years.
The NGO highlights the human impact of corruption, stating that it hinders access to essential services and affects the most vulnerable populations the hardest. It calls on governments to implement strong measures to fight corruption and strengthen democratic governance.
Regional comparisons include:
Angola, score 32, improved 17 points since 2015 but still ranks low
Mozambique, lost 10 points over the past decade
Seychelles, top regional performer with 68 points, facing judicial delays in a money laundering case
Lowest scores: Sudan (14), Eritrea (13), Somalia (9), South Sudan (9)
“Corruption in the public sector always hits the most vulnerable people the hardest,” said Paul Banoba, Regional Advisor for Africa at Transparency International. He urged African governments to translate commitments into decisive action, including strengthening oversight institutions, enhancing transparency, and protecting civic space.

title_en: DRC Records First Legal Gold Exports from Haut-Katanga, Targets 15 Tons by 2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has officially exported its first legal artisanal gold from Haut-Katanga, following the opening of a provincial branch of DRC Gold Trading S.A.A. in Lubumbashi. In just a few days, over 20 kilograms of gold were
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has officially exported its first legal artisanal gold from Haut-Katanga, following the opening of a provincial branch of DRC Gold Trading S.A.A. in Lubumbashi.
In just a few days, over 20 kilograms of gold were collected, traced, and exported—a historic first for a region traditionally known for copper and cobalt, where no artisanal gold had previously been legally exported.
The government has also expanded its presence in Haut-Uele, opening another DRC Gold Trading S.A.A. office in Durba to improve production traceability and bring administrative support closer to artisanal miners.
Authorities emphasize that this effort aims to formalize the gold sector, replacing the informal market with official channels to strengthen transparency and economic sovereignty.
Nationally, over 10 tons of gold have been exported in the past three years, generating $1.5 billion in revenue—compared to just 25 kilograms over the previous thirty years. The target for 2026 is 15 tons of exports, with expected revenue exceeding $2.6 billion.
Joseph Kazibazib Mahombi, CEO of DRC Gold Trading S.A.A., confirmed that the expansion will continue with new facilities in Mbuji-Mayi and Kinshasa, contingent on security and banking system support.
Currently, DRC Gold Trading S.A.A. operates approximately ten facilities nationwide, securing transactions and providing assurance to cooperatives and artisanal gold miners.

excerpt: Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Mercuria Energy Trading SA, a Swiss commodity trading company, has completed its first copper and cobalt transaction with the Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC), marking a significant step for the DRC’s strategic metals sector. This operation follow
title_en: Mercuria Purchases First Copper and Cobalt Lot from EGC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Mercuria Energy Trading SA, a Swiss commodity trading company, has completed its first copper and cobalt transaction with the Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC), marking a significant step for the DRC’s strategic metals sector. This operation follow
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Mercuria Energy Trading SA, a Swiss commodity trading company, has completed its first copper and cobalt transaction with the Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC), marking a significant step for the DRC’s strategic metals sector.
This operation follows the implementation of a cobalt export quota system in the Democratic Republic of Congo, established by the Regulatory and Control Authority for the Strategic Mineral Substances Market (ARECOMS) in 2025.
The transaction adheres to EGC’s supply chain management standards and emphasizes responsible practices in the artisanal and small-scale mining sector.
According to the press release, the copper cathodes are destined for markets in the United States, United Arab Emirates, and Saudi Arabia.
This first export of copper and cobalt strengthens the DRC’s position as a key player in the global critical metals market. It also builds on the creation of a joint venture between Gécamines and Mercuria announced in 2025.

title: EGC and Trafigura Launch First Copper and Cobalt Shipment via Lobito Atlantic Railway
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Trafigura announced their first shipment of copper and cobalt to international markets through the Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), marking a major step in creating a fast, efficient, and traceable mining supply
title_en: EGC and Trafigura Launch First Copper and Cobalt Shipment via Lobito Atlantic Railway
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Trafigura announced their first shipment of copper and cobalt to international markets through the Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), marking a major step in creating a fast, efficient, and traceable mining supply
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 13, 2026 – Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Trafigura announced their first shipment of copper and cobalt to international markets through the Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR), marking a major step in creating a fast, efficient, and traceable mining supply chain from the DRC.
The rail corridor, spanning 1,300 kilometers from the deep-water port of Lobito in Angola to the Congolese border at Luau, with an additional 450 kilometers to Kolwezi in the Copperbelt, is now the shortest route from Kolwezi to an African port, reducing inland transit time to approximately seven days.
Eric Kalala, CEO of EGC, said the shipment reflects progress toward an ethical, traceable, and transparent supply of large-scale artisanal cobalt and copper, facilitated by ARECOMS and the Congolese Ministry of Mines. “The copper shipment is initially destined for the United States, reflecting the strategic partnership between the DRC and the U.S., supported by Gécamines and FOMIN,” he added.
Franck Rogozin, Trafigura’s Head of Metals and Minerals in Africa, emphasized that the partnership strengthens the resilience of the global supply of critical metals. “This collaboration facilitates the responsible transport of copper and cobalt to global markets via the most efficient route, highlighting the importance of strong producer-trader partnerships,” he stated.
Nicholas Fournier, CEO of LAR, described the railway as a regional asset and a catalyst for positioning Angola and the DRC as key suppliers of metals and minerals vital for decarbonization, digitalization, and industrialization.
Owned by Trafigura, Mota-Engil, and Vecturis, LAR recently secured $753 million in financing from the International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) and the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA) for rehabilitation and expansion of the network.
Under existing agreements, Trafigura handles the marketing of cobalt supplied by EGC, which purchases minerals from artisanal producers across the DRC.
About the partners:
Trafigura: A leading employee-owned commodities group operating in over 150 countries, with 14,500 employees. Its portfolio spans metals, minerals, oil, gas, electricity, and renewable energy projects.
EGC: A subsidiary of Gécamines, established in 2019, with an exclusive mandate to purchase, process, and market strategic minerals like cobalt, coltan, and germanium from artisanal mining.
Lobito Atlantic Railway (LAR): Operates a 1,300 km line connecting Lobito port to Luau, plus a 450 km section to Kolwezi, under a 30-year concession. It collaborates with the DRC’s SNCC to modernize and operate the railway section within the DRC.
This milestone positions the DRC as a strategic supplier of critical metals, reinforcing ethical mining standards and enhancing regional export infrastructure.

title: IMF Warns of Rising Public Wage Bill as Major Fiscal Risk in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 15, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has identified the public wage bill as a major fiscal risk for the Democratic Republic of Congo under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program. According to the IMF’s second review, rapidly increasing salaries
title_en: IMF Warns of Rising Public Wage Bill as Major Fiscal Risk in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 15, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has identified the public wage bill as a major fiscal risk for the Democratic Republic of Congo under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program. According to the IMF’s second review, rapidly increasing salaries
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 15, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has identified the public wage bill as a major fiscal risk for the Democratic Republic of Congo under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF) program.
According to the IMF’s second review, rapidly increasing salaries in the education, health, and justice sectors are straining budget execution and reducing available fiscal space, particularly in a context already burdened by security expenditures.
The report highlights that the growth of the wage bill stems from salary adjustments, recruitment, administrative regularization, and the continuation of previously undertaken commitments by authorities. This increase has placed pressure on current expenditures in 2024–2025, exceeding initially projected levels.
The IMF warns that the public wage bill is consuming a growing share of budgetary resources, limiting the government’s capacity to fund public investment and social spending, which are priorities under the program. Rising security expenditures further exacerbate this fiscal strain.
For 2025 and 2026, the IMF notes that the widening deficit is partly explained by increased compensation in social and judicial sectors. The fund underscores that this trend, coupled with limited revenue mobilization, heightens the risk of reduced macro-budgetary flexibility.
The IMF calls on the Congolese authorities to:
Contain the growth of the public sector wage bill.
Develop and implement a coherent wage policy.
Strengthen control over civil service size.
Integrate these measures into broader public financial management reforms.
While the IMF did not provide specific timelines or instruments for these reforms, it emphasized that controlling the wage bill is critical for the credibility of the medium-term program and the pursuit of stabilization and development objectives.
Without corrective action, the rigidity of current expenditures could further reduce fiscal space, complicating efforts to maintain macroeconomic stability and support growth.

title: OCC Director General Suspended Over Alleged Fraudulent Import-Export System
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The Director General of the Congolese Office of Control (OCC), Étienne Tshimanga Mutombo, has been suspended from his duties by the Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku, following allegations of serious mismanagement. The suspension, decreed on F
title_en: OCC Director General Suspended Over Alleged Fraudulent Import-Export System
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The Director General of the Congolese Office of Control (OCC), Étienne Tshimanga Mutombo, has been suspended from his duties by the Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku, following allegations of serious mismanagement. The suspension, decreed on F
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The Director General of the Congolese Office of Control (OCC), Étienne Tshimanga Mutombo, has been suspended from his duties by the Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku, following allegations of serious mismanagement.
The suspension, decreed on February 16, 2026, aims to protect the institution from further administrative and technical misconduct.
Allegations against Mutombo include:
Installing a parallel computer system for import and export control, reportedly facilitating the use of fraudulent Verification Certificates (VCs).
Mismanagement of human and financial resources.
Acts of insubordination.
These irregularities are said to have caused significant financial losses, estimated at thousands of US dollars.
A reform commission for the OCC has been established, with its composition and mission to be defined by a separate ministerial decree. The Deputy Director General, Christelle Muabilu, has been appointed interim director during the investigation.
According to the Minister’s office, disciplinary proceedings against Mutombo had begun in late January, and his responses were deemed unsatisfactory, prompting the suspension. Additional administrative and extra-administrative measures will target any OCC agents complicit in the alleged acts.

A reform commission for the OCC has been established, with its composition and mission to be defined by a separate ministerial decree. The Deputy Director General, Christelle Muabilu, has been appointed interim director during the investigation.
According to the Minister’s office, disciplinary proceedings against Mutombo had begun in late January, and his responses were deemed unsatisfactory, prompting the suspension. Additional administrative and extra-administrative measures will target any OCC agents complicit in the alleged acts.

title: Washington Approves New DFC Investments in Africa to Secure Critical Minerals and Energy
excerpt: February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations. According to DFC Managin
title_en: Washington Approves New DFC Investments in Africa to Secure Critical Minerals and Energy
excerpt_en: February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations. According to DFC Managin
body_en:
February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations.
According to DFC Managing Director Ben Black, these investments are designed to support economic development, enhance energy resilience, and consolidate supply chains essential to U.S. growth, security, and innovation.
While the specific transactions remain confidential, they are part of a broader U.S. effort to expand strategic influence in Africa. All projects will undergo further steps, including Congressional notification, prior to final commitment and closing.
The approval follows a recent expansion of the DFC’s authority by the U.S. Congress, which:
Removed geographic restrictions in strategic sectors.
Raised the agency’s investment ceiling to $205 billion.
Strengthened equity financing capabilities and created a new revolving investment fund.
In mid-February, the United States and the African Union Commission launched a strategic working group on infrastructure and investment, tasked with translating strategic priorities into fundable projects. A cross-border pilot project has been proposed as a proof of concept, with the Democratic Republic of Congo explicitly mentioned, potentially within a regional economic integration framework with Rwanda.
Targeted sectors include infrastructure and critical mineral supply chains, with an emphasis on commercial viability and alignment with Agenda 2063. The U.S. plans to leverage financial instruments such as the DFC, U.S. Export-Import Bank (EXIM), and multilateral banks, while supporting regulatory reforms and legal harmonization to mitigate risks.
The DFC board meeting included both public and private sector members, and a public hearing was held to gather stakeholder input on the agency’s activities.
Social and Health

title_en: DRC Investigates Alleged Biometric Passport Price Hikes in Beni
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 – The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has dispatched a team to Beni, in North Kivu, to investigate reports of an illegal increase in the price of biometric passports. While the official fee is set at USD 75, some applicants claim to have paid up to USD 125 at the mo
body_en:
February 12, 2026 – The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has dispatched a team to Beni, in North Kivu, to investigate reports of an illegal increase in the price of biometric passports.
While the official fee is set at USD 75, some applicants claim to have paid up to USD 125 at the mobile data capture centers established in Beni and Butembo in October 2025.
Leading the mission, Teddy Kamembo Milambo, the Ministry’s Director of Legal Affairs and Litigation, urged citizens not to use intermediaries.
“If the allegations are true, it is up to the higher authorities to take the toughest possible action. The authorities' objective in setting the official price was to ease the difficulties faced by the population,” he said.
He emphasized that the official fee remains USD 75 and instructed citizens to submit applications directly, without intermediaries. “Those with old passports should continue to use them. No country rejects these documents,” he added.

title: DRC Plans Stricter Regulation of Gambling Sector
excerpt: February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from g
title_en: DRC Plans Stricter Regulation of Gambling Sector
excerpt_en: February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from g
body_en:
February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from gambling activities, while strengthening state control over a sector that generates significant financial resources, much of which currently escapes the public treasury.
According to Deputy Mishiki, who represents Walikale (North Kivu), this initiative aligns with the DRC’s strategic partnership commitments with the United States, particularly regarding the fight against money laundering and financing of terrorism.
“Our legislation no longer allows the Congolese state to effectively control this sector,” he said. He also highlighted social concerns: gambling addiction is impacting impoverished communities, further deepening poverty.
The bill includes a 5% tax on gambling revenue and proposes reforms to the National Lottery Society, modeled after the Canadian Lottery, which finances over 60% of social housing. Deputy Mishiki claims that, if implemented, the law could allow the state to recover nearly two billion dollars and strengthen the financial system.

title_en: Eight Missing After Kalelu Ferry Accident Between Lomami and Kasai-Oriental
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – At least eight people are missing following an incident on the Kalelu ferry, which links the Bakua Mulumba chiefdom (Lomami province) to the Bakua Kalonji chiefdom (Kasai-Oriental province). The accident occurred Friday morning during the transport of a vehicl
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – At least eight people are missing following an incident on the Kalelu ferry, which links the Bakua Mulumba chiefdom (Lomami province) to the Bakua Kalonji chiefdom (Kasai-Oriental province).
The accident occurred Friday morning during the transport of a vehicle on the ferry. According to eyewitnesses, around twelve people were in the vehicle.
As the ferry approached the shore and disembarkation began, the vehicle driver started the engine and suddenly put it in reverse, causing the vehicle to strike the ferry’s edge and plunge into the river.
Four passengers, including the driver, were rescued, while eight others remain missing. Search operations are ongoing to locate the victims.
Authorities are investigating the incident to determine the cause of the accident and assess safety measures on the ferry.

excerpt: February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses. Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate
title_en: Mobile Phone Services Restored After Month-Long Outage in North and South Kivu
excerpt_en: February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses. Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate
body_en:
February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses.
Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate again in Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, and Walikale in North Kivu. The signal was restored around 11 p.m. on Monday.
Residents reported that during the outage, making calls, sending messages, and accessing the internet had been extremely difficult, forcing some to travel several kilometers to reach minimal coverage areas. “The restoration allows us to resume communication, improves information flow, and even facilitates mobile payments for teachers and healthcare workers in rural areas,” one resident explained.
The communications blackout also had broader consequences, including disrupted commercial activities, challenges for Virunga National Park conservation operations, and difficulties for humanitarian and health workers in monitoring and responding to emergencies.
While no official statement has confirmed the cause, a Vodacom technician in Walikale reported that the disruption originated in Kinshasa, where heavy rains damaged satellite link devices in Maluku, causing cascading outages in multiple provinces.
