title: Grace Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, Released After First Hearing Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt: February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
title_en: Grace Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, Released After First Hearing Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt_en: February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
body_en:
February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
The hearing focused on a report by the General Inspectorate of Finance (IGF), which audited Bilolo's administration in 2025. According to his defense lawyers, Bilolo presented his arguments and stated that no alarming irregularities had been found relative to prior media reports.
Espoir Siasi, legal advisor to the governor, said: “We remain at the disposal of the justice system, but everything has been done. The governor was released and has returned home. Any further charges will be communicated by the prosecutor if necessary.”
The IGF report revealed multiple alleged irregularities, including:
Non-payment of provincial tax and duty revenues amounting to 24,928,597 Congolese francs.
Misappropriation of USD 137,417.04 transferred improperly to the Provincial Assembly.
USD 440,889 used for vehicle acquisition for provincial deputies.
USD 35,183 not allocated to public works.
USD 423,720 owed to Decentralized Territorial Entities (ETD) of Muanda, which remained unpaid.
The Attorney General, Firmin Mvonde, classified these acts as embezzlement of public funds, punishable under Article 145 of the Penal Code (Book II). The governor was invited to present his version regarding the seriousness of these allegations.

title: Judicial Police Officer Sentenced to Death for Murder
excerpt: February 10, 2026 – The Goma Garrison Military Court, sitting in Walikale, North Kivu, sentenced Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre, a judicial police officer assigned to the Mubi Judicial Inspectorate, to death on Monday, February 9, after being found guilty of murder. The incident occ
title_en: Judicial Police Officer Sentenced to Death for Murder
excerpt_en: February 10, 2026 – The Goma Garrison Military Court, sitting in Walikale, North Kivu, sentenced Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre, a judicial police officer assigned to the Mubi Judicial Inspectorate, to death on Monday, February 9, after being found guilty of murder. The incident occ
body_en:
February 10, 2026 – The Goma Garrison Military Court, sitting in Walikale, North Kivu, sentenced Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre, a judicial police officer assigned to the Mubi Judicial Inspectorate, to death on Monday, February 9, after being found guilty of murder.
The incident occurred early on Saturday, January 31, in Mubi Centre, Walikale territory. Two judicial police officers were executing an arrest warrant for Kambale Muhindo Jean, a suspected member of an armed group accused of illegal possession of weapons.
According to the investigation, when the suspect attempted to evade arrest, Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre fired his weapon without orders, fatally shooting the victim.
The military court not only sentenced him to death but also ordered payment of USD 10,000 in damages (equivalent in Congolese francs) to the victim’s family.
The prosecution described the verdict as “educational,” emphasizing that it sends a strong message against abuses by law enforcement officers.
Major Dieudonné Kasereka, head of communications for the 34th Military Region, highlighted that the ruling reinforces the obligation for security forces to respect rules of engagement and human rights, even during law enforcement operations.

title: Justice at a Standstill in Bulungu – 93 Detainees, Only 25 Convicted
excerpt: February 12, 2026 – The justice system in Bulungu, Kwilu province, is facing a critical impasse, leaving detainees to die without knowing their fate. Local sources report that at least five detainees have died since January while awaiting trial, due to a severe shortage of magist
title_en: Justice at a Standstill in Bulungu – 93 Detainees, Only 25 Convicted
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 – The justice system in Bulungu, Kwilu province, is facing a critical impasse, leaving detainees to die without knowing their fate. Local sources report that at least five detainees have died since January while awaiting trial, due to a severe shortage of magist
body_en:
February 12, 2026 – The justice system in Bulungu, Kwilu province, is facing a critical impasse, leaving detainees to die without knowing their fate.
Local sources report that at least five detainees have died since January while awaiting trial, due to a severe shortage of magistrates and the closure of the Bulungu High Court since December 15, 2025.
Currently, the central prison houses 93 detainees, of whom only 25 have been convicted. The remaining 68 detainees await hearings that have not taken place, including appeals from five territories across Kwilu Province.
Attorney Dirigeant Munzende, president of the Bulungu civil society organization, condemned the situation as a violation of the right to justice. He explained that the court is functioning with only the presiding judge and a single judge, relying on a legal aid lawyer to fill the panel.
“The last hearings were on December 15, 2025. Since then, no case has been heard, and several detainees have died during proceedings, while others remain in indefinite limbo,” Munzende stated.
The situation highlights the urgent need to reinforce judicial capacity in Kwilu to prevent further deaths and ensure timely access to justice for all detainees.

Currently, the central prison houses 93 detainees, of whom only 25 have been convicted. The remaining 68 detainees await hearings that have not taken place, including appeals from five territories across Kwilu Province.
Attorney Dirigeant Munzende, president of the Bulungu civil society organization, condemned the situation as a violation of the right to justice. He explained that the court is functioning with only the presiding judge and a single judge, relying on a legal aid lawyer to fill the panel.
“The last hearings were on December 15, 2025. Since then, no case has been heard, and several detainees have died during proceedings, while others remain in indefinite limbo,” Munzende stated.
The situation highlights the urgent need to reinforce judicial capacity in Kwilu to prevent further deaths and ensure timely access to justice for all detainees.

title: Kinshasa Military Court to Hear Case of Alleged ANR Abduction and Torture
excerpt: February 20, 2026 – The Kinshasa/Gombe Military Court has scheduled the first hearing in the case between Claudien Likulia, son of former Human Rights Minister Marie-Ange Mushobekwa, and Philémon Mambabwa Zebo, a senior official at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR). The hear

excerpt_en: February 20, 2026 – The Kinshasa/Gombe Military Court has scheduled the first hearing in the case between Claudien Likulia, son of former Human Rights Minister Marie-Ange Mushobekwa, and Philémon Mambabwa Zebo, a senior official at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR). The hear
body_en:
February 20, 2026 – The Kinshasa/Gombe Military Court has scheduled the first hearing in the case between Claudien Likulia, son of former Human Rights Minister Marie-Ange Mushobekwa, and Philémon Mambabwa Zebo, a senior official at the National Intelligence Agency (ANR). The hearing is set for Thursday, February 26, at the court’s premises on 46 Lubefu Avenue, Gombe, Kinshasa.
Marie-Ange Mushobekwa alleges that on December 21, 2025, her two minor children, Claudien (18) and Christopher Likulia (17), along with a 17-year-old friend, were abducted, tied up, beaten, and tortured at the private residence of the ANR official. She claims the attack was carried out by seven police officers and soldiers acting on Mambabwa’s orders.
Describing the incident as “arbitrary, brutal, and disproportionate”, Mushobekwa emphasized that her children were unarmed, not wanted by the police, and present by invitation, yet suffered serious physical and psychological trauma, including visible bruises, difficulty sitting, and functional impairment of one hand.
Mushobekwa denounced the incident as an abuse of personal power and a state affair, criticizing the absence of administrative or judicial sanctions nearly three weeks after the event. She called for a fair and impartial trial, stating, “This is not a political matter; it is a moral test for the state,” and urged the authorities to take responsibility.
The upcoming hearing will test the Congolese justice system’s ability to address alleged abuses by state security agents and deliver accountability for serious human rights violations.

title: DRC Trains 2,500 New Magistrates, Emphasizes Integrity and Rule of Law
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed the initial training of 2,500 new magistrates, the second wave of appointees under a presidential decree from March 28, 2025. The training, conducted from November 2025 to February 2026, focused on ethic
title_en: DRC Trains 2,500 New Magistrates, Emphasizes Integrity and Rule of Law
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed the initial training of 2,500 new magistrates, the second wave of appointees under a presidential decree from March 28, 2025. The training, conducted from November 2025 to February 2026, focused on ethic
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo has completed the initial training of 2,500 new magistrates, the second wave of appointees under a presidential decree from March 28, 2025. The training, conducted from November 2025 to February 2026, focused on ethics, professional conduct, and technical competence for both civilian and military magistrates.
Dieudonné Kamuleta Badibanga, President of the High Council of the Judiciary (CSM) and the Constitutional Court, urged the new magistrates to “resist pressure of all kinds, refuse unethical concessions, and remain steadfast in the face of corruption.” He stressed that true greatness is measured by integrity, conscience, and sense of justice, not rank or power.
Kamuleta emphasized that magistrates are servants of the Republic, entrusted with upholding the Constitution and safeguarding fundamental freedoms. He described the robes worn by magistrates as symbols of responsibility, not privilege, reminding them of their duty to the Congolese people.
Minister of Justice Guillaume Ngefa highlighted that this new cohort strengthens the judiciary, ensures adequate numbers for effective law enforcement, and supports the rule of law, judicial reform, and anti-impunity efforts. The program included 86 instructors across 31 modules, conducted in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi (Haut-Katanga).
This latest recruitment brings the total number of magistrates appointed since 2022 to 5,000, addressing a previous shortage of approximately 3,000 magistrates. The initiative aims to improve access to justice for over 100 million Congolese citizens, modernize the judiciary, and enhance ethical and professional standards.

title: UN Peacekeeping Chief Begins Visit for Ceasefire Consultations
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC February 9, 2026 – The Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, begins a three-day official visit to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on Monday, as efforts intensify to implement a ceasefire in the eastern region of the country. Ac
title_en: UN Peacekeeping Chief Begins Visit for Ceasefire Consultations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC February 9, 2026 – The Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, begins a three-day official visit to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on Monday, as efforts intensify to implement a ceasefire in the eastern region of the country. Ac
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC February 9, 2026 – The Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, begins a three-day official visit to the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) on Monday, as efforts intensify to implement a ceasefire in the eastern region of the country.
According to the United Nations (UN), the visit will include consultations with national and provincial authorities, as well as meetings with members of the political class, civil society, and religious organizations. Discussions are expected to focus on the evolving security situation and the progress of the ceasefire process.
In line with UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025), the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo is mandated to support the implementation of a permanent ceasefire. The mission’s support includes technical and logistical assistance to the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region within the framework of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus.
As part of this mechanism, an initial team of peacekeepers is set to deploy to Uvira, in South Kivu, to assist in monitoring the ceasefire. MONUSCO clarified that the deployment does not signal a permanent redeployment to the province, but rather constitutes limited and targeted support strictly confined to the verification framework.
Currently, MONUSCO forces remain deployed in Ituri and North Kivu provinces. The mission officially completed its withdrawal from South Kivu in June 2024, as part of its phased disengagement plan agreed upon with the Congolese government.

title: Despite Ceasefire Calls, AFC/M23 Announces Reinforcement of 7,532 Fighters
excerpt: February 10, 2026 – While diplomatic pressure mounts for a ceasefire in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the AFC/M23 rebellion has announced a significant reinforcement of its military forces, signaling continued tensions on the ground. In a statement released Tuesday, the m
title_en: Despite Ceasefire Calls, AFC/M23 Announces Reinforcement of 7,532 Fighters
excerpt_en: February 10, 2026 – While diplomatic pressure mounts for a ceasefire in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the AFC/M23 rebellion has announced a significant reinforcement of its military forces, signaling continued tensions on the ground. In a statement released Tuesday, the m
body_en:
February 10, 2026 – While diplomatic pressure mounts for a ceasefire in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, the AFC/M23 rebellion has announced a significant reinforcement of its military forces, signaling continued tensions on the ground.
In a statement released Tuesday, the movement confirmed the completion of a training cycle for new recruits within its armed wing, the Congolese Revolutionary Army (ARC). The ceremony reportedly took place in Tshanzu, where, according to the group, 7,532 commandos were officially integrated into its operational units. The figure, however, could not be independently verified.
The AFC/M23, which has been accused by Kinshasa and several international partners of receiving support from Rwanda, said the newly trained fighters would be deployed on missions aimed at securing and defending strategic positions, controlling key axes and operational zones, and maintaining what it described as “tactical superiority.”
The announcement comes at a time when diplomatic initiatives are intensifying. African leaders meeting in Luanda recently urged both the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 to commit to an immediate ceasefire, while the United Nations reiterated that MONUSCO stands ready to support its implementation.
Simultaneously, representatives of the Congolese government and the armed group reaffirmed their commitment to the ceasefire framework agreement signed in November 2025 in Doha, during a session of the monitoring and verification mechanism held under the auspices of Qatar. The meeting brought together delegates from the African Union, the United States, and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region.
Despite these diplomatic engagements, the armed movement maintained a firm tone.
“If the Kinshasa regime wants peace, we are ready; if it chooses war, we are too,” the AFC/M23 declared in its communiqué.
The latest development underscores the fragile nature of ongoing peace efforts, as military posturing continues alongside high-level diplomatic negotiations.

title: New Wave of Mobondo Surrenders, Significant Cache of Weapons Recovered
excerpt: Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province. After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that seve
title_en: New Wave of Mobondo Surrenders, Significant Cache of Weapons Recovered
excerpt_en: Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province. After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that seve
body_en:
Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province.
After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that several Mobondo militiamen have laid down their arms in the villages of Ipongi and Mulosi, as well as near the Kwango Bridge.
Among those who surrendered are fighters affiliated with the group led by militia commander Mouton, described by officials as one of the most resistant factions within the movement. The militiamen reportedly handed themselves over to the defense and security forces, along with what authorities say is a significant quantity of weapons.
Deputy Minister of Defense Eliezer Ntambwe confirmed the development, noting that weapons are still being collected and that a precise inventory will be provided once the operation concludes in Kinshasa.
“Our brothers who were involved in this movement have agreed to lay down their arms. Many have done so. We are currently preparing to travel with them to Kinshasa so that those who choose to join the army can do so, and those who opt for vocational training can also access it. This also falls within our purview. I cannot give you a precise number of weapons, as we are still collecting them along the way. You will have more details once we arrive in Kinshasa,” stated Minister Ntambwe.
According to authorities, the surrendered fighters will be evacuated to Kinshasa, where some may undergo military integration, while others will benefit from vocational training programs as part of the broader disarmament and reintegration process.
Local militia leaders in Ipongi reportedly encouraged remaining fighters to abandon violence and join the peace process, signaling a possible shift within certain factions of the armed group.
Despite this progress, officials stress that the mission remains ongoing. Further security operations are expected in areas where the Mobondo threat persists, as the government seeks to restore stability across affected territories.

title_en: Man Dies in Detention After Alleged Torture by Wazalendo Militiamen in Musimba
excerpt_en: Lubero February 10, 2026 – A man from Kirumba, in Lubero territory, died on Sunday, February 8, while detained in an underground cell allegedly run by Wazalendo militiamen in Musimba, on the southern outskirts of Butembo, in North Kivu. According to local civil society sources in
body_en:
Lubero February 10, 2026 – A man from Kirumba, in Lubero territory, died on Sunday, February 8, while detained in an underground cell allegedly run by Wazalendo militiamen in Musimba, on the southern outskirts of Butembo, in North Kivu.
According to local civil society sources in Musimba, the victim is said to have died after being subjected to torture while held in what residents describe as a clandestine detention facility. The man had initially been accused of rape, arrested, and later granted provisional release by judicial authorities.
However, the decision reportedly triggered opposition from those who had arrested him, who allegedly organized his re-arrest before transferring him to the Wazalendo militia.
He was subsequently taken to an underground cell in Musimba, where he later died. The exact circumstances of his death remain disputed. Leaders of the Wazalendo militia deny allegations of torture, claiming instead that the detainee committed suicide by hanging.
The incident has reignited concerns over human rights abuses attributed to certain local armed groups operating in the region. title: MONUSCO Plans Aerial Reconnaissance Over Uvira Ahead of Gradual Ground Deployment
excerpt: Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees. According
title_en: MONUSCO Plans Aerial Reconnaissance Over Uvira Ahead of Gradual Ground Deployment
excerpt_en: Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees. According
body_en:
Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees.
According to a UN source, the mission intends to launch reconnaissance flights as a first step, to be followed by a limited ground deployment, and eventually a progressive increase in troop presence, subject to recommendations expected before March. Officials stress that “nothing will be done without security guarantees,” a message reportedly conveyed to relevant parties and diplomatic representatives.
Securing Uvira, in South Kivu, is described as a key priority during this initial phase. The operational timeline foresees the reopening of the air route, followed by surveillance flights, and then a possible ground deployment if conditions permit. No official figures have been disclosed regarding the number of personnel to be deployed.
The stated objective of this phase is to support the implementation of the ceasefire, with MONUSCO expected to initiate its verification and observation mandate.
However, the United Nations underscores that it cannot single-handedly guarantee the success of peace efforts. The process also depends on the engagement of the agreement’s guarantors, notably the United States, Qatar, and the African Union.
This phased return would precede the approval of a full operational mandate expected in March, particularly concerning South Kivu. The UN aims to rapidly re-establish its footprint on the ground while preparing recommendations focused on operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

title: Armed Attack in Kavumu Leaves Couple and Child Dead
excerpt: Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu. According to local sources, including rep
title_en: Armed Attack in Kavumu Leaves Couple and Child Dead
excerpt_en: Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu. According to local sources, including rep
body_en:
Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu.
According to local sources, including representatives of civil society in Kabare, the attack took place on the night of Sunday, February 8, at around 9:00 p.m. in the sub-village of Chirhodu, located in the Bugorhe groupement in Kavumu.
The victims were identified as Janvier Ombeni Bagula, his wife, and their young child. The circumstances surrounding the attack remain unclear, and no group has claimed responsibility.
Local civil society actors have strongly condemned the killings and are calling for reinforced security measures in the area. They are also urging residents to cooperate closely with security services to help prevent further violence.
The incident adds to growing concerns over persistent insecurity in parts of South Kivu, where armed attacks against civilians continue to be reported.

title: Death Toll from ADF Attack in Mambimbi-Isigo Rises to 21
excerpt: Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people
title_en: Death Toll from ADF Attack in Mambimbi-Isigo Rises to 21
excerpt_en: Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people
body_en:
Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people still reported missing.
According to Kakule Kagheni Samuel, president of the local civil society in Bapere, six additional bodies were discovered on Monday, bringing the total number of victims to twenty-one. The attack occurred during the night of Friday, February 6, to Saturday, February 7, 2026. Assailants reportedly set fire to homes and destroyed property during the incursion.
Initial reports had confirmed at least fifteen deaths, including two women, along with the burning of several houses. Survivors described scenes of devastation, with one witness stating he was unable to count the number of bodies encountered while fleeing. Civil society had earlier reported a provisional toll of fifteen dead and seven houses burned.
The attack followed several days of reported ADF movements in the area. Residents had raised alerts about the presence of suspected rebels for more than four days prior to the assault. The security situation deteriorated rapidly, triggering mass displacement toward Njiapanda and other localities considered relatively safer.
Local sources indicate that the affected village remained inaccessible until Saturday evening, delaying the burial of victims, as several bodies were still lying at the scene.
The violence extends beyond Lubero. In neighboring Beni territory, six civilians were killed in an ambush on the evening of February 4, 2026, in Malibo, along the Oicha–Mamove road. The attack came just hours after another ambush on the same road that claimed four additional lives. In total, at least ten civilians were killed in one day, with several motorcycles burned during the assaults.
In a report released on February 3, the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination indicated that at least 63 civilians have been killed since the beginning of the year by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero territories. Of these, 52 deaths were recorded in Lubero and 10 in Beni, making Lubero the hardest-hit area.
Beyond the human toll, the attacks have caused extensive material damage, including the burning of a health post, 67 shops, and 10 houses, as well as the destruction of 23 motorcycles and a traditional “barza” used for community meetings.
The repeated violence has forced thousands of families into displacement, leaving them in precarious humanitarian conditions. Ongoing insecurity continues to prevent residents from returning to several localities now classified as high-risk zones, deepening the crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

excerpt: Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone strikes on positions held by the AFC/M23 rebellion in Mindjendje, a village near Mpety, in the Kisimba groupement of Walikale territory, North Kivu. According to local sour

excerpt_en: Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone strikes on positions held by the AFC/M23 rebellion in Mindjendje, a village near Mpety, in the Kisimba groupement of Walikale territory, North Kivu. According to local sour
body_en:
Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone strikes on positions held by the AFC/M23 rebellion in Mindjendje, a village near Mpety, in the Kisimba groupement of Walikale territory, North Kivu.
According to local sources, the strikes were conducted on Sunday and Monday, targeting rebel positions in the area. Several fighters were reportedly wounded and evacuated to the Mweso General Referral Hospital for treatment. Independent sources based in Kalembe have also confirmed the aerial bombardments.
The strikes come amid a renewed escalation of clashes between government forces and the AFC/M23, as fighting intensifies in parts of Walikale. The rebel movement is reportedly reinforcing its positions around Pinga, a locality considered strategically significant in the region.
The latest developments signal a further deterioration of the security situation in North Kivu, where tensions remain high despite ongoing diplomatic efforts aimed at restoring stability.

title: UN’s Jean-Pierre Lacroix Meets CENCO-ECC on Social Pact for Peace
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Con
title_en: UN’s Jean-Pierre Lacroix Meets CENCO-ECC on Social Pact for Peace
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Con
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) to discuss the implementation of the Social Pact for Peace and the broader push for an inclusive national dialogue.
The ECC delegation was led by Pastor Maurice Mondengo, Deputy Chief of Staff to the National President of the ECC in charge of communication, media, and public relations, while CENCO was represented by Father Georges Kalenga, Deputy Secretary-General of the episcopate.
Speaking on the outcomes of the meeting, Pastor Mondengo highlighted discussions on operationalizing commitments from recent diplomatic negotiations in Washington and Doha, which aim to stabilize eastern DRC and promote lasting peace.
“UN Under-Secretary-General Jean-Pierre Lacroix, a man of peace, expressed his satisfaction and encouragement for our social pact initiative for peace and harmonious coexistence to continue its progress. He believes that through this initiative, we will achieve the long-awaited dialogue in Congo, and an inclusive dialogue,” Pastor Mondengo stated.
Although a joint roadmap for the national dialogue initiative has been validated with other religious denominations and the Presidency of the Republic, implementation by the government has been slow. Pastor Mondengo emphasized that rebuilding mutual trust remains crucial for progress.
“The well-being of Congo, the return of peace to Congo, is first and foremost a matter for the Congolese people. It does not necessarily depend on the support of the United Nations. It depends on you and me,” he added.
Following a meeting of African leaders in Luanda on February 9, Angola was tasked with initiating consultations with all relevant Congolese parties to create conditions for a national inter-Congolese dialogue. President Félix Tshisekedi has previously recognized the importance of national dialogue, although certain proposed conditions were rejected by opposition parties.
The opposition continues to demand an inclusive dialogue to foster national cohesion, at a time when M23/AFC rebels, reportedly supported by Rwanda, continue advancing in the east, seizing territories across North Kivu and South Kivu.
The discussions with CENCO and ECC underscore ongoing efforts by religious leaders and the UN to promote peaceful coexistence and create conditions for a comprehensive political dialogue in eastern DRC.

“The well-being of Congo, the return of peace to Congo, is first and foremost a matter for the Congolese people. It does not necessarily depend on the support of the United Nations. It depends on you and me,” he added.
Following a meeting of African leaders in Luanda on February 9, Angola was tasked with initiating consultations with all relevant Congolese parties to create conditions for a national inter-Congolese dialogue. President Félix Tshisekedi has previously recognized the importance of national dialogue, although certain proposed conditions were rejected by opposition parties.
The opposition continues to demand an inclusive dialogue to foster national cohesion, at a time when M23/AFC rebels, reportedly supported by Rwanda, continue advancing in the east, seizing territories across North Kivu and South Kivu.
The discussions with CENCO and ECC underscore ongoing efforts by religious leaders and the UN to promote peaceful coexistence and create conditions for a comprehensive political dialogue in eastern DRC.

title_en: Calm Returns to Kilama After Three Days of Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt_en: Kilama Rutshuru February 11, 2026 – A gradual return to calm has been reported in Kilama, part of the Bambo group in Rutshuru territory, North Kivu, following three days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the Collective of Movements for Change/Peo
body_en:
Kilama Rutshuru February 11, 2026 – A gradual return to calm has been reported in Kilama, part of the Bambo group in Rutshuru territory, North Kivu, following three days of intense clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters of the Collective of Movements for Change/People’s Defense Forces (CMC/FDP).
Local sources indicate that the fighting erupted on February 8, when AFC/M23 forces launched simultaneous attacks on Wazalendo positions in the villages of Mayengo and Bugabo, as well as in areas near Domaine in Kilama.
The assaults reportedly involved the use of kamikaze drones, heavy artillery, and aerial bombardment, followed by attempted ground advances. After several hours of intense combat, Wazalendo forces successfully repelled the rebels on all fronts, according to local reports.
The clashes prompted population movements, as residents sought safety in areas considered more secure. The return of calm comes as authorities and local communities monitor the situation to prevent renewed violence.

title: ADF Attack in Mangadu Claims Five Lives
excerpt: Mangadu Beni February 11, 2026 – Violence continues to escalate in the Beni-Mbau area, as an attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters on Tuesday, February 10, left at least five civilians dead in Mangadu-Upende, located 7 kilometers from Mbau town in Beni territory, Nort
title_en: ADF Attack in Mangadu Claims Five Lives
excerpt_en: Mangadu Beni February 11, 2026 – Violence continues to escalate in the Beni-Mbau area, as an attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters on Tuesday, February 10, left at least five civilians dead in Mangadu-Upende, located 7 kilometers from Mbau town in Beni territory, Nort
body_en:
Mangadu Beni February 11, 2026 – Violence continues to escalate in the Beni-Mbau area, as an attack by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters on Tuesday, February 10, left at least five civilians dead in Mangadu-Upende, located 7 kilometers from Mbau town in Beni territory, North Kivu.
According to Kisaki Luis, president of the local civil society organization in the Batangi Mbau group, the victims’ bodies were recovered early Wednesday morning.
“We found five bodies lying on the ground, four men and one woman. The victims were killed with firearms. Before withdrawing, the attackers placed an explosive device on one of the bodies, which is why we recovered four bodies. There is also one missing person and material damage,” Luis reported.
Civil society actors warn that attacks continue to occur despite prior warnings about ADF movements. Local leaders expressed frustration at what they describe as the inaction of security forces, noting that the armed group has carried out numerous killings since the beginning of the year.
“Right now, the population is moving towards areas considered safe, and we are tired of what is happening. Our armed forces must pursue the assailants to their strongholds. From Otomabere to here, they are carrying out a series of killings, and we don't understand this lethargy on the part of the armed forces,” lamented Kisaki Luis.
The latest attack adds to a rising climate of fear in Beni and surrounding areas, where more than 60 civilians have reportedly been killed since the start of 2026 due to ADF insurgency.

title: Kinshasa and Brazzaville Strengthen Military Cooperation for Joint Border Security
excerpt: February 11, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Congo are consolidating bilateral military cooperation to enhance security along their shared border, as Deputy Prime Minister of National Defense Guy Kabombo visited Brazzaville to meet with Congolese
title_en: Kinshasa and Brazzaville Strengthen Military Cooperation for Joint Border Security
excerpt_en: February 11, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Congo are consolidating bilateral military cooperation to enhance security along their shared border, as Deputy Prime Minister of National Defense Guy Kabombo visited Brazzaville to meet with Congolese
body_en:
February 11, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Congo are consolidating bilateral military cooperation to enhance security along their shared border, as Deputy Prime Minister of National Defense Guy Kabombo visited Brazzaville to meet with Congolese counterparts.
According to Kabombo’s office, the visit aims to fortify mutual trust and promote a strategic rapprochement between the two neighboring countries. Charles Richard Mondjo, Minister of National Defense of the Republic of Congo, emphasized that the discussions are designed to strengthen diplomatic ties and address common security challenges, while ensuring that the Republic of Congo will not serve as a rear base to undermine regional stability.
“I want to clearly reiterate that the Republic of Congo will not undertake any action that could jeopardize the collective security and stability of our region,” Mondjo stated.
“Our shared concern is to make these areas safe and controlled, facilitating the smooth flow of traffic to support trade and the development of our countries. Incidents along the 1,200 km river border must be addressed through dialogue and in accordance with national interests, while respecting the bonds of fraternity between our peoples and heads of state.”
Both officials highlighted the importance of military training programs, describing them as a platform for dynamic South-South cooperation that contributes to regional stability. Kabombo underscored that the DRC expects neighboring countries to support ongoing diplomatic initiatives, including the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus, and to resist manipulations based on old pretexts.
“We aim to transform the eastern part of our country into a reservoir of supported resources,” Kabombo said, stressing the need for practical collaboration to secure national territory.
The visit comes amid ongoing Rwandan aggression through the AFC/M23 rebellion, which continues to control large areas in North Kivu and South Kivu, and amid slow progress on diplomatic initiatives in Washington and Doha.
Historically, rapprochement between Brazzaville and Kigali has been viewed skeptically in Kinshasa due to Rwanda’s perceived role in destabilizing eastern DRC. Despite these concerns, leaders in Brazzaville and Kinshasa have consistently reaffirmed their commitment to joint security efforts and broader regional cooperation. President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC maintains regular engagements with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, to address security challenges and other pressing international issues affecting the sub-region.

title: FARDC Launches Drone Strikes on AFC/M23 Positions in Mpety
excerpt: Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone airstrikes on AFC/M23 rebel positions around Mpety, in the Kisimba area of Walikale territory, North Kivu, on Wednesday. Local administrative and traditional sources report
title_en: FARDC Launches Drone Strikes on AFC/M23 Positions in Mpety
excerpt_en: Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone airstrikes on AFC/M23 rebel positions around Mpety, in the Kisimba area of Walikale territory, North Kivu, on Wednesday. Local administrative and traditional sources report
body_en:
Walikale February 11, 2026 – The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) carried out drone airstrikes on AFC/M23 rebel positions around Mpety, in the Kisimba area of Walikale territory, North Kivu, on Wednesday.
Local administrative and traditional sources reported that the first explosions were heard around 1 p.m., triggering panic among villagers and prompting several families to flee into the bush.
These strikes come just 48 hours after drone operations targeting rebel positions in Mindjendje, near Mpety in the Banakindi area, which reportedly caused multiple injuries among AFC/M23 fighters, according to local sources. The casualty figures from Wednesday’s strikes remain unknown.
The Pinga-Mpety-Mindjendje axis has been a flashpoint for violent clashes between the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo forces, and the AFC/M23 rebels over the past several months. The area’s strategic importance has made it a key target for both sides, fueling ongoing instability.
According to military sources, the current operations are part of the FARDC’s broader strategy to weaken AFC/M23 military capabilities and regain control of key positions around Pinga, a locality considered a security stronghold in this part of Walikale territory.

title: Angola Proposes Ceasefire Starting February 18
excerpt: February 11, 2026 – The Republic of Angola has proposed a ceasefire between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the M23 armed group, set to take effect at noon on February 18, the Angolan presidency announced Tuesday. The proposal follows a high-level meeting i
title_en: Angola Proposes Ceasefire Starting February 18
excerpt_en: February 11, 2026 – The Republic of Angola has proposed a ceasefire between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the M23 armed group, set to take effect at noon on February 18, the Angolan presidency announced Tuesday. The proposal follows a high-level meeting i
body_en:
February 11, 2026 – The Republic of Angola has proposed a ceasefire between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the M23 armed group, set to take effect at noon on February 18, the Angolan presidency announced Tuesday.
The proposal follows a high-level meeting in Luanda on Monday, attended by Angolan President João Lourenço, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi, Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé, the African Union mediator, and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, representing the AU-designated facilitators of the DRC peace process.
According to the announcement, the proposed ceasefire date is conditional upon a public declaration of acceptance by both parties. Angola also indicated that the start of the preparatory phase for the inter-Congolese dialogue, scheduled to be held in Luanda, will be announced at a later date.
The initiative underscores regional efforts to stabilize eastern DRC and curb ongoing hostilities involving the M23 rebellion.

title: MONUSCO Acting Head to Visit Goma Ahead of Ceasefire Verification
excerpt: February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced. Ms. van de Perre, serving as the A
title_en: MONUSCO Acting Head to Visit Goma Ahead of Ceasefire Verification
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced. Ms. van de Perre, serving as the A
body_en:
February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced.
Ms. van de Perre, serving as the Acting Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General, will arrive by air, marking a significant operational step after a prolonged interruption of air access to Goma since January 2025. During the visit, she will engage with relevant stakeholders to advance practical arrangements for the ceasefire verification mechanism.
Under UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025), MONUSCO is authorized to assist in the implementation of a permanent ceasefire, including technical and logistical support to the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) through the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+).
“I am going to Goma to support preparations for monitoring and verifying the ceasefire, in close coordination with the established ceasefire architecture, including the EJVM+,” Ms. van de Perre stated.
MONUSCO emphasized that its support will remain strictly within its mandate and in full respect of the sovereignty of the DRC.
A UN source indicated that the mission is also preparing a gradual resumption of operations in eastern DRC, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights, followed by a limited ground deployment, and then a progressive increase in operational presence, contingent on security guarantees.
These measures aim to bolster the momentum of the ceasefire, though the UN stresses that successful peace efforts also rely on the engagement of the guarantors of the agreements, including the United States, Qatar, and the African Union.

Local traditional sources report that the victims, all displaced farmers from Mulema, were traveling from Rusamambu in the Ikobo group, where they had sought refuge, to their fields in Minga to collect food for their families.
The civilians were reportedly ambushed by Wazalendo fighters from the CMC group of Bigabo before reaching their fields and have been held captive in Muteresi ever since. The motives for their detention remain unclear.
Families of the hostages, still in Rusamambu, expressed deep concern, having received no news of their loved ones. They are urgently appealing for their release so that they can return home and provide for their dependents.
Several villages in the Mulema area have remained largely deserted due to recurring clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. Many displaced families have sought refuge in Rusamambu, Bukumbirwa, and Buleusa, living in precarious humanitarian conditions amid ongoing insecurity.

title: ADF Attack in Ilimba Kills Two Civilians

body_en:
February 13, 2026 – Violence continues to grip Beni territory, North Kivu, as Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters carried out an attack on Thursday, February 12, in Ilimba, a village along the Oicha–Mantumbi road, killing two civilians.
Local sources report that the victims were the wife and son of the president of the Mantumbi civil society organization, both shot with firearms. In addition, two motorcycles were burned during the assault.
“In Miliese, where they were stopped by the Congolese army, the enemy set fire to a motorcycle near a military position. They also bypassed the area to kill civilians in Ilimba, where they shot and killed the wife of the president of the civil society organization and his son. Another motorcycle was also set ablaze,” said Kakule Katena, spokesperson for civil society in Mantumbi. He urged residents to remain vigilant and called on the Congolese government to intensify operations to track down the assailants.
This attack comes three days after a deadly assault in Mangadu, where five farmers were killed, and has further intensified the climate of fear that has gripped the Beni-Mbau area since the beginning of the week, following multiple ADF attacks on civilians.

title: Rival Wazalendo Groups Clash Over Control of Katatwa-Karete Axis
excerpt: February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3. The rival groups incl
title_en: Rival Wazalendo Groups Clash Over Control of Katatwa-Karete Axis
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3. The rival groups incl
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3.
The rival groups include the Mai-Mai Kifuafua, led by Shukuru Bulenda, and Raia Mutomboki, under the command of Kalumende. Local sources report that these rivalries have persisted for about two months, creating a constant threat of armed clashes as both sides assert ownership of the road.
A key consequence of this dispute is the proliferation of illegal roadblocks. Travelers along the route are forced to pay fixed sums at multiple checkpoints, often under threat of violence or reprisals.
“We are suffering because of the selfish interests of those in charge of these armed groups. You pay here, then a few meters further on, you pay again to the other side. It’s a real ordeal,” testified one traveler.
Reports also indicate cases of torture and ill-treatment for those unable to pay the imposed taxes. Residents are further burdened by the requirement to feed fighters daily, intensifying the hardship for a population already weakened by chronic insecurity.
Many families have begun fleeing their villages to escape this pressure, worsening the humanitarian crisis in the area.
“Several people are starting to leave the area. It’s better to live on the move than to remain in this form of slavery,” said a resident of Ibiro.
Civil society in Walikale has condemned the actions of these armed groups and called on military authorities to intervene urgently to protect civilians and prevent the situation from escalating into deadly clashes.
The Katatwa–Karete axis, part of National Route 3, is a crucial corridor for trade between Hombo and Walikale, making it a highly coveted area for armed groups seeking to finance their operations through illegal taxation. The ongoing struggle has effectively turned this key economic route into a lawless zone, severely impacting the local population.

title_en: Looting in Kateku Village Attributed to AFC/M23 Rebels
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – The village of Kateku, in the Ikobo group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, experienced systematic looting on the night of Thursday, February 13, local sources report. Armed men reportedly stormed the village while residents were asleep, surrounding the area
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – The village of Kateku, in the Ikobo group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, experienced systematic looting on the night of Thursday, February 13, local sources report. Armed men reportedly stormed the village while residents were asleep, surrounding the area before carrying out a methodical theft operation.
Witnesses stated that the looters went house to house, stealing livestock, cell phones, money, and other valuables. Residents blamed AFC/M23 rebels, who maintain control over parts of the region.
Following the attack, the assailants retreated to an unknown location, leaving behind a traumatized and impoverished population. By Friday morning, fear and despair dominated the village, according to local reports.
In response to the resurgence of violence, several residents are considering leaving Kateku to seek safety, fearing further attacks in the coming days.

excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – The Batakirwa area of the Bafuna group (Wanianga sector) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, is facing a serious security crisis as two Wazalendo factions compete for control of the region. Since February 11, the Uhuru RDC armed group, led by Mashite Kashira, h
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – The Batakirwa area of the Bafuna group (Wanianga sector) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, is facing a serious security crisis as two Wazalendo factions compete for control of the region.
Since February 11, the Uhuru RDC armed group, led by Mashite Kashira, has deployed fighters in the villages of Kilambo, Buringa, and Iseya, threatening clashes with NDC-Rénové fighters under Muissa Shimiray Guidon if they attempt to enter the area. Local sources report that Uhuru RDC claims exclusive control over this mineral-rich territory, denying other armed groups any operational presence.
Civilians are caught in the crossfire. The local chief, who received threats, was forced to flee to Walikale town. He reported that residents are regularly intimidated by Uhuru RDC fighters, accused of supporting their rivals, NDC-Rénové.
“The population is in grave danger. These armed men openly threaten civilians and equate them with their enemies,” declared Chief Kabaki.
The chief has issued an urgent appeal to military and administrative authorities to intervene swiftly and defuse tensions before the situation escalates further, risking additional loss of life.

title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Withdraw from Buhaya Near Pinga
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – AFC/M23 fighters withdrew overnight on Thursday, February 12, from the Buhaya position, a strategic hill overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area, approximately 15 kilometers from Pinga in the Kisimba group, Walikale territory, North Kivu. The rebels had occup
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – AFC/M23 fighters withdrew overnight on Thursday, February 12, from the Buhaya position, a strategic hill overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area, approximately 15 kilometers from Pinga in the Kisimba group, Walikale territory, North Kivu.
The rebels had occupied Buhaya Hill since November 2025, after dislodging Wazalendo forces. The reason for the sudden withdrawal remains unknown, and no information is available about the fighters’ destination, according to the administrative secretary of Kisimba group, who confirmed the departure.
Residents of Katobi reported discovering on Friday morning that Buhaya Hill had been abandoned. Later in the day, Wazalendo forces regained control of the position, which they had lost three months earlier.
The withdrawal occurs amid a continuing unstable security situation in Walikale, where the movements of armed groups continue to fuel fear and uncertainty among the civilian population.

title: AFC/M23 Denounces Kinshasa’s “Diplomatic Fragmentation” Despite Angolan Ceasefire Proposal
excerpt: February 14, 2026 – Following renewed calls for a ceasefire, the AFC/M23 rebellion reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the mechanism agreed upon in the Doha peace process. In a statement released on Friday, February 13, political coordinator Corneille Nangaa emphasized that
title_en: AFC/M23 Denounces Kinshasa’s “Diplomatic Fragmentation” Despite Angolan Ceasefire Proposal
excerpt_en: February 14, 2026 – Following renewed calls for a ceasefire, the AFC/M23 rebellion reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the mechanism agreed upon in the Doha peace process. In a statement released on Friday, February 13, political coordinator Corneille Nangaa emphasized that
body_en:
February 14, 2026 – Following renewed calls for a ceasefire, the AFC/M23 rebellion reaffirmed its commitment to implementing the mechanism agreed upon in the Doha peace process. In a statement released on Friday, February 13, political coordinator Corneille Nangaa emphasized that this stance reflects a sense of political responsibility and a desire for a negotiated, lasting, and inclusive settlement of the conflict.
“However, the AFC/M23 denounces the strategy of diplomatic fragmentation employed by the illegitimate and corrupt regime in Kinshasa, characterized by the proliferation of parallel frameworks and initiatives outside a centralized and consensual process. Such an approach compromises mediation efforts, weakens credibility, and risks delaying a serious political settlement,” Nangaa stated.
He also accused the Kinshasa government of continuing belligerent acts, including offensives against populated areas, use of mercenaries, and indiscriminate bombings, despite its public support for the ceasefire. Nangaa described the government’s acceptance of the ceasefire principle as a public relations maneuver, aimed at deceiving national and international opinion while continuing a militaristic strategy.
This statement follows an Angolan ceasefire proposal, announced after a meeting in Luanda with Angolan President João Lourenço, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi, Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé (AU mediator), and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, representing AU-designated facilitators for the DRC peace process.
The diplomatic momentum was preceded by a high-level meeting in Lomé, Togo, on January 17, 2026, aimed at consolidating the peace process in the DRC and the Great Lakes region. Initiated by Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, AU lead mediator for eastern DRC, the meeting reinforced coordination with the United States and Qatar to encourage parties to honor their commitments.
Following Lomé, the African Union outlined its mediation structure, under Gnassingbé’s authority, supported by five co-facilitators with specific responsibilities and a joint secretariat comprising the AU and regional organizations, tasked with steering the peace process in eastern DRC.

title: FARDC Accuses AFC/M23 of Burning Houses Ahead of Ceasefire
excerpt: Fizi-Uvira February 14, 2026 – Four days before the scheduled ceasefire between the Congolese government and the M23, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) accused the AFC/M23-RDF coalition of burning civilian homes on February 11 in the Rusankuku area of t
title_en: FARDC Accuses AFC/M23 of Burning Houses Ahead of Ceasefire
excerpt_en: Fizi-Uvira February 14, 2026 – Four days before the scheduled ceasefire between the Congolese government and the M23, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) accused the AFC/M23-RDF coalition of burning civilian homes on February 11 in the Rusankuku area of t
body_en:
Fizi-Uvira February 14, 2026 – Four days before the scheduled ceasefire between the Congolese government and the M23, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) accused the AFC/M23-RDF coalition of burning civilian homes on February 11 in the Rusankuku area of the Fizi-Uvira highlands, citing a military statement.
The statement, signed by acting spokesperson Lieutenant Colonel Mongba Hazukay Mak, described the actions as “serious violations of International Humanitarian Law and Human Rights.” According to the FARDC, the operation was intended to punish local populations who refused to comply with the rebels’ demands. The army condemned the acts as terrorist attacks, emphasizing that they demonstrate the cruelty and determination of the Rwandan army and its proxies to undermine the ongoing peace process.
This comes as Kinshasa announced acceptance of an Angolan ceasefire proposal, set to take effect at noon on February 18, 2026. The Presidency emphasized that this decision reflects responsibility, appeasement, and the search for a peaceful solution, while commending Angola for its efforts toward a lasting return to peace in the Great Lakes region.
The ceasefire falls under the monitoring and verification mechanism signed in Doha on October 14, 2025, which stipulates:
Immediate freeze on military positions
Halt to all reinforcements and offensive rotations
No modification of the status quo on the ground
End of external support for armed groups
Protection of civilians and respect for international humanitarian law
Kinshasa warned that any unilateral military consolidation during the ceasefire would seriously undermine the credibility of the process.
The Angolan proposal followed a Luanda meeting involving Angolan President João Lourenço, DRC President Félix Tshisekedi, Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé (AU mediator), and former Nigerian President Olusegun Obasanjo, designated by the AU as facilitator. This diplomatic momentum was preceded by a high-level meeting in Lomé on January 17, 2026, which defined the AU mediation structure for the DRC peace process, led by Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, supported by five co-facilitators and a joint secretariat.
For its part, the AFC/M23 confirmed readiness to implement the Doha mechanism in good faith, but political coordinator Corneille Nangaa criticized Kinshasa for a “strategy of diplomatic fragmentation”, calling the government’s ceasefire acceptance a public relations maneuver. He also accused the authorities of continuing belligerent acts, including offensives on populated areas, the use of mercenaries, and indiscriminate bombings affecting civilians.

title: Tshisekedi Urges MONUSCO’s “Credible Technical” Support for Ceasefire
excerpt: February 14, 2026 – On the sidelines of the 39th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi called on UN Secretary-General António Guterres for “urgent and credible technical support” from MONUSCO to operationalize the ceasefire monitoring and verif
title_en: Tshisekedi Urges MONUSCO’s “Credible Technical” Support for Ceasefire
excerpt_en: February 14, 2026 – On the sidelines of the 39th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi called on UN Secretary-General António Guterres for “urgent and credible technical support” from MONUSCO to operationalize the ceasefire monitoring and verif
body_en:
February 14, 2026 – On the sidelines of the 39th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi called on UN Secretary-General António Guterres for “urgent and credible technical support” from MONUSCO to operationalize the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism in eastern DRC.
The meeting focused on the security situation in the Great Lakes region, strengthening multilateral cooperation, and the DRC’s role as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council. President Tshisekedi reaffirmed the DRC’s commitment to consolidating peace efforts and emphasized the need to move from exhortations to action to ensure compliance with international law and agreements under regional and international frameworks.
“We need credible technical support from MONUSCO to guarantee the operationalization of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism,” Tshisekedi stated, citing UN Security Council resolution 2808 (2025).
Secretary-General Guterres pledged the UN’s support for the implementation of the established ceasefire architecture, welcoming the DRC’s engagement in fair and effective multilateralism.
On the ground, the acting head of MONUSCO, Vivian van de Perre, traveled to Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying the ceasefire. Arriving by air—marking the first flight access to Goma since January 2025—she is scheduled to meet with stakeholders to advance the practical arrangements for the mechanism.
“I am going to Goma to support preparations for monitoring and verifying the ceasefire, in close coordination with the established ceasefire architecture, including the EJVM+,” van de Perre said.
MONUSCO is authorized under resolution 2808 (2025) to provide technical and logistical support to the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) through the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+). An initial team of peacekeepers will be deployed to Uvira, South Kivu, to assist the ceasefire monitoring mechanism. This deployment is limited and technical, not constituting a permanent return to the province, from which MONUSCO withdrew in June 2024.
Peacekeepers remain actively deployed in Ituri and North Kivu, continuing their support for security and monitoring operations in eastern DRC.

title: Explosive Devices Found in Residents’ Fields in Ruwenzori
excerpt: Ruwenzori Beni February 14, 2026 – Two explosive devices were discovered in Manzembe and Mwenda, areas within the Beni territory of North Kivu, reportedly left behind by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels during their retreat, according to Kalungo Mambo of the Civil Protection
title_en: Explosive Devices Found in Residents’ Fields in Ruwenzori
excerpt_en: Ruwenzori Beni February 14, 2026 – Two explosive devices were discovered in Manzembe and Mwenda, areas within the Beni territory of North Kivu, reportedly left behind by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels during their retreat, according to Kalungo Mambo of the Civil Protection
body_en:
Ruwenzori Beni February 14, 2026 – Two explosive devices were discovered in Manzembe and Mwenda, areas within the Beni territory of North Kivu, reportedly left behind by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels during their retreat, according to Kalungo Mambo of the Civil Protection service in the Ruwenzori sector.
Experts from the United Nations Mine Action Service (UNMAS) intervened in Manzembe to defuse a bomb discovered by residents last Saturday. Civil Protection authorities urged locals to exercise caution in areas near former ADF strongholds, highlighting the risks posed by abandoned explosive devices.
“The bomb discovered in Manzembe posed a danger near a busy road leading to the population's fields. We urge everyone to be careful when working in the fields, because after the attackers passed through, several explosive devices were left behind,” Mambo said.
In Mwenda, another device was located by FARDC forces, buried in the sand and awaiting demining to allow safe access for residents.
The discovery of such explosive hazards has become increasingly frequent following the recapture of several ADF strongholds by the Congolese army in the Ruwenzori sector. Authorities continue to call for heightened vigilance among civilians in these high-risk areas.

title_en: Kinshasa and Luanda Establish Joint Defense and Security Commission
excerpt_en: February 15, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Angola signed an agreement in Luanda establishing a Joint Defense and Security Commission, following two days of meetings between security and defense experts from both countries. The agreement, signed by the respecti
body_en:
February 15, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Angola signed an agreement in Luanda establishing a Joint Defense and Security Commission, following two days of meetings between security and defense experts from both countries.
The agreement, signed by the respective Ministers of the Interior and Security, aims to enhance bilateral security cooperation and strengthen coordination along the shared border. Both countries emphasized the importance of regular information sharing and scheduled meetings between military and police commands to address cross-border threats.
Deputy Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani and his Angolan counterpart, Manuel Gomes, also addressed the issue of Rwandan aggression in eastern DRC, condemning the use of force to seize power and highlighting the need to respect democratic principles for regional stability.
Experts from both nations praised the political commitment of President Félix Tshisekedi and the Angolan President in reinforcing fraternal ties and fostering cooperation between their peoples.
This joint commission marks a strategic step in addressing security challenges and reinforcing peace and stability along the DRC-Angola border.

title: Deadly Clashes in Panu: Nine Face Military Court over Terrorism Charges
excerpt: February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special sessio
title_en: Deadly Clashes in Panu: Nine Face Military Court over Terrorism Charges
excerpt_en: February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special sessio
body_en:
February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special session held in Idiofa.
Eight civilians are charged with terrorism, while a police captain faces prosecution for failing to assist a person in danger, after allegedly filming his colleague’s beheading during the clashes. The eight injured police officers have filed civil suits, though no civilian victims have appeared in court.
“We expect the court to convict all these alleged perpetrators of terrorism. We expect reparations for the acts committed because they injured, robbed, and vandalized the property of the police officers they killed,” said Toto Nkonde, part of the victims’ legal team.
According to court proceedings, the confrontation erupted after police arrested three major gang leaders. In retaliation, young bandits mobilized, attacked police with stones, and attempted to expel them from the town. Despite warning shots, the clashes escalated before the bandits eventually surrendered.
The case underscores the persistent insecurity in the region and the military court’s role in addressing terrorism and violent unrest.

title_en: Traffic Resumes on Chivanga-Bulambika Road Despite Rebel Harassment
excerpt_en: February 15, 2026 – South Kivu – Road traffic resumed on Sunday, February 8, along the Chivanga–Kalonge–Bulambika–Hombo road in Kalehe territory, offering relief after months of paralysis caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. Motorcycle taxi drivers are
body_en:
February 15, 2026 – South Kivu – Road traffic resumed on Sunday, February 8, along the Chivanga–Kalonge–Bulambika–Hombo road in Kalehe territory, offering relief after months of paralysis caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
Motorcycle taxi drivers are now transporting goods from Bukavu to Hombo, enabling a tentative resumption of commerce. However, users report harassment at rebel checkpoints:
AFC/M23 rebels at Chivanga are reportedly demanding 50,000 FC per motorcycle.
Wazalendo fighters at the entrance to Kahuzi-Biega National Park are imposing 30,000 FC per motorcyclist.
Locals warn that these roadblocks may drive up transportation costs, affecting the price of basic necessities. Motorcycle taxi drivers have urged the armed groups to dismantle the checkpoints, warning that continued harassment threatens the region’s economic recovery.
The Miti–Bulambika–Hombo axis had been closed for several months, leading to serious economic and social consequences for the population. Traffic resumption marks a step toward normalcy, but security and fair passage remain major concerns.

title: Over 20 Schools Closed Amid Rising ADF Violence
excerpt: Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks. The closures have affected schools
title_en: Over 20 Schools Closed Amid Rising ADF Violence
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks. The closures have affected schools
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks.
The closures have affected schools in villages including Vurondo, Kisasa, Ndondi, Kiriva, Kisungu, Vulera, Kyondo, and Kitumbu, leaving students and teachers displaced to nearby towns such as Butuhe and Butembo. Classes have been suspended since Monday, January 26, disrupting the academic calendar, particularly the first semester exams for secondary students.
Civil society leaders are calling on the Congolese government and school authorities to:
Strengthen security measures in affected villages.
Protect school infrastructure from looting or occupation by armed groups.
Ensure displaced students can complete the school year.
The school closures coincide with continued ADF attacks in the region:
Upende/Mangadu (Feb 10): Four civilians, including a woman, were executed, most by beheading.
Mavete (Feb 14): Two civilians killed while traveling to their fields.
Since the start of 2026, at least 63 civilians have been killed by suspected ADF fighters in Beni and Lubero territories, with Lubero being the hardest hit (52 deaths) compared to Beni (10 deaths), according to the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination.
The growing threat has left parents and residents fearful for their safety, highlighting the urgent need for restored security and protection of civilian life and education in the region.

excerpt_en: February 16, 2026 – Chanjikiro, Kisimba group, North Kivu – Nine fighters from the AFC/M23 rebellion voluntarily surrendered to the Wazalendo (Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland) on Saturday, February 15, in Chanjikiro, Banamukema area. The surrendering rebels handed over
body_en:
February 16, 2026 – Chanjikiro, Kisimba group, North Kivu – Nine fighters from the AFC/M23 rebellion voluntarily surrendered to the Wazalendo (Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland) on Saturday, February 15, in Chanjikiro, Banamukema area. The surrendering rebels handed over four AK-47 rifles to the VDP.
Local security sources reported that the former combatants were immediately transported to Pinga for processing and identification.
These surrenders are linked to increased military pressure by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), which has intensified drone strikes on key AFC/M23 positions around Pinga, including Mpety and Mindjendje, known as major logistical bases for the rebellion.
Security officials view these voluntary surrenders as a sign of the FARDC’s growing operational effectiveness in the Walikale territory.

title_en: Traders Looted on Route to Malimingi Mining Site
excerpt_en: February 16, 2026 – Maasha, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – A convoy of traders traveling from Lubero to the Malimingi mining site was attacked by unidentified armed men on Saturday, February 15, in Maasha. According to administrative and security sources from the W
body_en:
February 16, 2026 – Maasha, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – A convoy of traders traveling from Lubero to the Malimingi mining site was attacked by unidentified armed men on Saturday, February 15, in Maasha.
According to administrative and security sources from the Wanianga sector, the assailants systematically looted the convoy, stealing money, cell phones, and merchandise. The victims, traumatized by the attack, were forced to return to Rusamambu. No fatalities were reported.
This incident highlights the ongoing insecurity in Walikale, where multiple armed groups operate and frequently target traders on strategic routes. A similar attack occurred in November 2025 along the same route.
Local traders and economic stakeholders are urging authorities to strengthen security measures to ensure safe passage to mining sites and protect the movement of people and goods.

excerpt_en: February 16, 2026 – Kateku, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – The five civilians abducted during the armed incursion attributed to AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday, February 13, remain missing. Local sources confirm that no information has emerged about the hostages’ wherea
body_en:
February 16, 2026 – Kateku, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – The five civilians abducted during the armed incursion attributed to AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday, February 13, remain missing.
Local sources confirm that no information has emerged about the hostages’ whereabouts or the intentions of their captors. Traditional and administrative authorities report no sign of life from the victims.
"So far, we have no news of our compatriots. All efforts undertaken with community leaders and security services have been unsuccessful," stated a local official.
Families of the abducted civilians are in deep distress. “We spend our nights without sleep; we don’t even know if they’re still alive,” said a family member.
Civil society in Walikale is calling for the swift and unconditional release of the hostages and urges provincial and national authorities to strengthen civilian protection in this volatile area.
