title: Council of Ministers Focuses on Mines, Sugar Industry, and Economic Reforms
excerpt: Bamako, February 13, 2026 – In an ordinary session at the Koulouba Palace chaired by President Assimi Goïta, the Council of Ministers adopted several measures with significant economic impact, particularly in the mining, industrial, and commercial sectors. Under the Ministry of M
title_en: Council of Ministers Focuses on Mines, Sugar Industry, and Economic Reforms
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 13, 2026 – In an ordinary session at the Koulouba Palace chaired by President Assimi Goïta, the Council of Ministers adopted several measures with significant economic impact, particularly in the mining, industrial, and commercial sectors. Under the Ministry of M
body_en:
Bamako, February 13, 2026 – In an ordinary session at the Koulouba Palace chaired by President Assimi Goïta, the Council of Ministers adopted several measures with significant economic impact, particularly in the mining, industrial, and commercial sectors.
Under the Ministry of Mines, the Council approved a draft decree renewing the gold mining permit for the Loulo Mining Company (SOMILO S.A.). Originally granted in 1996 for the exploitation of the Loulo gold mine in the Kéniéba district, the permit is renewed for ten years. Feasibility studies by Barrick Mining Corporation indicate that exploitable reserves could support substantial production, boosting the mining sector’s contribution to the national economy.
In the industrial and commercial sector, the Council noted the official launch of the 2025-2026 sugar campaign for SUKALA and N-SUKALA, with an anticipated combined production of approximately 120,000 tons, meeting nearly 34% of Mali’s annual sugar needs. Measures have been implemented to ensure domestic supply ahead of Ramadan 2026.
These decisions reflect the authorities’ commitment to strengthening Mali’s economic sovereignty through the development of natural resources, support for local production, and securing essential goods, amid ongoing economic and geopolitical challenges.

title: Upper Niger Valley Office Opens 34th Session, Highlights Agricultural Gains
excerpt: Ségou, February 12, 2026 – Daniel Siméon Kelema, Minister of Agriculture, presided over the opening of the 34th ordinary session of the Upper Niger Valley Office (OHVN) for the 2025 agricultural campaign on Thursday, February 12, 2026, in Ségou. The campaign has shown promising r
title_en: Upper Niger Valley Office Opens 34th Session, Highlights Agricultural Gains
excerpt_en: Ségou, February 12, 2026 – Daniel Siméon Kelema, Minister of Agriculture, presided over the opening of the 34th ordinary session of the Upper Niger Valley Office (OHVN) for the 2025 agricultural campaign on Thursday, February 12, 2026, in Ségou. The campaign has shown promising r
body_en:
Ségou, February 12, 2026 – Daniel Siméon Kelema, Minister of Agriculture, presided over the opening of the 34th ordinary session of the Upper Niger Valley Office (OHVN) for the 2025 agricultural campaign on Thursday, February 12, 2026, in Ségou.
The campaign has shown promising results, with production targets largely met:
Cereals: 347,964 tons (82% of target)
Seed cotton: 19,200 tons (70%)
Pulses: 54,351 tons (79%)
Sesame: 4,859 tons (72%)
Vegetables: 134,035 tons (91%)
The campaign has resulted in a cereal surplus of approximately 7,388 tons.
As part of agricultural modernization efforts, equipment was provided to 25 family farms, three input storage warehouses were renovated, and two organic sesame storage warehouses were constructed. Additionally, 6,025 tons of mineral fertilizers were made available to farmers in the OHVN zone to support continued growth.

title: Mali Launches 2025–2026 Sugar Campaign, Government Reassures on Supply
excerpt: Ségou, February 5, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Industry and Trade, Moussa Alassane Diallo, officially launched the 2025–2026 sugar campaign on Thursday at the Séribala and Bewani sugar complexes in the Ségou region. The minister was accompanied by senior officials from his departme
title_en: Mali Launches 2025–2026 Sugar Campaign, Government Reassures on Supply
excerpt_en: Ségou, February 5, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Industry and Trade, Moussa Alassane Diallo, officially launched the 2025–2026 sugar campaign on Thursday at the Séribala and Bewani sugar complexes in the Ségou region. The minister was accompanied by senior officials from his departme
body_en:
Ségou, February 5, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Industry and Trade, Moussa Alassane Diallo, officially launched the 2025–2026 sugar campaign on Thursday at the Séribala and Bewani sugar complexes in the Ségou region.
The minister was accompanied by senior officials from his department, including the National Director of Industry and a representative of the National Transitional Council (CNT), alongside regional and local authorities.
Repairs Completed After August Attacks
During a tour of the Séribala industrial facilities, Minister Diallo confirmed that repairs following the attacks last August had been successfully completed. He stated that restoration work was carried out efficiently through the joint mobilization of Malian and Chinese technical teams, underscoring the strength of the bilateral technical partnership.
Assurance on Sugar Availability
The official launch of the campaign comes amid concerns about production disruptions. Authorities reassured the public that industrial operations have resumed normally and that sugar supply will be maintained throughout the campaign.
The event signals the government’s commitment to ensuring continuity in strategic agro-industrial production despite security and logistical challenges.

title: WAEMU Grants CFA 100 Million to Mali to Combat Desert Locust Resurgence
excerpt: Bamako, February 5, 2026 – Mali has received an exceptional financial contribution of 100 million CFA francs from the Commission of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) to strengthen efforts against the resurgence of the desert locust in the western part of the co
title_en: WAEMU Grants CFA 100 Million to Mali to Combat Desert Locust Resurgence
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 5, 2026 – Mali has received an exceptional financial contribution of 100 million CFA francs from the Commission of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) to strengthen efforts against the resurgence of the desert locust in the western part of the co
body_en:
Bamako, February 5, 2026 – Mali has received an exceptional financial contribution of 100 million CFA francs from the Commission of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU) to strengthen efforts against the resurgence of the desert locust in the western part of the country.
The symbolic check was presented on Thursday at the Ministry of Agriculture by Roberto Alexandre Vieira, WAEMU Commission Representative in Mali, to the Minister of Agriculture, Daniel Siméon Kelema. The funds were subsequently handed over to the National Locust Control Center (CNLCP) during the ceremony.
According to WAEMU’s representative, the special contribution is intended to support the implementation of Mali’s National Locust Risk Response Plan, reinforcing prevention, monitoring, and rapid intervention activities to protect agricultural production.
The initiative reflects regional solidarity within WAEMU and aims to mitigate potential threats to food security posed by desert locust infestations.

Bamako, February 5, 2026 – Strengthening bilateral cooperation in the transport and infrastructure sector was at the center of discussions between Mali’s Minister of Transport and Infrastructure, Dembélé Madina Sissoko, and Li Xiang, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to Mali.
The meeting, held Thursday in Bamako, marked the first official exchange between the two officials. Ambassador Li paid a courtesy visit to Minister Sissoko shortly after presenting his credentials to General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition and Head of State.
Discussions focused on reinforcing the Sino-Malian partnership in key infrastructure projects and exploring avenues to deepen collaboration in transport development, a strategic sector for Mali’s economic growth and regional connectivity.
The engagement reflects the continued dynamism of relations between Mali and China, particularly in infrastructure development and public works.

title: Mali Targets CFA 1.45 Trillion in Government Bond Issuances for 2026
excerpt: Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Mali has unveiled its 2026 government securities issuance calendar, aiming to mobilize 1.45 trillion CFA francs on the regional financial market of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). The program forms part of the government’s strategy
title_en: Mali Targets CFA 1.45 Trillion in Government Bond Issuances for 2026
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Mali has unveiled its 2026 government securities issuance calendar, aiming to mobilize 1.45 trillion CFA francs on the regional financial market of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU). The program forms part of the government’s strategy
body_en:
Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Mali has unveiled its 2026 government securities issuance calendar, aiming to mobilize 1.45 trillion CFA francs on the regional financial market of the West African Economic and Monetary Union (WAEMU).
The program forms part of the government’s strategy to meet its financing needs through structured, market-based instruments.
According to details presented at the launch ceremony, the annual target is distributed as follows:
340 billion CFA francs in the first quarter
400 billion CFA francs in the second quarter
430 billion CFA francs in the third quarter
280 billion CFA francs in the fourth quarter
Authorities stated that this quarterly allocation is intended to enhance market transparency and allow investors to better plan their participation throughout the year.
Mali Inaugurates Tier III Data Center, Advances Digital Sovereignty
As part of the third edition of Mali’s Digital Week, Minister of Communication, Digital Economy and Administrative Modernization Alhamdou Ag Ilyène officially inaugurated a Tier III Data Center, a strategic infrastructure aimed at strengthening national and regional digital sovereignty.
The ceremony was attended by digital ministers from Niger and Burkina Faso, members of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES).
Designed to meet high international standards, the facility guarantees 99.982% service availability, full redundancy of critical systems, uninterrupted operations during maintenance, and advanced physical and cybersecurity safeguards.
The data center will provide secure hosting for:
Government databases and critical applications
National e-government platforms and public digital services
Future shared digital infrastructure within the AES region
Officials emphasized that the infrastructure will reduce dependence on foreign hosting services, enhance cybersecurity, and create a foundation for the development of artificial intelligence, digital financial services, and sovereign digital platforms.
According to participating ministers, control over national data hosting and processing is essential for protecting sensitive state information and reinforcing independent public decision-making.

excerpt: Bamako, February 4, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the newly appointed Country Director of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Mali, Cédric Achille Mbeng Mezui, and the new Resident Coordinator of the United Na
title_en: Foreign Minister Abdoulaye Diop Receives New AfDB Country Director and UN Resident Coordinator
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 4, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the newly appointed Country Director of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Mali, Cédric Achille Mbeng Mezui, and the new Resident Coordinator of the United Na
body_en:
Bamako, February 4, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Abdoulaye Diop, received the newly appointed Country Director of the African Development Bank (AfDB) in Mali, Cédric Achille Mbeng Mezui, and the new Resident Coordinator of the United Nations system in Mali, Hanaa Fikry Ahmed Singer, during an official audience on Wednesday in Bamako.
The two officials were present to submit their letters of accreditation.
Focus on Multilateral Cooperation
Following formalities, discussions centered on the evolving national context and the prospects for strengthened multilateral cooperation. Minister Diop highlighted what he described as a paradigm shift in Mali’s governance, marked by renewed national ownership and revised principles guiding public action and partnerships.

title_en: Ministry of National Entrepreneurship Signs MoU with UNHCR to Support Refugees and Displaced Persons
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 6, 2026 – Minister Oumou Sall Seck, head of the Ministry of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training (MENEFP), presided over the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), fo
body_en:
Bamako, February 6, 2026 – Minister Oumou Sall Seck, head of the Ministry of National Entrepreneurship, Employment and Vocational Training (MENEFP), presided over the signing of a memorandum of understanding (MoU) with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), focusing on the socio-professional integration and capacity building of refugees, internally displaced persons (IDPs), and stateless persons in Mali.
The ceremony brought together UNHCR Resident Representative Pierre Camara, Ministry staff, and UNHCR personnel.
Supporting Vulnerable Populations
UNHCR highlighted that over 280,000 refugees reside in Mali, 58% of whom are women, and contribute to national development. The organization emphasized the importance of vocational training, micro-enterprise creation, and socio-professional integration in empowering displaced populations.
Minister Oumou Sall Seck commended UNHCR’s pragmatism and recalled Mali’s commitment, under President Assimi Goïta and Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga, to protect displaced persons while creating conditions for voluntary return or integration. She underscored the need for coordinated action with national and international stakeholders to deliver effective and sustainable solutions.
Key Areas of Cooperation
The MoU will guide three years of collaborative initiatives, including:
Institutional support for state structures in entrepreneurship, employment, and vocational training;
Inclusion of refugees, IDPs, and stateless persons in national vocational training and employability programs;
Enhanced cooperation to mobilize funding from development partners and financial institutions.
The Minister emphasized that this partnership is rooted in Mali’s cultural concepts of “Maya” and “Diatiguiya”, reflecting collective responsibility toward vulnerable populations. She described the MoU as the foundation for future programs aimed at empowering displaced persons and integrating them into Mali’s socio-economic fabric.
The memorandum is renewable every three years by mutual agreement, establishing a long-term framework for sustainable cooperation.

Bamako, February 5, 2026 – Youssouf Sissoko, editor-in-chief of the daily newspaper L’Alternance, was placed in pretrial detention on Thursday in Bamako, facing prosecution for “spreading false information,” “damaging the reputation of the state,” and “insulting a foreign head of state.”
According to the Association of Private Press Publishers (ASSEP), the arrest follows the publication of an article in the February 2 edition of the newspaper.
The journalist’s hearing is scheduled for March 9, 2026, while the charges against him continue to raise concerns over freedom of expression and press freedom in Mali.
In a statement, ASSEP said it is closely monitoring the case and reaffirmed its commitment to the constitutional protections for freedom of the press enshrined in the July 22, 2023 Constitution.

title: Massive Human Rights Violations Reported in Azawad and Central Mali – 2025
excerpt: Bamako, February 5, 2026 – The 2025 annual report of a leading human rights monitoring organization reveals a disturbing surge in human rights violations in Azawad (northern Mali) and parts of central Mali, documenting 374 serious incidents committed amid a non-international arme
title_en: Massive Human Rights Violations Reported in Azawad and Central Mali – 2025
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 5, 2026 – The 2025 annual report of a leading human rights monitoring organization reveals a disturbing surge in human rights violations in Azawad (northern Mali) and parts of central Mali, documenting 374 serious incidents committed amid a non-international arme
body_en:
Bamako, February 5, 2026 – The 2025 annual report of a leading human rights monitoring organization reveals a disturbing surge in human rights violations in Azawad (northern Mali) and parts of central Mali, documenting 374 serious incidents committed amid a non-international armed conflict.
The report attributes most violations to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) operating alongside foreign armed actors, including Wagner Group and later Africa Corps. Documented abuses include:
Extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and arbitrary arrests.
Torture and the destruction and looting of civilian property.
Drone strikes causing hundreds of casualties, including women and children, contributing to a reported 553 deaths.
The economic, social, and environmental impact is equally alarming: over 2,600 civilian properties have been destroyed or looted, and deliberate forest fires have further endangered vulnerable communities. While sexual violence remains under-documented due to security challenges, the report classifies it as a war crime, highlighting the gravity of the abuses.
In response to these systematic violations of international humanitarian law, the organization calls for:
Independent investigations.
Immediate cessation of attacks on civilians.
A strong fight against impunity.
The report urges both Malian authorities and the international community to take urgent action to protect civilians, ensure justice, and restore prospects for lasting peace in Mali.

title: Alarming Human Rights Violations Reported in Azawad – January 2026
excerpt: Bamako, February 6, 2026 –The security and humanitarian situation in Azawad has sharply deteriorated, with a surge in human rights violations against civilians in January 2026, according to a new report by a local human rights organization. The report documents multiple forms of
title_en: Alarming Human Rights Violations Reported in Azawad – January 2026
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 6, 2026 –The security and humanitarian situation in Azawad has sharply deteriorated, with a surge in human rights violations against civilians in January 2026, according to a new report by a local human rights organization. The report documents multiple forms of
body_en:
Bamako, February 6, 2026 –The security and humanitarian situation in Azawad has sharply deteriorated, with a surge in human rights violations against civilians in January 2026, according to a new report by a local human rights organization.
The report documents multiple forms of abuse, highlighting a troubling trend of violence and lawlessness:
10 cases of abduction, enforced disappearance, and torture, primarily targeting civilians.
8 cases of summary executions and airstrikes, resulting in loss of life.
11 cases of looting, destruction, and ransacking of civilian property, affecting homes, businesses, and livelihoods.
Over 10 humanitarian and environmental consequences, including forced displacement, food insecurity, and deteriorating living conditions.
8 cases of environmental damage, linked to bombings, fires, and infrastructure destruction.
Notably, no cases of rape or sexual violence were officially recorded this month, though the report cautions this may reflect limitations in documentation rather than absence of the crime.
The findings underscore a systematic violation of international humanitarian law and a pressing need for action. The organization calls for the urgent protection of civilians, the initiation of independent investigations, and the prosecution of perpetrators.
The situation in Azawad remains critical, with both human and environmental consequences intensifying as the month progresses.

body_en:
Bamako, February 7, 2026 – The Minister of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, Mamoudou Kassogué, officially launched the first phase of the recruitment examination for prison and juvenile justice officers at the Faculty of Private Law (FDPRI) in Badalabougou, known as the hill of knowledge.
This session saw 4,403 candidates registered for 200 available positions, highlighting the growing appeal of careers in the judicial and correctional system.
The examination began with a general knowledge test, personally administered by the Minister. The test focused on the importance of work in achieving independence, a theme reflecting both civic values and the country’s current socio-economic challenges.
Addressing the candidates, Minister Kassogué assured them of the transparency, fairness, and credibility of the recruitment process, stressing that the competition would be based solely on merit, skills, and equal opportunity.
The recruitment drive forms part of a broader initiative to strengthen the prison service and juvenile justice system, aimed at improving security, prison management, and the social reintegration of individuals under judicial supervision, in line with directives from the transitional authorities.

body_en:
Bamako, February 9, 2026 – As part of the 4th annual Justice Week, Minister of Justice and Human Rights Mamoudou Kassogué presented a consignment of solar equipment and office furniture to the National Human Rights Directorate (DNDH) on Monday, February 9, 2026.
Valued at 33 million CFA francs and funded by the European Union’s Sahel-Mali mission (EUCAP), the support aims to provide the DNDH with energy independence, addressing frequent power outages that have hampered operations since its commissioning in September 2024.
Abdoul Karim Diarra, National Director of Human Rights, highlighted the crucial importance of the donation, noting that the new solar energy systems will stabilize working conditions for staff and strengthen the department’s operational capacity.
Minister Kassogué reaffirmed that the DNDH remains a key institution for implementing national human rights policy, ensuring transparent and responsible management of the new systems in support of the rule of law.

title_en: CD-DPA 2025 Report Highlights Severe Human Rights Violations in Azawad and Central Mali
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 –The 2025 annual report by the CD-DPA reveals a deteriorating human rights situation in Azawad and parts of central Mali, documenting 374 incidents of serious violations against civilian populations amid a non-international armed conflict. The report notes a hea
body_en:
February 12, 2026 –The 2025 annual report by the CD-DPA reveals a deteriorating human rights situation in Azawad and parts of central Mali, documenting 374 incidents of serious violations against civilian populations amid a non-international armed conflict.
The report notes a heavy death toll of 553, including many women and children, and attributes the abuses primarily to the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) operating alongside foreign armed actors, notably Wagner and later the Africa Corps.
Documented violations include torture, arbitrary arrests, enforced disappearances, and the widespread destruction of civilian property, illustrating a systematic pattern of violence in flagrant violation of international humanitarian law.

Bamako, February 14, 2026 – To conclude the 4th edition of Justice Week, a press luncheon was held on Saturday, February 14, 2026, at the Bamako International Conference Center (CICB). The event was attended by Minister of Justice and Human Rights Mamoudou Kassogué, members of his staff, the General Secretariat, judicial stakeholders, technical and financial partners, as well as numerous civilian and military figures.
The luncheon provided a forum for discussion, allowing the Minister of Justice to review the week’s activities and highlight the Ministry’s key achievements over the past year. The opening ceremony included the screening of a documentary showcasing the Ministry’s initiatives for 2025.
Dr. Boubacar Sidiki Diarrah, Secretary General and Chairman of the Organizing Committee, expressed satisfaction with the achievement of objectives, describing the event as a major institutional milestone. Minister Kassogué praised the event’s success, congratulated the national organizing committee, and highlighted ongoing reforms and ambitious prospects for 2026.

title_en: First Class Graduates from Mali’s New School of Penitentiary Administration
excerpt_en: Koulikoro, February 13, 2026 – As part of Justice Week, Minister of Justice Mamoudou Kassogué presided over the graduation ceremony for the first class of the Koulikoro School of Penitentiary Administration and Juvenile Detention on Friday, February 13, 2026, marking a historic m
body_en:
Koulikoro, February 13, 2026 – As part of Justice Week, Minister of Justice Mamoudou Kassogué presided over the graduation ceremony for the first class of the Koulikoro School of Penitentiary Administration and Juvenile Detention on Friday, February 13, 2026, marking a historic milestone for Mali since independence.
Established in 2023, the school aims to strengthen the staffing and operational capacities of prison personnel, ensuring a balance between security imperatives and respect for human rights.
The inaugural graduating class included 124 recruits, among them 32 women, and was named in honor of Lieutenant Colonel Tiémoko Keïta, an officer who died in the line of duty in Gao in 2021.
After six months of rigorous training combining military discipline and legal instruction, the new officers, under Commander Cheick Ibrahim Cissouma, were officially appointed, symbolizing a commitment to integrity, dedication, and service in the prison administration.

title_en: Minister Kassogué Visits Victims of Human Trafficking and Launches Fourth Edition
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 12, 2026 – As part of the 4th annual Justice Week, Minister of Justice and Human Rights Mamoudou Kassogué visited the Enda Mali reception center in Boulkassoumbougou-Kouloubléni on Thursday, February 12, 2026, to show the State’s solidarity with victims of human
body_en:
Bamako, February 12, 2026 – As part of the 4th annual Justice Week, Minister of Justice and Human Rights Mamoudou Kassogué visited the Enda Mali reception center in Boulkassoumbougou-Kouloubléni on Thursday, February 12, 2026, to show the State’s solidarity with victims of human trafficking.
During the visit, the Minister toured facilities, including dormitories, restrooms, staff offices, and the courtyard, and listened to poignant testimonies from residents. Deeply moved by accounts of sexual exploitation and fraud, he condemned this “silent tragedy” and promised rigorous sanctions against perpetrators, while commending the remarkable work of partner organizations. He also urged stakeholders to guarantee respect for human dignity in Mali.
Earlier the same day, Minister Kassogué officially launched the fourth edition of Justice Week at the Bamako International Conference Center (CICB). The event brought together government members, technical and financial partners, judicial stakeholders, and other prominent figures, under the theme “Justice in the Era of Implementing and Strengthening Reforms.”
Dr. Aboubacar Sidiki Diarrah, chairman of the organizing committee, highlighted that “there is no growth without reforms, nor reforms without growth.” Established in 2022 by the transitional government, Justice Week aims to bring justice closer to citizens, promote a more efficient public justice system, and restore public trust.
In his address, Minister Kassogué emphasized that justice is no longer a silent institution, underscoring the importance of transparency and accessibility. He added that legal professionals must not lecture citizens if they themselves openly break the law, reaffirming the commitment to a more accessible and reliable justice system for all Malians.

title_en: JNIM Ambushes Malian Army Convoy in Kayes, Dozens Killed
excerpt_en: Kayes, January 29, 2026 – The JNIM (Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims) claimed responsibility for an ambush on a Malian army convoy escorting tanker trucks between Diboli and Kayes in the Kayes region on Thursday, January 29, 2026. According to the group, the attack resu
body_en:
Kayes, January 29, 2026 – The JNIM (Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims) claimed responsibility for an ambush on a Malian army convoy escorting tanker trucks between Diboli and Kayes in the Kayes region on Thursday, January 29, 2026.
According to the group, the attack resulted in:
2 Malian soldiers killed.
Four military vehicles set on fire.
Seizure of a motorcycle, various weapons, and a large quantity of ammunition.
Approximately 50 tanker trucks burned, aggravating the country’s energy crisis.
15 drivers killed in the ambush.
The incident underscores the intense security threats facing both military personnel and civilians in western Mali.

excerpt_en: Niamey, January 31, 2026 – The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) strongly condemned the barbaric and cowardly attack carried out on the night of January 28-29, 2026, targeting Air Base 101 and Diori Hamani International Airport in Niamey, Niger. The AES described the assault as
body_en:
Niamey, January 31, 2026 – The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) strongly condemned the barbaric and cowardly attack carried out on the night of January 28-29, 2026, targeting Air Base 101 and Diori Hamani International Airport in Niamey, Niger.
The AES described the assault as a premeditated, coordinated, and indiscriminate attack, endangering both strategic infrastructure and civilian facilities, and posing serious risks to innocent civilians and property.
In a statement, the AES emphasized that the violence is part of a broader destabilization strategy, fueled by support networks, including foreign actors, whose moral and political responsibility is called into question.
The Confederation reaffirmed that:
Perpetrators, along with anyone who finances, arms, informs, or politically supports them, will be held accountable.
Member states remain united, vigilant, and committed to a coordinated and sovereign fight against terrorism.
The AES expresses full solidarity with the people and government of Niger, praising the courage of its defense and security forces.
The Confederation concluded by reaffirming the determination of the Sahelian peoples to defend sovereignty, protect populations, and pursue a future of peace, justice, and independence.

Mali, February 2, 2026 – The military junta in Mali is facing a severe security crisis, with jihadist groups reportedly taking advantage of the government’s inability to protect civilians in the south and west of the country.
According to local reports, these armed groups have established agreements with hundreds of villages across the Ségou, Mopti, and Kita regions, while the army struggles to ensure safety even on the outskirts of the capital.
Observers warn that the situation is extremely critical, emphasizing the urgent need for the return to democracy and the end of the Goïta regime, which has concentrated power indefinitely, following the self-proclamation of the junta leader as general with “indefinite” authority.

Bla, February 4, 2026 – Local sources report a serious cross-border incident in the village of Tourdou, near Bla, in Malian territory, in which ten Mauritanian nationals were reportedly killed in gruesome circumstances.
According to multiple accounts, the victims, from Hassi Alak (Djiguenni district), were grazing livestock when they were allegedly attacked. Witnesses suggest that a unit of the Malian army may be involved. The bodies were reportedly burned and concealed under branches.

body_en:
Ségou, February 7, 2026 – The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Mali announced that during territorial surveillance operations west of Ségou, several armed terrorist groups were located and neutralized.
According to the military, a group of approximately fifteen individuals hiding in a wooded area was targeted successfully. A second strike eliminated about ten terrorists and their equipment as they attempted to land by dugout canoe on the left bank of the Niger River.
In the same region, another group of roughly ten terrorists on motorcycles was also located and neutralized.
The Chief of the General Staff assured the public that coordinated operations to search for and neutralize terrorist elements are continuing throughout the country, reflecting the army’s commitment to maintaining security and territorial integrity.

body_en:
Mali, February 11, 2026 – The country faces a collapse of its security system, following a deadly attack by JNIM on January 29, 2026, between Diboli and Kayes. The assault claimed the lives of 15 drivers and 2 soldiers, destroyed four military vehicles and 50 tanker trucks, and left the bodies at the scene for 12 days without proper care.
Authorities only reacted after ten days and the threat of a drivers’ union strike, finally authorizing the burial of the victims. The incident underscores the serious security gaps and the humanitarian consequences of insufficient protection in Mali’s western regions.

Conclusion
The period from February 2 to 15, 2026, underscores a Mali defined by a stark tension between diplomatic assertiveness and internal fragility. While the transitional government under General Assimi Goïta continues to promote a vision of sovereign diplomacy and national ownership, the realities on the ground reveal an escalating security crisis and mounting humanitarian challenges.
Key Takeaways
Diplomatic Recalibration: Mali is actively diversifying its international partnerships, consolidating relations with Saudi Arabia, Iran, China, and Japan. At the same time, ties with traditional Western partners, notably the United States, remain contingent on compliance with constitutional benchmarks and clarity regarding foreign military presence.
Security & Humanitarian Crisis: Despite ongoing efforts to neutralize terrorist cells, insurgent groups such as JNIM and ISIS-Sahel continue to display high operational mobility, launching deadly ambushes across the north, center, and even previously stable western and southern regions. The abduction of senior officials and reports of severe food shortages within the military highlight systemic vulnerabilities in national defense structures.
Economic Sovereignty vs. Fragility: The government has undertaken strategic initiatives to secure economic independence, including the launch of a Tier III Data Center and the renewal of gold mining permits. However, these efforts are undermined by a persistent fuel crisis and the ongoing extortion of rural populations through "zakat" and ransom demands by armed groups.
Human Rights Challenges: Reports from 2025 and January 2026 depict a grim situation of systematic violations, including extrajudicial killings and drone strikes. While judicial reforms have been pursued, the detention of journalists and allegations of military-involved massacres reveal a complex road toward accountability and rule of law.
Ultimately, Mali stands at a crossroads. The government’s pursuit of absolute sovereignty is being rigorously tested by a resilient insurgency and a worsening humanitarian landscape. The success of the “Mali Kura” vision will hinge on the state’s ability to translate diplomatic ambition into concrete security and economic stability for its citizens.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – The Government of Mali and the European Union (EU) held a high-level working session on Tuesday aimed at strengthening political dialogue and redefining cooperation in the Sahel, according to official sources.
The meeting brought together Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop and Minister for Malians Abroad Mossa Ag Attaher with a European delegation led by EU Special Representative for the Sahel João Gomes Cravinho, who was on an official visit to Bamako.
Focus on New Cooperation Framework
During what officials described as frank and interactive discussions, Malian authorities emphasized a strategic shift in governance, highlighting the country's determination to ensure national sovereignty, self-determination, and sustainable development.
Minister Diop presented Mali’s new governance vision, stressing the authorities’ commitment to taking control of the country’s political and security trajectory.
Talks focused on several key issues, including:
The EU’s new intervention approach in the Sahel
Ongoing security challenges linked to terrorism
The role of hybrid armed actors and state sponsors
The importance of a confederal dimension in Sahel interventions
Strengthening pragmatic and realistic cooperation
Priority Areas Identified
Both sides discussed cooperation in areas of common interest, including:
Peace and reconciliation under national ownership
Management of regular migration

title: Saudi Arabia Strengthen Ties During Saudi Founding Day Celebration
excerpt: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako. Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the c
title_en: Saudi Arabia Strengthen Ties During Saudi Founding Day Celebration
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako. Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the c
body_en:
Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako.
Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the ceremony at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador Abdullah Saleh Saber, representing the Malian authorities at the official event.
Official Congratulations to Saudi Leadership
Speaking on behalf of Mali’s leadership, Minister Diop conveyed congratulations and best wishes to King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, as well as to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia, and to the Saudi people.
The Malian minister highlighted the historic religious and civilizational ties linking Mali and Saudi Arabia, recalling the famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 by Mansa Kankou Moussa, one of the most renowned rulers of the Mali Empire.
Longstanding Cooperation
Minister Diop praised the longstanding friendship and cooperation between the two countries, noting several major achievements supported by Saudi Arabia, including:
The Grand Mosque of Bamako
The Second Bamako Bridge
Various development projects
These projects were presented as symbols of strong diplomatic relations and solidarity between the two nations.
Toward Stronger Economic Partnership
Both Malian and Saudi officials stressed the importance of expanding cooperation through productive investments and structuring development projects aimed at boosting economic and trade exchanges.
Discussions also highlighted the need for closer collaboration in the fight against terrorism in Mali and across the AES Confederation, reflecting shared security priorities in the Sahel region.
Officials from both sides expressed their commitment to building a mutually beneficial partnership based on solidarity, economic cooperation, and regional stability.

title_en: Minister Abdoulaye Diop Joins Collective Iftar Under “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Initiative
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 24, 2026 – Mali’s Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop took part Tuesday in a collective iftar in the Korofina district of Bamako, as part of Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026,” a national initiative launched by Transitional President General Assimi Goïta to
body_en:
Bamako, February 24, 2026 – Mali’s Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop took part Tuesday in a collective iftar in the Korofina district of Bamako, as part of Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026,” a national initiative launched by Transitional President General Assimi Goïta to promote solidarity and national unity.
The event, held at the ASKO grounds, brought together administrative officials, municipal authorities, and religious leaders in what participants described as a moment of spiritual reflection, community sharing, and social cohesion during the holy month of Ramadan.
Promoting Solidarity and National Unity
Officials said the initiative aims to reinforce social and religious values, encourage civic engagement, and strengthen national unity at a time when the country continues to face major political and security challenges.
Speaking at the gathering, Minister Diop emphasized the importance of faith, solidarity, and collective responsibility, noting that recent difficulties faced by Mali highlight the need for national cohesion and divine guidance.
Ramadan and Lent: A Symbol of Unity
The minister also pointed out that the coincidence of Ramadan with the Christian Lent offers a unique opportunity for Malians to deepen both spiritual devotion and social solidarity.
He called on citizens to strengthen brotherhood, mutual assistance, and patriotism, urging Malians to work together in a spirit of active solidarity and national commitment.
Minister Diop concluded by appealing for prayers, unity, and patriotic action, stressing that Mali remains a nation that brings together all its citizens regardless of religion or ethnicity.

excerpt: Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development. The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Of
title_en: AES Confederation – Prime Minister Chairs Strategic Meeting on Year II Roadmap
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development. The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Of
body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development.
The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Office in Bamako, brought together members of the steering committee of the AES national committee to discuss the adoption of a consensus-based roadmap for the confederation’s second year of operations.
Irreversible Regional Alliance
Officials described the AES Confederation as an established and irreversible regional framework, strongly supported by the three member states:
Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso and current AES Chair
General Assimi Goïta, Transitional President of Mali
General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of Niger
The alliance was presented as a key instrument for strengthening regional sovereignty, security cooperation, and economic integration in the Sahel.
Building on Year I Achievements
Participants reviewed the concrete achievements of Year I, implemented under Mali’s presidency, and discussed priorities for the coming year.
According to officials, the Year II roadmap will incorporate lessons learned during the first phase and will be developed through consultation with all member states.
Three Strategic Pillars
The new roadmap is structured around three main pillars:
Defense and Security
Diplomacy
Development
Authorities said the plan aims to strengthen collective security, improve regional coordination, and promote sustainable development across AES member countries.
The meeting concluded with a commitment to finalize and implement the consensus roadmap, seen as a key step in consolidating the institutional framework of the AES Confederation.

title_en: EU Envoy Presents “New Approach” to Sahel to Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga held talks Tuesday with European Union Special Representative for the Sahel João Gomes Cravinho, who presented the EU’s new strategy for engagement in the Sahel, officials said. The meeting took place at the Prime
body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga held talks Tuesday with European Union Special Representative for the Sahel João Gomes Cravinho, who presented the EU’s new strategy for engagement in the Sahel, officials said.
The meeting took place at the Prime Minister’s Office in Bamako, where the EU envoy was received in the presence of Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop, who formally introduced the visiting delegation.
EU Seeks Renewed Engagement
During the visit, João Gomes Cravinho, accompanied by the Head of the European Union Delegation to Mali, outlined the key pillars of what Brussels describes as a “New Approach” to the Sahel.
According to the EU representative, the strategy aims to:
Maintain the European Union’s commitment in the Sahel
Improve political dialogue
Strengthen cooperation with Sahel states
Rebuild mutual trust
He noted that the 27 member states of the European Union have agreed on the need to revitalize relations with countries in the Sahel region.
Focus on Political Dialogue
The discussions emphasized the importance of constructive dialogue between Mali and the European Union, at a time when regional security and development challenges remain significant.
The visit forms part of ongoing diplomatic consultations between Mali and its international partners, aimed at redefining cooperation frameworks and strengthening strategic partnerships in the Sahel.

body_en:
Bamako, February 19, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of National Education, Dr. Amadou Sy Savane, met Thursday with British Ambassador Angus McKee to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in education, officials reported.
The meeting, held in Bamako, brought together the ministers’ respective teams to review ongoing and future collaborations between Mali and the United Kingdom in the educational sector.
UK Support for Malian Education
Officials highlighted the United Kingdom’s support, both bilaterally and through multilateral initiatives, particularly the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), which contributes to improving access, quality, and equity in Mali’s education system.
Year of Education and Culture 2026-2027
Minister Sy Savane also reminded the British delegation of Mali’s decision to declare 2026–2027 as the “Year of Education and Culture”, emphasizing the government’s commitment to strengthening educational programs and cultural initiatives nationwide.
The meeting underscored the desire of both countries to expand cooperation, promote knowledge exchange, and support sustainable development in education.

title: Mali Celebrates 299th Anniversary of Saudi Arabia’s Founding
excerpt: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated on Monday in the celebration of the 299th anniversary of the Founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador to Mali, Abdullah Saleh Sa

Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated on Monday in the celebration of the 299th anniversary of the Founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador to Mali, Abdullah Saleh Saber.
At the solemn and convivial ceremony, Minister Diop, on behalf of Mali’s highest authorities, congratulated His Majesty King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and the Saudi people, extending wishes for happiness, peace, and prosperity.
Highlighting Shared Heritage and Cooperation
The Minister also emphasized the civilizational and religious heritage of Mali, recalling Mansa Kankou Moussa’s historic pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324. He expressed satisfaction with the long-standing friendship and cooperation between Mali and Saudi Arabia, citing major projects such as the Grand Mosque of Bamako and the second Bamako Bridge.
Strengthening Bilateral Partnership
Minister Diop and the Saudi Ambassador underscored the need to enhance bilateral cooperation through:
Mutually beneficial productive investments
Implementation of structuring development projects
Promotion of economic and trade exchanges
Close collaboration in the fight against terrorism in Mali and within the AES Confederation
The ceremony reinforced Mali’s commitment to deepening diplomatic and economic ties with Saudi Arabia in a spirit of solidarity and partnership.

title: Senior Officials Review Draft Roadmap for Year Two of ESA Confederation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confede
title_en: Senior Officials Review Draft Roadmap for Year Two of ESA Confederation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confede
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confederation.
The draft, proposed by Burkina Faso, which has held the rotating presidency of the ESA since December 23, 2025, aims to consolidate the achievements of Year One and continue building the confederation.
Leadership and Delegations
The opening session was chaired by Bassolma Bazie, President of the National Commission of the AES Confederation and head of the Burkinabe delegation, alongside Bayard Mariama Gamatie, head of the Nigerien delegation, and Ambassador Mahamane Hamadou Maiga, head of the Malian delegation.
Objectives and Vision
Officials emphasized that the roadmap must:
Serve as a consensus-based guide for priority actions
Promote peace, security, and the fight against terrorism
Ensure free movement of people and goods
Support endogenous economic development
Reflect the shared vision of the three Heads of State
The Malian delegation stressed that completing the roadmap successfully is essential for enhancing the well-being of populations across the Confederation.
The Burkinabe delegation underlined that the process requires sacrifice, unity, consultation, and solidarity, noting:
“It is essential to act in unity, coherence, and complementarity because this is a confederation roadmap, and from this perspective, the teams from the three sister countries should come together to determine the direction they are taking.”
Next Steps
The 48-hour preparatory meeting will conclude on February 26, with the results submitted for consideration by ministers responsible for the three pillars of the AES Confederation: Defence-Security, Development, and Diplomacy.
The exercise is expected to provide a clear, actionable compass to guide the future development and cohesion of the Confederation.

excerpt_en: Koulouba, Bamako, February 26, 2026 – President of the Transition General Assimi Goïta received two newly appointed Malian ambassadors on Thursday, February 25, 2026, to provide instructions before their departure to their assigned posts abroad. The diplomats are: Major General I
body_en:
Koulouba, Bamako, February 26, 2026 – President of the Transition General Assimi Goïta received two newly appointed Malian ambassadors on Thursday, February 25, 2026, to provide instructions before their departure to their assigned posts abroad.
The diplomats are:
Major General Ibrahima Dahirou Dembélé, designated Ambassador of Mali to the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia (appointed November 5, 2025)
Colonel-Major Maouloud Ould Mohamed, designated Ambassador of Mali to Libya
Mandates and Priorities
Major General Dembélé outlined his mission focusing on:
Strengthening economic cooperation with Saudi Arabia, particularly through infrastructure projects
Consolidating security cooperation, including training, technical support, and intelligence sharing
Enhancing social, cultural, and religious ties between Mali and the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia
Colonel-Major Maouloud Ould Mohamed emphasized his priorities:
Regional security collaboration
Strengthening economic relations
Improving living conditions of Malians residing in Libya
Both ambassadors expressed gratitude for the trust placed in them and reaffirmed their determination to carry out their missions with loyalty and efficiency, representing Mali’s interests abroad.

title: Ministerial Meeting Finalizes Year II Roadmap for AES Confederation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap. The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Min
title_en: Ministerial Meeting Finalizes Year II Roadmap for AES Confederation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap. The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Min
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap.
The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs, and included:
Madina Sissoko Dembélé, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure
Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
Moussa Alassane Diallo, Minister of Industry and Trade
Focus of the Meeting
The meeting, attended by ministers responsible for the three strategic pillars of the AES Confederation, aimed to:
Consolidate institutional and operational achievements
Define future priorities for the Confederation
Align the roadmap with security, political, and economic objectives
Progress and Leadership
During the opening ceremony, Heads of Delegation from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger highlighted the significant progress made since the Confederation’s establishment. They attributed these achievements to strengthened coordination and the shared vision of the member states, emphasizing the leadership of Presidents Ibrahim Traoré, Assimi Goïta, and Abdourahamane Tiani.
The Year II Roadmap, which will be submitted for adoption by the Heads of State, is designed to sustainably strengthen integration, sovereignty, and solidarity among AES member countries, building on the momentum initiated during Mali’s inaugural presidency under President Assimi Goïta.

title: ESA Foreign Ministers Engage Citizen Watchdogs to Combat Disinformation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associ
title_en: ESA Foreign Ministers Engage Citizen Watchdogs to Combat Disinformation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associ
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associations (CNAVC).
Theme and Objectives
The forum, held under the theme “The Strategic Role of Citizen Watchdogs in Defending the Sovereignty of the ESA Region in the Face of Disinformation and the War on Information”, aimed to:
Empower citizens to counter fake news and disinformation
Protect the image and sovereignty of the AES leadership
Harmonize responsible civic engagement across member states
According to Labidi Naba, general rapporteur of the forum, the event addresses the need to restructure, frame, and harmonize civic participation to support political action and defend the Confederation from external influence.
Participation and Key Messages
The meeting was chaired by H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso, and attended by H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangare of Niger and H.E. Abdoulaye Diop of Mali.
The ministers emphasized:
Citizen mobilization as a key political asset to support ongoing AES actions and thwart destabilization efforts (Bakary Yaou Sangare)
The importance of information and communication technologies to promote cultural values and support governments (Abdoulaye Diop)
The need for a change in mindset and unity among citizens to highlight AES successes and counter disinformation (Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré)
Outcome and Next Steps
The forum concludes on Saturday, February 28, at the Thomas Sankara Memorial, with the drafting of:
The Citizen Vigilance Charter
A roadmap to guide future actions
The initiative reflects a growing focus on active citizen vigilance as a tool to protect sovereignty, strengthen regional unity, and counter information warfare across the ESA Confederation.

Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associations (CNAVC).
Theme and Objectives
The forum, held under the theme “The Strategic Role of Citizen Watchdogs in Defending the Sovereignty of the ESA Region in the Face of Disinformation and the War on Information”, aimed to:
Empower citizens to counter fake news and disinformation
Protect the image and sovereignty of the AES leadership
Harmonize responsible civic engagement across member states
According to Labidi Naba, general rapporteur of the forum, the event addresses the need to restructure, frame, and harmonize civic participation to support political action and defend the Confederation from external influence.
Participation and Key Messages
The meeting was chaired by H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso, and attended by H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangare of Niger and H.E. Abdoulaye Diop of Mali.
The ministers emphasized:
Citizen mobilization as a key political asset to support ongoing AES actions and thwart destabilization efforts (Bakary Yaou Sangare)
The importance of information and communication technologies to promote cultural values and support governments (Abdoulaye Diop)
The need for a change in mindset and unity among citizens to highlight AES successes and counter disinformation (Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré)
Outcome and Next Steps
The forum concludes on Saturday, February 28, at the Thomas Sankara Memorial, with the drafting of:
The Citizen Vigilance Charter
A roadmap to guide future actions
The initiative reflects a growing focus on active citizen vigilance as a tool to protect sovereignty, strengthen regional unity, and counter information warfare across the ESA Confederation.

excerpt_en: Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Mali has announced a new policy for public procurement, emphasizing national products and local companies, according to a government directive issued this month. The Ministry of Economy and Finance, led by Minister Alousseïni Sanou, issued a memo on Fe
body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Mali has announced a new policy for public procurement, emphasizing national products and local companies, according to a government directive issued this month.
The Ministry of Economy and Finance, led by Minister Alousseïni Sanou, issued a memo on February 13, 2026, instructing all officials handling public contracts to prioritize Malian companies and products manufactured within the country.
Supporting SMEs and National Production
The decision aligns with a national decree guiding public procurement towards small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and supporting domestic production under Malian law.
Officials noted that the measure also follows recommendations from a government meeting held on February 11, 2026, aimed at promoting economic sovereignty, local industry, and the growth of national businesses.
This new approach signals Mali’s commitment to strengthening the domestic economy while ensuring that public spending benefits local enterprises.

title: Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Launched: 600 Tons of Rice Donated to Vulnerable Communities
excerpt: Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on behalf of Transitional President General Assimi Goïta, launched Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Friday, delivering 600 tons of rice to vulnerable populations across Bamako and the regions. The launch
title_en: Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Launched: 600 Tons of Rice Donated to Vulnerable Communities
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on behalf of Transitional President General Assimi Goïta, launched Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Friday, delivering 600 tons of rice to vulnerable populations across Bamako and the regions. The launch
body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on behalf of Transitional President General Assimi Goïta, launched Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Friday, delivering 600 tons of rice to vulnerable populations across Bamako and the regions.
The launch took place at the ASKO football field in Korofina, Commune I of Bamako District, marking the start of a nationwide social assistance campaign coordinated by the government.
Distribution Across the Country
The initiative is set to operate at multiple locations:
19 sites in Bamako
4 sites in Kati
3 sites per region in other areas of the country
Of the total 600 tons of rice, 400 tons are allocated to the regions, while 200 tons will support three key ministerial departments, ensuring assistance reaches those most in need.
A Commitment to Solidarity
Government officials described the operation as a demonstration of national solidarity, aiming to support vulnerable populations, strengthen social cohesion, and promote a spirit of communal assistance during challenging times.

Bamako, February 16, 2026 – Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga conducted visits Thursday to key storage facilities for essential goods, as part of efforts to guarantee availability and accessibility of critical products for the Malian population.

Warehouses Stocked with Essential Goods
At the Mamadou Diarra S.A. warehouses, the Prime Minister observed stocks of:
15,000 tons of sugar
45,000 tons of rice

body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, announced that the launch of Mali’s e-Justice platform has been postponed, following administrative requirements needed to ensure secure digital access for all citizens.
The announcement comes after the inaugural digital issuance of criminal records and nationality certificates, which was celebrated on February 10, 2026, as part of the 4th edition of Justice Week at the Ministry of Justice.
Reasons for the Delay
Officials explained that the delay is due to essential administrative formalities required to guarantee:
Secure digital access for Malians at home and abroad
Proper functionality and protection of sensitive legal documents
The official launch date and details on access and usage will be communicated in a future press release.
Public Advisory
The Minister of Justice urged the public to remain vigilant and cautious, warning against misinformation or unauthorized initiatives that could compromise the integrity of the digital services.
Authorities emphasized that the postponement is intended to ensure a safe, reliable, and fully operational e-Justice platform for the nation.

Kidal, February 18, 2026 – The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM) announced that it targeted a military vehicle carrying Malian army personnel and Russian mercenaries with a landmine near Tiskdouine, on the outskirts of Aguelhok, on Wednesday evening, February 18, 2026.
According to reports, the explosion killed six militia members affiliated with General El Hadj Ag Gamou, including the son of the sub-prefect of Tajamert, who was serving as acting prefect of Aguelhok.
Details of the Attack
The victims were escorting a convoy of Russian mercenaries tasked with securing logistical supplies. Local sources indicate that several of the deceased had previously been implicated in the deaths of dozens of civilians in the same area.
The incident underscores the persistent threats posed by armed groups in the Kidal region and highlights the risks faced by militias and foreign personnel operating in conflict zones.

title_en: Idaksahak Leaders Hold Community Meeting Supporting ALF Ideals
excerpt_en: Tinzaoutene, February 17–19, 2026 – Political, religious, and traditional leaders of the Idaksahak community convened in Tinzaoutene for a three-day meeting focused on social cohesion, neighborly relations, and mobilization in support of the Azawad Liberation Front (ALF). Key Out
body_en:
Tinzaoutene, February 17–19, 2026 – Political, religious, and traditional leaders of the Idaksahak community convened in Tinzaoutene for a three-day meeting focused on social cohesion, neighborly relations, and mobilization in support of the Azawad Liberation Front (ALF).
Key Outcomes of the Meeting
Creation of a monitoring and awareness committee composed of religious scholars and faction leaders
Several community leaders formally joining the ALF, including Mahmoudane Ag Mohama and Jaddi Ag Wataya
Rejection of any misuse of the Idaksahak name for conflict-related purposes
The leaders also expressed gratitude to sister communities and local youth for organizing the event, emphasizing the importance of unity, responsible leadership, and community engagement in advancing the group’s objectives.

title: Deliberate Destruction of Water Points and Worsening Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries. Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nom
title_en: Deliberate Destruction of Water Points and Worsening Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries. Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nom
body_en:
Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries.
Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nomadic settlements, these forces are systematically destroying water sources used by civilian populations. Previously, poisoning water points with barrels of acid and other harmful substances was reported; now, reports indicate the outright destruction of the few remaining functional water infrastructure.
A new incident was recorded on Friday, February 27, 2026, in the Efali nomadic settlement, about 20 kilometers northeast of Tessalit, during Ramadan. Residents claim that the destruction of water points is intended to suffocate local communities, expose them to thirst, and force displacement, aggravating an already severe humanitarian situation in northern Mali.
Conclusion
The second half of February 2026 reflects a Mali navigating a dual reality: a government actively asserting its sovereignty and regional leadership, while simultaneously facing a volatile security environment and worsening humanitarian concerns.
Strategic Sovereignty and Diplomacy
Mali has reinforced its “Mali-first” approach through the formalization of the AES Confederation Year II Roadmap, which prioritizes defense, diplomacy, and development independent of traditional Western frameworks. While the government maintains engagement with the European Union and the United Kingdom, it is pivoting decisively toward strategic partnerships with Saudi Arabia, China, and Iran.
Domestically, this orientation is reflected in new economic directives favoring local products and national companies in public procurement, signaling a push for economic self-reliance and support for Malian enterprises. Initiatives like Operation Sunkalo Solidarity 2026 further underscore the government’s emphasis on social cohesion, national unity, and community support.
Persistent Security and Humanitarian Friction
Despite these political and diplomatic strides, security challenges remain severe. The Mopti and Kidal regions continue to be flashpoints for asymmetric warfare, with JNIM and Islamic State – Sahel Province conducting frequent ambushes, IED attacks, and targeted operations against Malian forces and Russian mercenaries.
Compounding this, reports of water point destruction, abductions, and other human rights violations in northern Mali signal a deepening humanitarian crisis. These developments threaten the impact of national initiatives like Sunkalo Solidarity and underscore the fragile state of civilian protection in conflict-affected regions.
Looking Ahead
The trajectory of Mali’s transitional government will depend on whether the institutional consolidation of the AES Confederation can translate into tangible stability and security for populations in the northern and central regions, while maintaining social cohesion and advancing economic self-reliance.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

title: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Says UN Has Failed to Learn from Past Genocides
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulne
title_en: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Says UN Has Failed to Learn from Past Genocides
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulne
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulnerable communities decades after the Holocaust and the Genocide against the Tutsi.
Speaking at the 81st commemoration of the Genocide against Jews at the Kigali Genocide Memorial, Nduhungirehe said that despite global vows of “never again,” mass atrocities have continued. “In 1945, the whole world said it would never happen again, but it happened again 49 years later in Rwanda,” he said, referring to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. “Even today, 32 years later, Tutsi and Mulenge communities in eastern DRC are still being targeted because of their identity.”
He questioned whether the UN has truly learned from the genocides in Europe and Rwanda, arguing that hate speech and violence continue to be ignored in parts of the region.
The ceremony brought together international organizations, members of the Jewish community in Rwanda, diplomats, and senior Rwandan officials. It marked the annual remembrance of the Holocaust, in which more than six million Jews were killed under Nazi rule.
Israel’s Ambassador to Rwanda, Einat Weiss, reflected on the shared histories of Israel and Rwanda, describing humanity as a mix of great good and profound evil. He acknowledged the persistence of Holocaust denial and distortion but praised Rwanda for its approach to remembrance, justice, reconciliation, and reconstruction.
The UN Resident Coordinator in Rwanda, Ozonnia Ojielo, called for stronger international cooperation to combat hate speech and punish those who trivialize genocide, stressing that the principle of ntibizongere (“never again”) must be implemented, not merely repeated.
German Ambassador Heike Uta Dettmann noted that while Jews rebuilt their lives in Germany after the Holocaust, antisemitism continues to surface worldwide, calling it shameful and urging stronger action against hatred.

title: MPs Call for Pensioner Representation on RSSB Board
excerpt: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Mi
title_en: MPs Call for Pensioner Representation on RSSB Board
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Mi
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Yusuf Murangwa, on a report by the Auditor General reviewing RSSB’s performance over the past 10 years.
MP Yvonne Mujawabega emphasized that the board of directors of insurance institutions should include representatives for all stakeholders, including employees, employers, and the government, to ensure that the interests of members are reflected in investment and policy decisions. She raised concerns about past pension contribution increases, noting that some employees and employers were surprised by the changes and questioned how members’ voices are represented.
MP Mukabunani Christine noted that while RSSB invests to generate profits, there are times when projects may not be profitable. She questioned whether increased contributions translate into higher benefits for members, including medical care coverage and pension payouts, and whether these benefits keep pace with rising living costs.
Minister Yusuf Murangwa explained that the increase in contributions was necessary and had been delayed due to Covid-19 and rising prices. The decision had been under study for nearly eight years, and consultations were held prior to approval. He stressed that RSSB’s primary role is to manage members’ contributions efficiently and generate profits, with oversight from MINECOFIN.
On governance, Minister Murangwa acknowledged a gap and stated that the RSSB board should be reformed to include capable representatives of all members, including pensioners. “It is time to reform the RSSB Board of Directors… we hope that as the years go by, it will improve,” he said.
Murangwa also noted that RSSB is financially stable, contrary to some beliefs, and contributes significantly to the national economy, even supporting key development projects in the country.

title: Rwanda Announces 20th National Dialogue Conference for February 2026
excerpt: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has announced that the 20th National Dialogue Conference will be held on February 5–6, 2026, according to decisions from a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on January 28. The Cabinet confirmed it had been briefed
title_en: Rwanda Announces 20th National Dialogue Conference for February 2026
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has announced that the 20th National Dialogue Conference will be held on February 5–6, 2026, according to decisions from a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on January 28. The Cabinet confirmed it had been briefed
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has announced that the 20th National Dialogue Conference will be held on February 5–6, 2026, according to decisions from a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on January 28.
The Cabinet confirmed it had been briefed on preparations for the event, which serves as a national platform bringing together Rwandans at home and abroad to discuss the country’s development, assess progress in improving citizens’ well-being, and hold leaders accountable for their actions.
The conference focuses on evaluating national performance, identifying challenges across key sectors, and shaping policies aimed at sustainable development.
The last National Dialogue Conference was held on January 23–24, 2024, and was inaugurated by President Kagame. It drew participants from across the country and the diaspora, with gatherings in locations such as Kigali, Gatsibo, Rutsiro, Burera, Nyanza, and Poland.
At that time, President Kagame reaffirmed that Rwanda was secure and called on citizens—especially the youth—to take the lead in advancing national development. He emphasized that Rwanda’s future must be shaped first and foremost by Rwandans themselves, urging unity, responsibility, and self-reflection as the foundation of national progress.
