title_en: Burundi Ombudsman Says She Is Being Threatened for Exposing Illegal Activities
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 28, 2026 — Burundi’s Ombudsman, Aimée-Laurentine Kanyana, has told the National Assembly that powerful individuals are threatening her in an effort to obstruct her work and silence her for exposing illegal activities. Addressing lawmakers, Kanyana said those be
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 28, 2026 — Burundi’s Ombudsman, Aimée-Laurentine Kanyana, has told the National Assembly that powerful individuals are threatening her in an effort to obstruct her work and silence her for exposing illegal activities.
Addressing lawmakers, Kanyana said those behind the pressure would have arrested her if they could. “The problem is that they do not arrest the Ombudsman, otherwise there would be people who would have arrested her,” she stated.
In response, National Assembly Speaker Daniel Gélase Ndabirabe urged parliamentarians to support Kanyana so she can continue her duties without intimidation.
Her remarks come amid broader concerns over pressure on public officials. On December 28, 2025, Finance Minister Alain Ndikumana told the Senate that the management of the fertilizer company FOMI was intimidating him after the government refused to grant more than 50 billion Burundian francs not предусмотр in its contract.
Ndikumana said he would continue his work despite the pressure, stressing the need for responsible public spending. Senate President Gervais Ndirakobuca pledged legislative support, saying lawmakers would help confront corruption and defend those who speak the truth.

title: Rwanda Urges UN to Enforce International Law Equally for All Countries
excerpt: New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by S
title_en: Rwanda Urges UN to Enforce International Law Equally for All Countries
excerpt_en: New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by S
body_en:
New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by Somalia on international law enforcement.
Ambassador Ngoga stressed that international law exists, but its enforcement is inconsistent. “The collapse of respect for the law did not start yesterday… principles were respected only when necessary,” he said, highlighting that serious violations are often ignored when committed by influential states, while developing nations are punished disproportionately.
He criticized the council for delaying action even when civilians are dying and for failing to prevent ethnic persecution, stating, “Violations of international humanitarian law are discussed rather than condemned. Silence and discrimination destroy trust faster than any weapon.”
Ngoga emphasized that security concerns of all states must be taken seriously, regardless of size or power. “Selective enforcement… undermines the credibility of this institution. The question is not whether the rule of law is necessary, but whether we want to enforce it equally for all countries, large and small,” he said.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres acknowledged that powerful countries often dictate what is considered acceptable, particularly during conflicts and divisions, creating a “wall” that influences international law selectively.
Ambassador Ngoga concluded that for international law to be effective, regional and international organizations must cooperate, and UN agencies need stronger coordination to ensure equal enforcement across all countries.

body_en:
Kigali, January 29, 2026 — Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe reminded the European Parliament that it has no jurisdiction over Rwanda, stressing that the country will not accept external directives or interference in its judicial affairs.
He stated that Rwanda will not tolerate the arrogance and interference of EU lawmakers, particularly regarding cases before Rwandese courts. His remarks followed an EU Parliament statement issued on January 28, after members received Rémy Amahirwa, son of opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, who is currently detained and on trial in Rwanda.
The minister emphasized that Rwanda is not an EU member and has been independent from European colonialism for over 60 years. Meanwhile, Justice Minister Emmanuel Ugirashebuja told the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on January 21 that Rwanda continues to make progress in human rights, adding that the justice system is functioning transparently.
Rwandan authorities also recalled that the Rwandan Parliament previously condemned EU calls for the release of Ingabire and others, reaffirming the country’s sovereignty and judicial independence.

title_en: Gnassingbé Arrives in Rwanda to Advance Mediation Efforts in DRC Conflict
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 30, 2026 — The Prime Minister of Togo, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, arrived in Rwanda on the night of January 29, 2026, for an official visit. He was received by Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe. Gnassingbé, who has visited Rwanda on sever
body_en:
Kigali, January 30, 2026 — The Prime Minister of Togo, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, arrived in Rwanda on the night of January 29, 2026, for an official visit. He was received by Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe.
Gnassingbé, who has visited Rwanda on several occasions, last met with President Paul Kagame in April 2025, shortly after being appointed by the African Union (AU) as mediator in the conflict between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
The visit aims to reinforce his commitment to working with regional and international stakeholders to achieve a lasting solution to the crisis in eastern DRC. Discussions focused on the progress of regional peace talks and efforts to stabilize the region.
On March 24, 2025, Angola announced that President João Lourenço would step down as mediator in the DRC–Rwanda conflict to concentrate on continental initiatives. He subsequently proposed Gnassingbé as his successor, a move later endorsed by the African Union.
In early April 2025, the AU supported the proposal, and on April 12, 2025, the AU General Assembly unanimously appointed Gnassingbé as mediator between Rwanda and the DRC.
Gnassingbé has since made several visits to Rwanda to discuss security, regional stability, and African cooperation. He also traveled to Kigali in January 2025 for a two-day working visit, during which both countries agreed to deepen bilateral cooperation.
Relations between Rwanda and the DRC have deteriorated in recent years due to the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC. Kinshasa accuses Rwanda of supporting the AFC/M23 alliance, while Rwanda accuses the DRC of backing the FDLR, a group linked to perpetrators of the 1994 genocide against the Tutsi.
Recently, the African Union reduced the mandate of mediators in the eastern DRC conflict. This decision followed a security meeting held in Lomé, Togo, from January 16 to 17, 2026.
The mediation process is currently led by Prime Minister Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, supported by a team from Togo’s Ministry of Foreign Affairs and his office.

excerpt_en: Kampala, January 30, 2026 — Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has issued an apology to the United States following remarks he made targeting the U.S. Embassy in Kampala, which he later said were based on false information. Gen Muhoozi, who is also the son
body_en:
Kampala, January 30, 2026 — Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has issued an apology to the United States following remarks he made targeting the U.S. Embassy in Kampala, which he later said were based on false information.
Gen Muhoozi, who is also the son of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, had earlier posted on social media accusing the U.S. Embassy of helping opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, to flee the country. He also announced a suspension of military cooperation with the United States, including joint operations in Somalia.
Bobi Wine was last seen at his home on the night of January 15–16, 2026, shortly after the presidential election, when security forces reportedly attempted to arrest him but he escaped. On January 29, he said publicly that no soldier knew his whereabouts and challenged Gen Muhoozi, saying, “Catch me if you can.”
Later the same day, Gen Muhoozi retracted his earlier statements, acknowledging that the claims were incorrect.
“I would like to apologize to our great friends, the United States of America, for the earlier message I deleted. I was misinformed. I spoke to the U.S. Ambassador to our country and everything is fine. We will continue our military cooperation as usual,” he said.
Gen Muhoozi further explained that Uganda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Adonia Ayebare, played a key role in resolving the misunderstanding and praised him for his swift diplomatic intervention, suggesting he be appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs.

title_en: Rwanda and Egypt Hold Talks to Strengthen Water Sector Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 30, 2026 — Egypt’s Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Prof. Hani Sewilam, is in Rwanda for high-level talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in the water sector and the management of natural water resources. Prof. Sewilam arrived in Kigali on
body_en:
Kigali, January 30, 2026 — Egypt’s Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Prof. Hani Sewilam, is in Rwanda for high-level talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in the water sector and the management of natural water resources.
Prof. Sewilam arrived in Kigali on Thursday, January 29, 2026, and is scheduled to meet with Rwanda’s Minister of Environment, Dr. Bernadette Arapu, and the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Dr. Ndabamenye Telesphore, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Water Resources.
The Egyptian official and his Rwandan counterparts are also expected to attend the closing ceremony of the Rwanda–Egypt Joint Steering Group meeting and visit various sites earmarked for the implementation of joint projects.
Officials said the discussions aim to provide practical solutions through knowledge-sharing, capacity building, and support for the execution of bilateral initiatives.
In September 2025, Rwanda and Egypt signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) during President Paul Kagame’s visit to Egypt, covering areas such as water management, investment promotion, land exchange, and urban and housing development.
The two countries maintain strong ties across several sectors, including trade and investment, health, defense, infrastructure, and education.

title_en: Denis Mukwege Emerges as Potential Challenger to Mushikiwabo for OIF Leadership
excerpt_en: February 2, 2026 — Congolese-born Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege is emerging as a leading contender to challenge Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda for the post of Secretary General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Following Rwanda’s announceme
body_en:
February 2, 2026 — Congolese-born Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege is emerging as a leading contender to challenge Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda for the post of Secretary General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF).
Following Rwanda’s announcement last month that it would nominate Mushikiwabo for a third term, the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has intensified efforts to put forward a rival candidate.
Initially, the DRC considered Isidore Kwandja Ngembo, an OIF observer involved in election monitoring and the organization of the 2023 Francophonie Games in Kinshasa. However, after a final decision was taken on January 30, 2026, two additional names emerged as potential challengers.
Dr. Mukwege, founder of Panzi Hospital in Bukavu and internationally renowned for his work treating survivors of sexual violence, has become the most prominent figure under consideration. Although he opposed President Félix Tshisekedi during the 2023 presidential campaign, reports indicate the two have since entered into dialogue and are expected to meet in New York in September 2025.
Another candidate being considered is Freddy Matungulu, former Minister of Finance (2001–2003) and former official at both the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the African Development Bank (AfDB).

title: U.S. Government Offices Close in Burundi Amid Federal Shutdown
excerpt: Bujumbura — February 2, 2026 — The United States Embassy in Burundi announced that several U.S. government offices in the country will be closed due to the ongoing federal government shutdown in Washington. In a statement published on February 2, the embassy said: “U.S. offices w
title_en: U.S. Government Offices Close in Burundi Amid Federal Shutdown
excerpt_en: Bujumbura — February 2, 2026 — The United States Embassy in Burundi announced that several U.S. government offices in the country will be closed due to the ongoing federal government shutdown in Washington. In a statement published on February 2, the embassy said: “U.S. offices w
body_en:
Bujumbura — February 2, 2026 — The United States Embassy in Burundi announced that several U.S. government offices in the country will be closed due to the ongoing federal government shutdown in Washington.
In a statement published on February 2, the embassy said: “U.S. offices will be closed starting February 3, 2026, until further notice regarding the government shutdown.”
The closure does not affect the U.S. Embassy, which will continue to operate normally. However, the shutdown impacts U.S.-run libraries, cultural centers, and other affiliated facilities.
The embassy also indicated that routine announcements on its social media platforms will be reduced to essential updates only, in line with guidance issued to U.S. diplomatic missions across Africa.
The shutdown stems from a failure in Congress to pass the budget for several federal departments, amid disputes over immigration policy and the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).
The standoff intensified following protests in Minneapolis after two civilians were killed by Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents.
Democrats have called for ICE reform, while Republicans argue existing immigration laws should remain in force. The budget impasse resulted in funding lapses, forcing some departments to suspend operations.
This follows the end-of-2025 shutdown, which halted government operations for 43 days, the longest shutdown in U.S. history.

title_en: President Kiir Appoints Deceased Candidate to Election Team
excerpt_en: Juba South Sudan , 4 February 2026 – President Salva Kiir of South Sudan has caused a political stir by appointing a presidential election team member who had been dead for five years. On 30 January 2026, a decree named Steward Soroba Budia, a former member of the opposition Unit
body_en:
Juba South Sudan , 4 February 2026 – President Salva Kiir of South Sudan has caused a political stir by appointing a presidential election team member who had been dead for five years.
On 30 January 2026, a decree named Steward Soroba Budia, a former member of the opposition United Democratic Party (UDP), to oversee preparations for the December 2026 presidential election. However, it was later revealed that Budia had passed away five years ago.
The announcement triggered widespread social media ridicule. Following the revelation, Kiir fired David Amour Major, former presidential press secretary, and Chief of Staff Valentino Dhel Maluet, citing errors in relying on collaborators for appointments.
A statement from President Kiir’s office expressed gratitude for their work while confirming their dismissal.
Budia had been a key figure in the 2018 peace agreement, which aimed to end the post-independence fighting in South Sudan that began in 2011.

title: Obasanjo Urges Root-Level Solutions to Congo Crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up. Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 Feb
title_en: Obasanjo Urges Root-Level Solutions to Congo Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up. Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 Feb
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up.
Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 February 2026, Obasanjo emphasized that the ongoing crisis in the DRC stems from mismanagement of internal conflicts and tensions with neighboring countries.
Reflecting on his first visit to the Congo in 1960, during the Katanga independence struggle led by Moïse Tshombe, Obasanjo said, “The problem that led to the UN peacekeeping mission in Leopoldville in 1960 is still here today. Understanding the problem properly is the first step toward solving it.”
He stressed that previous attempts, particularly those led from Washington, failed because the root causes were not addressed, and that a comprehensive African-led approach is necessary. Obasanjo added that while international partners like Washington, Qatar, and France can contribute, the solution must be driven by Africans.
President Museveni noted that the current situation in the DRC is less severe than during Tshombe’s era, as there is no desire among Congolese provinces for independence. He called for leveraging the support of AU mediators to achieve lasting peace.

title_en: New Economic Partnership Signed
excerpt_en: Rwanda-Brazil, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda and Brazil have formalized a strategic partnership to boost trade, investment, and sectoral cooperation. The agreement was signed during the ‘Rwanda-Brazil Economic Cooperation Forum’. Rwanda was represented by Jean-Guy Afrika, Director Gen
body_en:
Rwanda-Brazil, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda and Brazil have formalized a strategic partnership to boost trade, investment, and sectoral cooperation. The agreement was signed during the ‘Rwanda-Brazil Economic Cooperation Forum’.
Rwanda was represented by Jean-Guy Afrika, Director General of the National Development Board (RDB), while Brazil was represented by Jorge Viana of its Export Promotion Agency (APEX-Brazil).
The deal sets a clear framework for trade promotion, investment facilitation, trade-related travel, and sectoral collaboration. Additionally, APEX-Brazil signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Private Sector Federation, led by Stephen Ruzibiza, to further strengthen private sector engagement.
Jean-Guy Afrika highlighted the complementary strengths of the two nations: Brazil with its leadership in agriculture, industry, and energy, and Rwanda offering a safe investment environment and strategic access to East and Central African markets.
Brazilian Ambassador Irene Vida Gala encouraged Brazilian investors to explore opportunities in Rwanda, calling the agreement a major step in bilateral cooperation.
Rwanda-Brazil relations date back to 1981, with agreements on air services (2019) and food security (2011). Since 2022, Rwanda has imported wheat and sugar from Brazil, replacing some imports from Ukraine.
The partnership aims to expand trade and investment while reinforcing the private sector and sustainable economic growth in both countries.

title: Rwanda Recognized Globally for Excellence in Government Services
excerpt: Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) i
title_en: Rwanda Recognized Globally for Excellence in Government Services
excerpt_en: Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) i
body_en:
Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) in Dubai, UAE.
The award-winning initiative is the IremboGov platform, developed by the Irembo company, which has significantly enhanced citizens’ access to government services through digital technology.
The Rwandan Ambassador to the UAE, John Mirenge, accepted the award on behalf of the government, alongside Estelle Kayitesi, Director General for Policy and Partnerships at Irembo.
The WGS, established in 2013, convenes government leaders, sector experts, and the private sector to address governance challenges and explore emerging technologies for effective service delivery. The 2026 summit brought together participants from 150 countries.
The GovTech Prize honors government agencies that innovatively improve service delivery through technology. Over the past decade, thousands of applications from 126 countries have competed for this recognition.
Since its launch in 2015, IremboGov now offers over 240 services, enabling citizens to access government services remotely, without physically visiting offices. Monthly, the platform processes over 500,000 requests, with 80% of services paid electronically.
Rwanda’s digital government expansion is supported by growing internet and mobile access. According to the National Institute of Statistics (NISR), over 12 million Rwandans own and use phones, and nine million access the internet, while in 2024, approximately 680 government services were available digitally.
This recognition underscores Rwanda’s leadership in leveraging technology for citizen-centric governance.

title: DRC Minister Urges Banyamulenge to Visit Government-Controlled Areas Amid Tensions
excerpt: 5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being kill
title_en: DRC Minister Urges Banyamulenge to Visit Government-Controlled Areas Amid Tensions
excerpt_en: 5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being kill
body_en:
5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being killed.
The announcement follows a meeting on 4 February 2025 in Washington D.C., United States, where DRC Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya met with Congolese Tutsi, predominantly Banyamulenge. The meeting, widely publicized, aimed to deny reports of atrocities committed in Minembwe since 2017.
According to Muyaya, representatives including Me Emile Muhizi stated that the AFC/M23 opposes the DRC government, and that Rwanda allegedly seeks to unite them with other Congolese. They pledged to continue denouncing AFC/M23 actions.
Minister Nduhungirehe emphasized that media campaigns alone are insufficient, stating:"The meeting in nice rooms in Washington that was advertised in the media is good, but these people visiting areas controlled by the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and FDNB, unaccompanied, would be better."
The Mahoro Peace Association (MPA), representing Banyamulenge in the United States, criticized the meeting, asserting that Muhizi and his colleagues are not elected representatives. The MPA, led by President Douglas G. Kabunda, stated:"These individuals who were selected, not elected, met with Minister Muyaya on their own. What they said has nothing to do with the position of the Banyamulenge Community living in the United States and has nothing to do with our elected institutions."
Muhizi and colleagues claimed that allegations of mistreatment of the Banyamulenge are false. However, tensions with Wazalendo groups, led by Gen. William Amuri Yakutumba and John Makanaki, continue, as they regard the Banyamulenge as Rwandans who should leave the DRC.
Hatred toward the Banyamulenge has escalated in South Kivu and North Kivu. In September 2025, Wazalendo fighters expelled Brig Gen Olivier Gasita from Uvira, labeling him a Tutsi, Rwandan, and enemy, giving the community 10 days to leave. In January 2026, Habyarimana Mbitse (alias Jules Mulumba), speaking for Wazalendo, attacked Lt Gen Pacifique Masunzu, calling him a traitor despite his service to the DRC government after separating from forces supporting the Banyamulenge.
The situation underscores ongoing tensions between the Banyamulenge, Wazalendo, and the DRC government, highlighting deep-rooted mistrust and security concerns in the eastern provinces.

The announcement follows a meeting on 4 February 2025 in Washington D.C., United States, where DRC Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya met with Congolese Tutsi, predominantly Banyamulenge. The meeting, widely publicized, aimed to deny reports of atrocities committed in Minembwe since 2017.
According to Muyaya, representatives including Me Emile Muhizi stated that the AFC/M23 opposes the DRC government, and that Rwanda allegedly seeks to unite them with other Congolese. They pledged to continue denouncing AFC/M23 actions.
Minister Nduhungirehe emphasized that media campaigns alone are insufficient, stating:"The meeting in nice rooms in Washington that was advertised in the media is good, but these people visiting areas controlled by the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and FDNB, unaccompanied, would be better."
The Mahoro Peace Association (MPA), representing Banyamulenge in the United States, criticized the meeting, asserting that Muhizi and his colleagues are not elected representatives. The MPA, led by President Douglas G. Kabunda, stated:"These individuals who were selected, not elected, met with Minister Muyaya on their own. What they said has nothing to do with the position of the Banyamulenge Community living in the United States and has nothing to do with our elected institutions."
Muhizi and colleagues claimed that allegations of mistreatment of the Banyamulenge are false. However, tensions with Wazalendo groups, led by Gen. William Amuri Yakutumba and John Makanaki, continue, as they regard the Banyamulenge as Rwandans who should leave the DRC.
Hatred toward the Banyamulenge has escalated in South Kivu and North Kivu. In September 2025, Wazalendo fighters expelled Brig Gen Olivier Gasita from Uvira, labeling him a Tutsi, Rwandan, and enemy, giving the community 10 days to leave. In January 2026, Habyarimana Mbitse (alias Jules Mulumba), speaking for Wazalendo, attacked Lt Gen Pacifique Masunzu, calling him a traitor despite his service to the DRC government after separating from forces supporting the Banyamulenge.
The situation underscores ongoing tensions between the Banyamulenge, Wazalendo, and the DRC government, highlighting deep-rooted mistrust and security concerns in the eastern provinces.

title: Congolese Lawyers Move to Halt DRC-US Mineral Deal
excerpt: February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States. The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American in
title_en: Congolese Lawyers Move to Halt DRC-US Mineral Deal
excerpt_en: February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States. The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American in
body_en:
February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States.
The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American investors to control several mineral mines in the DRC in exchange for US support in building the country’s security forces.
Earlier, on December 24, 2025, Catholic Bishop Fulgence Muteba criticized the agreement, calling it a mortgage of the country’s natural resources. Speaking to Catholics in Lubumbashi, he said:"Did you know that we signed a 99-year agreement to exploit natural resources? Precious minerals will not last forever. How can someone mortgage a country's resources for 99 years?"
Following President Donald Trump’s announcement that the US would support peace in the DRC and invest in mining, the DRC government sent a list of mines to Washington D.C. in mid-January 2026 for American inspection.
In the January 2026 lawsuit, the lawyers argued that the agreement:
Violates the Constitution, as it required Parliamentary approval or a popular vote before signing.
Undermines the country’s sovereignty over natural resources.
Contravenes the principle of equality before the law.
Lawyer Jean-Marie Kalonji, one of the plaintiffs, said: "By filing this lawsuit with the Constitutional Court, we are fulfilling our obligations as Congolese to protect the sovereignty of our country and preserve our resources for future generations."
The Oakland Institute, a US-based organization advocating for property rights, expressed support for the lawsuit, calling it well-founded and pledging to continue assisting the plaintiffs.
This legal challenge marks a significant escalation in debates over the DRC’s mineral wealth, foreign investment, and national sovereignty, placing Tshisekedi’s government under intense scrutiny.

title: Gen Muhoozi Clashes with Ugandan Communications Minister

title_en: Gen Muhoozi Clashes with Ugandan Communications Minister
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda – February 5, 2026 – Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Defence Staff and son of President Yoweri Museveni, has publicly criticized the country’s Communications Minister, Dr. Chris Baryomunsi, over remarks about his social media activity. The dispute erupted after
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda – February 5, 2026 – Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Defence Staff and son of President Yoweri Museveni, has publicly criticized the country’s Communications Minister, Dr. Chris Baryomunsi, over remarks about his social media activity.
The dispute erupted after Dr. Baryomunsi revealed that he had informed President Museveni that Gen Muhoozi’s posts on X (formerly Twitter) were interfering with his duties as Government Spokesperson.
Baryomunsi defended his stance, explaining that Gen Muhoozi’s social media posts are often jokes, not official statements, saying: "The Chief of Defence Staff does not speak on behalf of the Government of Uganda, but he likes to use X. He writes messages, deletes them, and I hope Ugandans have already made up their minds about what he writes."
The statement reportedly angered Gen Muhoozi, who responded publicly on X:"Baryomunsi, you traitor, I will never be a Minister again."
Baryomunsi replied firmly: "I have come a long way to where I am because of my own abilities, not because of anyone’s gifts. I am a self-made man. Being a Minister is not the best thing in life. My goals are much higher than that. Let’s serve Uganda. Thank you."
The feud continued online, with Gen Muhoozi demanding an apology and reconciliation, while Baryomunsi defended his independence and work ethic, stating: "My father taught me to believe in myself. He gave me freedom and I don’t suffer from Peter Pan Syndrome. Those who criticize X don’t know what we, the true Kikes, are going through. Go away a little."
This public clash highlights growing tensions within the upper echelons of Uganda’s government and the challenges posed by social media in official communications.

excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda – February 5, 2026 – President Paul Kagame opened the 20th Umushyikirano Conference, a national forum aimed at sharing ideas, solving problems, and guiding Rwandans. In his address, Kagame called on leaders to fulfill their responsibilities and warned that those wh

excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda – February 5, 2026 – President Paul Kagame opened the 20th Umushyikirano Conference, a national forum aimed at sharing ideas, solving problems, and guiding Rwandans. In his address, Kagame called on leaders to fulfill their responsibilities and warned that those wh
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda – February 5, 2026 – President Paul Kagame opened the 20th Umushyikirano Conference, a national forum aimed at sharing ideas, solving problems, and guiding Rwandans. In his address, Kagame called on leaders to fulfill their responsibilities and warned that those who exceed their authority should be held accountable.
Turning to regional relations, Kagame criticized Burundi, saying that the country has broken the brotherhood traditionally shared with Rwanda by aligning itself with the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC).
He said: "As far as I knew, Rwandans and Burundians are twins, but Burundians chose to say, ‘No, we don’t want you to be twins anymore, we want to be twins with Congolese.’ I have no problem with it if someone chooses who they are born with or who they live with as a twin. I have nothing to do with that, I accept it."
Kagame added: "But being twins especially involves bad politics, a politics of self-denial and hatred of others, which they share. This is not a secret because they themselves, the leaders of those countries, are saying it. I am not inventing anything new."
He also addressed the international situation, refuting claims that Rwanda is responsible for insecurity in eastern DRC, and reaffirmed the country’s position on regional stability.
The speech comes amid growing tensions between Rwanda, Burundi, and the DRC, highlighting Kigali’s firm stance on regional diplomacy and security issues.

title: RRA Gives Vehicle Owners One Month to Complete ‘Mutation’ or Face Penalties
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscatio
title_en: RRA Gives Vehicle Owners One Month to Complete ‘Mutation’ or Face Penalties
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscatio
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscation of vehicles. The announcement was made during a joint press conference with the Rwanda National Police, which is responsible for road safety.
The campaign runs from January 26 to February 28, 2026, and aims to assist owners who acquired vehicles through purchase, inheritance, or gifts but have not transferred them to their names, as required by law within eight days of ownership change.
Improved Services for Vehicle Transfers
Deputy Commissioner for Taxation and Communications at RRA, Uwitonze Jean Paulin, said the agency has expanded services to facilitate transfers:
In Kigali, transfers are now available in Gikondo, Canal Olympia in Rebero, and Kigali Pelé Stadium in Nyamirambo, in addition to the Masaka office.
Working days have been increased from Tuesdays and Thursdays to every day except Sundays, and staff handling transfers have been increased tenfold.
Provincial offices will also provide services daily except Sundays.
So far, more than 16,000 people have applied for vehicle transfers: 3,000 with no obstacles will receive services immediately, while 10,000 must first resolve specific issues. Uwitonze emphasized that all applications will be processed and no applicant will be denied service.
Common obstacles include: the previous owner being deceased or abroad, or unresolved tax arrears, which must be cleared before the transfer. Fees for transfers are 30,000 Rwf for motorcycles and 60,000 Rwf for cars, payable by one or both parties involved.
Safety and Enforcement Concerns
National Police Spokesperson ACP Rutikanga noted that untransferred vehicles complicate traffic enforcement. Vehicles may be driven by someone other than the registered owner, making it difficult to assign responsibility for violations or fines.
He added that some drivers intentionally use unregistered vehicles, which may contribute to accidents and hinder police investigations, as drivers often flee the scene.
The RRA and National Police urged all vehicle owners to complete the mutation process promptly to avoid penalties and improve road safety.

title: NAEB Pushes to Reach $1.5 Billion in Exports by 2029
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Developme
title_en: NAEB Pushes to Reach $1.5 Billion in Exports by 2029
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Developme
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Development (NST2) and Vision 2050, according to NAEB Director General Bizimana Claude.
NAEB is working to facilitate timely export of agricultural and livestock products, focusing on market expansion, particularly in West and Central Africa. In December 2025, Rwanda signed a cooperation agreement with its Embassy in the Republic of Congo to export fruits and vegetables, following Bizimana’s working visit. The partnership also involves RwandAir, which helps address logistical challenges, including limited cargo space, ensuring products reach markets efficiently.
On January 21, 2026, 17 tons of Rwandan fruits and vegetables were shipped directly to Congo-Brazzaville, demonstrating improved coordination between government institutions and embassies to reduce transit delays, prevent losses, and increase foreign exchange earnings.
Bizimana emphasized the role of cold storage in processing, preserving, and consolidating goods to maintain quality until they reach international markets. He also highlighted that export initiatives respond to the needs of Rwandans living abroad, ensuring they have access to local products.
Rwanda’s exports continue to grow across Africa and beyond. Between December 22–26, 2025, the country earned $15,647,992 from exports to countries including the United Kingdom, Netherlands, UAE, Germany, and France, while vegetables alone totaled 241 tons, with the UAE, UK, and Spain as top destinations.
Agricultural exports remain a major source of income, with $893.1 million earned in 2025. Between January 12–16, 2026, exports generated more than $15.2 million (22.2 billion Rwf), and from January 19–23, 2026, they earned $13,947,661 (over 20 billion Rwf).
NAEB and the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock aim to surpass $1 billion in agricultural export revenue for the 2025/26 fiscal year, as part of ongoing efforts to expand Rwanda’s presence in regional and international markets.

On January 21, 2026, 17 tons of Rwandan fruits and vegetables were shipped directly to Congo-Brazzaville, demonstrating improved coordination between government institutions and embassies to reduce transit delays, prevent losses, and increase foreign exchange earnings.

title_en: Rwanda and Jamaica Sign MoU to Strengthen Capital Markets
excerpt_en: Kingston, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) and the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance investment opportunities and build capacity in both markets. The agreement was signed during the 21st Investment and Capita
body_en:
Kingston, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) and the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance investment opportunities and build capacity in both markets. The agreement was signed during the 21st Investment and Capital Markets Conference held in Kingston, Jamaica.
Rwanda was represented by RSE CEO Rwabukumba Pierre Célestin, while Jamaica was represented by Prime Minister Andrew Holness and JSE Chairman Livingstone Morrison.
The MoU focuses on developing capital markets, building innovation, and increasing visibility for companies in both countries to attract investment opportunities.
Rwabukumba emphasized that the agreement goes beyond formalities: “This partnership is more than just a document. It will be an opportunity to share experiences, grow together, and open new business and investment opportunities for professionals in the capital markets of both countries.”
Rwanda and Jamaica have previously collaborated in politics, tourism, transport, and industrial park development, and recently sent Rwandan military engineers to assist in infrastructure restoration after a major disaster in Jamaica in October 2025.

title: Rwanda Showcases Agricultural Exports at Dubai’s Gulfood Exhibition
excerpt: Dubai, January 29, 2026 — Rwanda participated in the Gulfood Exhibition, the world’s largest annual trade fair for vegetables, fruits, and flowers, bringing together more than 8,500 exhibitors from 195 countries across 280,000 square meters in Dubai. The country was represented b
title_en: Rwanda Showcases Agricultural Exports at Dubai’s Gulfood Exhibition
excerpt_en: Dubai, January 29, 2026 — Rwanda participated in the Gulfood Exhibition, the world’s largest annual trade fair for vegetables, fruits, and flowers, bringing together more than 8,500 exhibitors from 195 countries across 280,000 square meters in Dubai. The country was represented b
body_en:
Dubai, January 29, 2026 — Rwanda participated in the Gulfood Exhibition, the world’s largest annual trade fair for vegetables, fruits, and flowers, bringing together more than 8,500 exhibitors from 195 countries across 280,000 square meters in Dubai.
The country was represented by the National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) alongside Rwandan farmers engaged in export-oriented production. NAEB described the event as a strategic opportunity to expand Rwanda’s access to markets in the Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries.
While in Dubai, NAEB CEO Claude Bizimana met with Mussab Aboud, CEO of Grandiose, a major UAE food retailer operating 47 stores. The discussions focused on strengthening a long-term partnership to supply Rwandan products such as coffee, flowers, avocados, and fresh produce to the UAE market.
NAEB reported that 90% of Rwanda’s avocado exports currently go to the UAE, with overall fruit exports continuing to rise. Trade between Rwanda and the UAE is expanding steadily, with bilateral trade value projected to reach $1.1 billion.
Export volumes have grown significantly over the past decade. In 2017, Rwanda exported about 40 tons per month of fruits, vegetables, and flowers; today, that figure exceeds 1,000 tons per month. From July 2023 to February 2024, Rwanda exported agricultural products worth $46 million.
The 31st edition of Gulfood was held for the first time across two venues — the Dubai World Trade Centre and the Dubai Exhibition Centre — reflecting the growing scale of the event.

Islamabad, January 29-30, 2026 — The Rwandan Embassy in Pakistan, in collaboration with the National Agriculture Export Board (NAEB), launched Rwanda’s first coffee exhibition in Pakistan, showcasing the country’s high-quality coffee.

title: Rwanda and Pakistan Strengthen Trade Ties via Gwadar Port
excerpt: Islamabad, January 30, 2026 — Rwanda and Pakistan have agreed to expand trade cooperation by using Gwadar Port as a gateway to export goods to African markets through maritime routes, following a bilateral meeting between Pakistan’s Minister for Shipping, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Ch
title_en: Rwanda and Pakistan Strengthen Trade Ties via Gwadar Port
excerpt_en: Islamabad, January 30, 2026 — Rwanda and Pakistan have agreed to expand trade cooperation by using Gwadar Port as a gateway to export goods to African markets through maritime routes, following a bilateral meeting between Pakistan’s Minister for Shipping, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Ch
body_en:
Islamabad, January 30, 2026 — Rwanda and Pakistan have agreed to expand trade cooperation by using Gwadar Port as a gateway to export goods to African markets through maritime routes, following a bilateral meeting between Pakistan’s Minister for Shipping, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, and Rwanda’s Minister of Commerce and Industry, Prudence Sebahizi.
Officials said that Gwadar Port will enable Pakistan to export goods efficiently to East African countries, which collectively represent a market of approximately 500 million people. New maritime routes connecting Karachi to major African ports, including Djibouti and Mombasa, are expected to reduce trade costs by 30% and shorten delivery times.
The Karachi–Djibouti route is set to play a central role in operations, while the Karachi–Mombasa route will further integrate regional trade networks.
Under the agreement, Pakistan plans to use Gwadar Port to export goods to East Africa and import Rwandan products such as tea, coffee, avocados, and other agricultural and livestock products. Rwanda, in turn, imports medical supplies, rice, clothing materials, and agricultural technology from Pakistan.
Rwanda highlighted that expanding water transport routes will help overcome existing logistics bottlenecks by combining port access with regional land transport networks. The initiative is also expected to help Rwanda access South and Central Asian markets.
The agreement aligns with Pakistan’s economic and maritime development strategy, which positions Gwadar Port as a key hub to boost trade between South Asia and East Africa.

title: Morocco Moves to Ratify Air Transport Agreement with Rwanda
excerpt: Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Avia
title_en: Morocco Moves to Ratify Air Transport Agreement with Rwanda
excerpt_en: Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Avia
body_en:
Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) session in Montreal, Canada, with Rwandan Ambassador Higiro Prosper representing Rwanda and Moroccan Transport Minister Abdessamad Kayouh signing on behalf of Morocco.
The cabinet review is part of the administrative process preceding final approval, which will be followed by implementation. Minister Kayouh presented draft law No. 67.25, aimed at securing parliamentary approval for the agreement.
The accord seeks to strengthen cooperation in civil aviation between the two countries. Minister Kayouh emphasized that Morocco aims to double passenger traffic from 40 million to 80 million by 2030.
Ambassador Higiro Prosper described the agreement as a significant milestone, highlighting its potential to expand RwandAir operations and accelerate the development of Kigali International Airport in Bugesera District, which will have a capacity of over 14 million passengers annually.
Currently, RwandAir operates flights to 30 destinations across 22 countries in Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, and the agreement is expected to further enhance the airline’s connectivity and growth prospects.

title: RRA Urges Timely Payment of Property and Rental Income Taxes
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the prev
title_en: RRA Urges Timely Payment of Property and Rental Income Taxes
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the prev
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the previous year.
Deputy Commissioner for Provinces and Local Government Taxes, Karasira Ernest, urged taxpayers to act early to avoid system delays and other obstacles, stating:
“We encourage those concerned to hurry up and declare and pay early. You can declare and pay later, but do not wait until the last day because it creates various obstacles.”
Property Tax (Patent Tax)
Applies to anyone starting a business, already in business, or operating a small or medium enterprise after a two-year exemption.
Taxpayers can pay annually or in installments. Annual payments are due by January 31, 2026. Installments are due:
1st installment: January 31
2nd installment: April 30
3rd installment: July 31
4th installment: October 31
Declarations can be completed via the RRA website or by dialling 800# on a mobile phone.
Rental Income Tax
Applies to individuals and companies owning rental properties in Rwanda.
Income includes rents from fully or partially rented houses, related activities, and interest from rental properties.
Deductions include 50% of maintenance costs and interest on bank loans.
Tax rates:
0% for annual rental income Rwf 1–180,000
20% for Rwf 180,001–1,000,000
30% for above Rwf 1,000,000
Karasira reminded all affected taxpayers to register rental properties with RRA and complete payments early to comply with the law.
Social and Health

title: TI-Rwanda Report Flags Persistent Gender-Based Corruption in Education and Health Sectors
excerpt: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors. The finding
title_en: TI-Rwanda Report Flags Persistent Gender-Based Corruption in Education and Health Sectors
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors. The finding
body_en:
Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors.
The findings were presented at a consultative meeting bringing together TI-Rwanda and key stakeholders to jointly assess the state of corruption in service provision.
Education Sector
The report highlights that one of the major challenges in education is the widespread demand for gender-based bribes, especially in higher education institutions and universities. Some teachers reportedly abuse their authority by soliciting sexual favors from female students in exchange for good grades, academic promotion, or access to internships.
Survey results from 1,350 respondents show that:
8% were asked to bribe to secure a school place,
5% were asked to bribe to obtain good grades,
5% were asked to bribe to win a school food supply contract,
5% were asked to bribe to change their major.
The report further notes that both sexual and financial bribery continue to undermine the education system, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups, including 7.8% of girls, 8.6% from poor families, 9.2% of persons with disabilities, 46.1% with mental disabilities, and 10.2% facing other challenges.
Health Sector
In the health sector, a separate survey of 1,400 residents found persistent risks of corruption in the delivery of health services, including the payment of bribes to receive care more quickly.
Gender-based corruption was particularly reported in maternal and reproductive health services, where some women said they were asked to provide sexual favors in exchange for services they are legally entitled to receive.
Overall, 26% of respondents reported encountering bribery in health facilities. Corruption rates were estimated at 5% in primary health care facilities, 4.4% in district health facilities, and 3.6% in central hospitals.

title: AI to Diagnose Patients and Prescribe Medication – Pilot Program Underway
excerpt: Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration
title_en: AI to Diagnose Patients and Prescribe Medication – Pilot Program Underway
excerpt_en: Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration
body_en:
Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration with the Bill Foundation and OpenAI.
The project, currently tested in about 50 hospitals over the past two years, aims to accelerate medical services and improve care without replacing doctors. Muhire Andrew, Director of Information Technology at the Ministry of Health, emphasized that the technology supports clinical decisions but does not substitute human judgment.
The application listens to patients describe their symptoms, records them, and helps medical staff determine the appropriate treatment, including urgent cases requiring advanced care. It is designed to function offline, addressing challenges in rural areas with limited internet access.
If successful, Horizon 1000 could expand to 1,000 hospitals across Africa by 2028. The technology seeks to address Rwanda’s healthcare workforce shortage, where currently one doctor serves 1,000 patients, compared to the WHO recommendation of four doctors per 1,000 patients.
Challenges remain, including language barriers, as the system currently operates in English, while 75% of Rwandans speak Kinyarwanda. Solutions are being explored to ensure accurate patient understanding and effective AI support.
Following the Cabinet’s 2023 approval of the five-year National Policy to Accelerate AI Technology, an estimated $76.5 million investment is projected to mainstream AI across sectors, boosting economic development and innovation in Rwanda.

title: UN Women Rwanda Launches $6 Million Plan to Empower Women
excerpt: Kigali 5 February 2026 – UN Women Rwanda has unveiled a new strategic plan for 2026-2029, allocating up to $6.3 million (over 9.17 billion Frw) to promote women’s empowerment, particularly in rural areas, and address gaps across multiple sectors. Of the planned budget, $3.5 milli
title_en: UN Women Rwanda Launches $6 Million Plan to Empower Women
excerpt_en: Kigali 5 February 2026 – UN Women Rwanda has unveiled a new strategic plan for 2026-2029, allocating up to $6.3 million (over 9.17 billion Frw) to promote women’s empowerment, particularly in rural areas, and address gaps across multiple sectors. Of the planned budget, $3.5 milli
body_en:
Kigali 5 February 2026 – UN Women Rwanda has unveiled a new strategic plan for 2026-2029, allocating up to $6.3 million (over 9.17 billion Frw) to promote women’s empowerment, particularly in rural areas, and address gaps across multiple sectors.
Of the planned budget, $3.5 million (55%) has already been secured. The remaining funds will be mobilized through partnerships with banks and financial institutions, including the National Bank of Rwanda (BNR), Equity Bank, I&M Bank, and government agencies.
The Director of UN Women Rwanda, Jennet Kem, emphasized collaboration with financial and governmental partners to expand opportunities for women, stating:"The fact that the government is here alone means that we have the strength, it will help us to see in its capacity how we can work together to continue to develop women."
The Minister of Gender and Family Development, Uwimana Consolée, highlighted the importance of partnerships for advancing women's programs, noting:"In these times when the world seems to not have enough money, there are ways we can collaborate and work together, and these activities are for Rwandans."
UN Women Rwanda provides training in governance, self-development, and combating violence, among other initiatives. Between 2020-2025, the agency trained over 85,000 people on gender-based violence, assisted 35,000 individuals (26,570 women and 8,876 men), helped 9,000 women access loans, and supported 3,000 women in starting small and medium-sized enterprises.
The UN Country Coordinator in Rwanda, Ozonnia Ojielo, praised Rwanda’s progress in women’s development, emphasizing the importance of sustaining economic growth to ensure women are not left behind. She said:"Rwanda now needs a better way to help it grow its economy… it needs to have a stable economy itself, which will help it go far."
UN Women first arrived in Rwanda in 1996 as UNIFEM and was rebranded in 2010. Its core mission remains the promotion of gender equality, women’s development, and the fight against violence.

title: Plea Bargaining Releases Over 600 Inmates in One Month
excerpt: Muhanga, January 26, 2026 — The Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) announced that 644 prisoners were released in one month through the plea bargaining program, according to CSP Hillary Sengabo, spokesperson for RCS. The announcement was made during the launch of Plea Bargaining We
title_en: Plea Bargaining Releases Over 600 Inmates in One Month
excerpt_en: Muhanga, January 26, 2026 — The Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) announced that 644 prisoners were released in one month through the plea bargaining program, according to CSP Hillary Sengabo, spokesperson for RCS. The announcement was made during the launch of Plea Bargaining We
body_en:
Muhanga, January 26, 2026 — The Rwanda Correctional Service (RCS) announced that 644 prisoners were released in one month through the plea bargaining program, according to CSP Hillary Sengabo, spokesperson for RCS. The announcement was made during the launch of Plea Bargaining Week at Muhanga Prison.
CSP Sengabo highlighted that the program has significantly reduced overcrowding in Rwandan prisons, noting that the overcrowding rate decreased from 143% to 101% since the program’s implementation.
He explained that the program allows the Criminal Investigation Department to connect perpetrators with victims or enable offenders to pay compensation for damages caused. In the first month alone, 337 prisoners remained incarcerated while 664 were released after completing sentences under the plea bargaining framework.
Vice President of the Supreme Court, Hitiyaremye Alphonse, confirmed that the program applies to all crimes, but emphasized that it does not remove the discretion of prosecutors or the courts.
Judiciary reports show that in the 2024/2025 judicial year, cases concluded through mediation increased by 32%, reaching 3,166 cases, up from 2,395 in the previous year. Meanwhile, 11,846 cases were settled through plea bargains, a rise from 9,851 cases in 2023/2024, representing a 20% increase.
The program is seen as a key measure in reducing prison congestion while maintaining legal oversight and promoting justice through reconciliation and compensation.

title: Rwanda Takes UK to International Court Over £50 Million Dispute
excerpt: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation. The Rwandan governmen
title_en: Rwanda Takes UK to International Court Over £50 Million Dispute
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation. The Rwandan governmen
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation.
The Rwandan government says the UK terminated the agreement unilaterally without prior consultation. The case, initially filed on November 24, 2025, invokes Article 22 of the agreement, which outlined provisions for sending undocumented migrants to Kigali and supporting economic development initiatives under the partnership.
The agreement, originally signed in April 2022 and implemented on April 25, 2024, was part of a joint effort to manage illegal migration and provide support for migrants living in precarious conditions. Rwanda emphasized that the agreement also addressed economic inequalities that push migrants into informal economies.
Following the election of UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in July 2024, the UK suspended the agreement, claiming it could not prevent undocumented migrants from entering the country by boat. Rwanda condemned the decision, saying it was made without consultation and contravened the terms of the agreement.
Rwanda also stated that in December 2024, the UK requested that £50 million payments due in April 2025 and April 2026 be delayed, citing plans to terminate the agreement. Negotiations to revise the terms did not occur, leaving Rwanda to insist that the funds must be paid as stipulated.
Rwanda’s complaint highlights multiple alleged breaches, including:
Failure to honor the agreed payment terms,
Non-compliance with Article 18 regarding financial obligations,
Violation of Article 19 concerning support for migrants facing hardship.
The Rwandan government emphasized that the dispute arose after repeated efforts to resolve issues amicably, which the UK refused, leaving Rwanda with no alternative but to seek legal recourse.
Rwanda underlined its ongoing commitment to protecting migrants, providing safe living conditions, and offering opportunities to support their survival and integration, despite the UK’s alleged refusal to fulfill its obligations.

title: Trial of Gen Philémon Yav Irung Accused of Collaborating with Rwanda
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government. The p
title_en: Trial of Gen Philémon Yav Irung Accused of Collaborating with Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government. The p
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government.
The prosecution, represented by Lt Gen Lucien-René Likulia, claimed that Gen Yav received a message from Rwandan officials advising him not to advance military operations, including a meeting with Brig Gen Mwehu Lumbu Evariste at the Serena Hotel in Goma.
The court confronted the prosecution over a lack of evidence, as Lt Gen Likulia could not produce the alleged message, citing inability to access Gen Yav’s phone. Gen Yav’s lawyer, Me Charles Ngwapitshi, dismissed the claims as rumors, highlighting contradictions in witness testimony and questioning the prosecution’s decision to involve Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, a prominent Rwandan military figure, to lend weight to their case.
Key witnesses, including Lt Gen Constant Ndima and Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge, provided conflicting accounts regarding the origin of the message, with some attributing it to Kabarebe’s advisor, and others unable to confirm.
Gen Yav, who was arrested in September 2022 amid ongoing AFC/M23 advances, stated in court on January 21, 2026, that the only message he received accused him and his colleagues of working with the FDLR terrorist group, with the sender still unknown.
The trial, which began on December 19, 2025, continues amid questions over the validity of the prosecution’s evidence and the role of regional political actors in the case.

Gen Yav’s lawyer, Me Charles Ngwapitshi, dismissed the claims as rumors, highlighting contradictions in witness testimony and questioning the prosecution’s decision to involve Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, a prominent Rwandan military figure, to lend weight to their case.
Key witnesses, including Lt Gen Constant Ndima and Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge, provided conflicting accounts regarding the origin of the message, with some attributing it to Kabarebe’s advisor, and others unable to confirm.
Gen Yav, who was arrested in September 2022 amid ongoing AFC/M23 advances, stated in court on January 21, 2026, that the only message he received accused him and his colleagues of working with the FDLR terrorist group, with the sender still unknown.
The trial, which began on December 19, 2025, continues amid questions over the validity of the prosecution’s evidence and the role of regional political actors in the case.

title: RIB Arrests Three, Including Barafinda, Over Alleged Spread of Public Disorder Rumors
excerpt: Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced. The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo
title_en: RIB Arrests Three, Including Barafinda, Over Alleged Spread of Public Disorder Rumors
excerpt_en: Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced. The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo
body_en:
Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced.
The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, Mazimpaka Patrick, and Nkeramihigo Japhet — were arrested on January 29, 2026, and are accused of disseminating misleading information through various YouTube channels.
They are currently being held at RIB stations in Kimironko, Kicukiro, and Kimihurura as investigations continue.
In a statement, RIB warned the public “to avoid using social media in a manner that is contrary to the law,” adding that it “will not tolerate anyone who uses it to commit crimes.”
Background on Barafinda
In February 2020, RIB summoned Barafinda, but he did not appear and was later arrested on February 11, 2020, before being referred to Caraes Ndera Psychiatric Hospital for medical evaluation.
In March 2020, authorities reported that examinations confirmed he was undergoing treatment for a mental illness and was not under criminal monitoring due to his condition. In July 2020, doctors confirmed his illness was chronic and urged the public and media to refrain from exploiting him for interviews.
Barafinda acknowledged in June 2017 that he had spent time at Ndera, a mental health facility, without providing further details.
He gained national attention during the August 2017 presidential elections after submitting a surprise candidacy, but the National Electoral Commission ruled him ineligible. He later sought to run again in the July 2024 elections, but was again disqualified.
Barafinda previously stated that he had “two thousand reasons” to develop Africa if elected and “20 thousand reasons” to improve the world.

title: Appeal Trial of Claude Muhayimana Convicted of Genocide Begins
excerpt: France February 3, 2026 -- The Appeals Chamber of the Court of Cassation in France is set to hear the appeal of Claude Muhayimana, who is contesting his 14-year prison sentence for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. On February 2, 2026, the list of participants in t
title_en: Appeal Trial of Claude Muhayimana Convicted of Genocide Begins
excerpt_en: France February 3, 2026 -- The Appeals Chamber of the Court of Cassation in France is set to hear the appeal of Claude Muhayimana, who is contesting his 14-year prison sentence for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. On February 2, 2026, the list of participants in t
body_en:
France February 3, 2026 -- The Appeals Chamber of the Court of Cassation in France is set to hear the appeal of Claude Muhayimana, who is contesting his 14-year prison sentence for his role in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. On February 2, 2026, the list of participants in the appeal proceedings was updated.
On February 3, 2026, the Inyangamugayo Bench expected to hear the case is to be confirmed, along with a list of at least 50 witnesses and experts, about 20 of whom will testify in Kigali. The defendant is also expected to be questioned, along with the investigator who assessed his background, behavior, and lifestyle.
On November 19, 2025, the President of the Paris Criminal Court met with lawyers to prepare the appeal, reviewing the list of witnesses.
Muhayimana is seeking to be cleared of the charges and declared innocent of crimes for which he was convicted nearly four years ago.
Born in 1961 in the former Kibuye Prefecture, western Rwanda, Muhayimana was a guest house driver during the genocide. He later fled to France, where he obtained citizenship in 2010 and resides in Rouen.
He was arrested on April 9, 2014, following a complaint by the CPCR, an organization pursuing genocide suspects. He was released under house arrest on April 10, 2015, while under investigation. His trial, initially scheduled for September 2020, was postponed due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
At his trial, which began on November 22, 2021, Muhayimana was accused of leading Interahamwe militias involved in killings of Tutsi in Kibuye between April and July 1994.
Prosecutors also alleged his involvement in massacres at the Kibuye Parish Church on April 17, 1994, at Gatwaro Stadium, and at Home St Jean the following day.
Defended by Me Philippe Meilhac and Françoise Marthe, Muhayimana pleaded not guilty, claiming he was a member of the RNC, an opposition group to the Rwandan government.
On December 16, 2021, the court found him guilty of complicity in genocide and crimes against humanity, sentencing him to 14 years in prison, confirming that he had led Interahamwe members.
However, the court did not find that he directly participated in the Kibuye town massacre, accepting his claim that he was transporting the body of a gendarme, Mwafrika, from Bisesero to Ruhengeri at the time.
The IBUKA organization, which represents survivors of the genocide, said the sentence was lenient compared to the crimes committed.

excerpt: Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Ugandan security forces have expelled US lawyer Robert Amsterdam, who represented opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine). Human rights activist Jeffrey Smith was also expelled. Both were accused of acting against Uganda’s intere
title_en: US Lawyer Expelled Over Opposition Ties
excerpt_en: Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Ugandan security forces have expelled US lawyer Robert Amsterdam, who represented opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine). Human rights activist Jeffrey Smith was also expelled. Both were accused of acting against Uganda’s intere
body_en:
Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Ugandan security forces have expelled US lawyer Robert Amsterdam, who represented opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine). Human rights activist Jeffrey Smith was also expelled. Both were accused of acting against Uganda’s interests and supporting groups opposed to President Yoweri Museveni.
Amsterdam’s expulsion followed comments he made on 2 February, accusing Chief of Defence Staff Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba of instilling fear among Ugandans and using his family’s wealth to consolidate power.
The lawyer had previously announced plans to seek Uganda’s suspension from the Commonwealth, citing what he called “intimidation” and “internal colonialism” by the Museveni family.
On 3 February, Jeffrey Smith also called for international sanctions against the Ugandan government, highlighting Gen Muhoozi’s recent attacks on the US Embassy in Kampala.

title: Rwanda Receives 15 FDLR Fighters and Their Families from DRC
excerpt: Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the reh
title_en: Rwanda Receives 15 FDLR Fighters and Their Families from DRC
excerpt_en: Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the reh
body_en:
Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the rehabilitation of former combatants.
The group crossed into Rwanda through Rubavu District on January 27, 2026. The fighters are scheduled to be transferred to the Rwandan Reintegration Commission (RDRC) facility in Mutobo, Musanze District, for reintegration programs.
Earlier in January, Rwanda received 13 FDLR fighters and six family members on January 20, followed by another 14 individuals, including eight fighters from the group’s special forces unit (CRAP), three days later.
MONUSCO reports that since the AFC/M23 coalition took control of Goma in January 2025, the number of FDLR fighters returning to Rwanda has increased, with nearly 300 having returned so far. The fighters are returning in small groups as Rwanda awaits the DRC army to launch operations to dismantle the terrorist group, as outlined in the peace agreement signed in Washington D.C. on June 27, 2025.
As of June 2025, the FDLR had an estimated 7,000–10,000 fighters, with most, including senior leaders, based in Walikale and Masisi Territories in North Kivu Province.
